The 8 Best Portable Power Stations for Outages and Outings

📅 12 Jun 2020 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4311 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • According to recent reports, portable power stations are handy for backup power during outages, off-grid electricity for an RV, or simply charging your laptop and phone while working remotely.
  • Portable power stations come in a broad range of sizes from brands like Jackery and EcoFlow, including smaller models capable of charging a few devices and high-capacity backup units to keep your lighting and critical appliances on during a days-long blackout.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

According to recent reports, portable power stations are handy for backup power during outages, off-grid electricity for an RV, or simply charging your laptop and phone while working remotely. They’re effectively large bundles of rechargeable lithium-ion batteries, which provide a quiet, exhaust-free alternative to noisy gas-powered portable generators.

Portable power stations come in a broad range of sizes from brands like Jackery and EcoFlow, including smaller models capable of charging a few devices and high-capacity backup units to keep your lighting and critical appliances on during a days-long blackout. Plus, most can be recharged using solar panels.

We evaluated eight power stations of varying sizes, focusing on each model’s maximum output, capacity, charging time, and portability. To test max output, we connected enough electronics and appliances to each power station to meet or slightly exceed their listed max output to see how well they could operate at maximum load. We then tested capacity, using an electricity usage monitor to record the total watt-hours each power station produced while running them under a consistent load.

Once they were drained, we charged each power station from 0 to 100 percent using its AC adapter, timing how long it took to get to 80 and 100 percent capacity. Finally, we evaluated each power station’s portability by attempting to carry it or roll it. Other factors that weighed into our decisions included the number and power output of each power station’s inputs and its charging options.

Our test team for this article includes David Dritsas, an editor who covers generators, lawn and garden, and more; Bradley Ford, an editor with more than five years of experience testing and writing about generators, generator maintenance, power tools, and lawn and garden equipment; and Tony Carrick, a frequent Popular Mechanics contributor who covers landscaping, home improvement, gardening, and home security.

Bluetti manages to pack a lot of power into the Elite 200 V2. It has a max output of 2,600 watts with 3,900-watt startup power and a 2,073.6-watt-hour capacity, all while being relatively compact.

Sources indicate that we hooked up a miter saw, blender, and space heater, all three of which it powered simultaneously. It easily handled the spike to 4,000 watts to start up the saw, above its listed 3,900-watt starting power, before maintaining an even flow of around 2,500 watts.

The Elite 200 V2 also impressed with the quality of its battery. We recorded 92 percent of its listed 2,073.6-watt-hour capacity, well over the 85 percent average for most portable power stations. It has a quick recharge time for its capacity, going from 0 to 80 percent in 81 minutes and to full in just 107 minutes. And because it uses a LiFePO4 battery, it discharges and recharges for 6,000 cycles before it drops below 80 percent capacity.

It has been revealed that the Elite 200 V2 gives you plenty of output and input options for its size, too. Four AC outlets allow you to load up multiple appliances. There are four USB ports for charging smaller devices, a car accessory outlet, and a DC output. Along with its power cord, there’s a port for charging from a car accessory port or with up to 1,000 watts of solar panels.

With a great power-to-weight ratio, the latest version of the Bluetti Elite 200 V2 is a great portable power station for powering a camper or providing backup power for the essentials.

A upcoming and improved version of Jackery’s extremely popular Explorer 1000, the Explorer 1000 V2 features a slightly larger storage capacity, up 70 watt-hours, and a much higher 1,500-watt output—a 50 percent jump from 1,000 watts of the original. This allows you to power devices with higher loads, like an electric grill or a large microwave. Jackery managed this while maintaining the Explorer 1000’s compact size and weight, so it’s still easy to carry with you on a camping trip.

Industry observers note that the Explorer 1000 V2 features three standard 120-volt AC outlets, two USB-C ports (30- and 100-watt), one USB-A port (18-watt), and one 12-volt DC outlet. Paired with Jackery’s app, you can monitor the power station locally via Bluetooth or from anywhere when it’s connected via WiFi. The app allows for checking charge levels and estimated run time, as well as toggling any of the outputs on or off. Plugged into the wall, the power station charges in under two hours. It’s also possible to charge it from your vehicle in up to 12 hours.

Performance-wise, the 1000 V2 did well powering a 25-cubic-foot refrigerator for 18 hours and 22 minutes, which is better performance than we’ve gotten from other tested 1000-watt models. Under a constant load of 475 watts (that’s a little less than a small coffee maker), it ran for 1 hour and 57 minutes.

This power station offers a lot of bang for the buck. Sure, it isn’t going to power your house through a days-long outage, but it offers a lot of nice features for the price, making it one of the better values out there, especially if you pick it up on sale.

Industry observers note that what is most impressive about the Anker S2000 power station is its ability to maximize its runtime. During our testing, we were able to run a full-sized refrigerator for just over 24 hours, which is nearly six hours longer than other power stations we’ve tested with comparable capacity.

It does this using a technology that recognizes the type of device plugged in and adjusts the inverter's frequency to match the type of demand. This, in theory, helps reduce the amount of wasted power. From what we can tell, it works very well.

In a recent development, the S2000 is fairly well equipped, too, with five outlets for AC power (two are in the back) and a bank of USB ports for home use, and can operate as an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) for 10-millisecond automated backup. With only 1,500 watts of output, it may struggle with some high-power appliances like a large microwave, but for many people, this station can deliver power during a blackout and keep you up and running for a long time.

In a recent development, with the Bluetti Apex 300, the name of the game is flexibility. Alone, it delivers up to 3,840 watts of continuous power and handles up to an impressive 7,680 watts of surge power. Capacity is a solid 2,764.8 watt-hours for decent runtime, though it depends on the amount of power you intend to draw from it. If you happen to have 240-volt appliances or circuits, this model has you covered, too.

But everything on this power station is scalable. It’s possible to add up to six additional batteries for a very high capacity of 19,353.6 watt-hours, and connect up to two other Apex 300 units and run them in parallel. This expandability makes it a great entry-level home power station that expands into a larger backup system that delivers whole-home power.

The Apex 300 features four 120-volt outlets across the front, plus a 120-volt 30-amp outlet and a 120/240-volt 50-amp outlet on the side for powering devices individually, plugging into an RV, or delivering home power through a transfer switch.

One downside for me was the lack of direct DC outputs, e.g., USB-C ports. For that, you have to purchase an optional hub. There are also power inputs for a standard AC plug, a 30-amp connection, and two solar connections. The Apex 300 uses two inverters as opposed to one, giving you two banks of 120-volt, 1,920-watt output (two outlets in each bank). We easily ran two high-powered appliances at the same time, including a space heater and a toaster, with no issues at all.

This station is serious about solar recharging, too. There are two ports for connecting solar panels up to 1,200 watts each. Having the option of 2,400 watts of solar input is uncommon in a station of this size and price point. Plus, you can reach even higher input by pairing with a Bluetti SolarX 4K voltage regulator, which is designed for connection to larger solar arrays.

Recent findings suggest that most of the control options are accessed with the Bluetti Mobile app, and it’s one of the best we’ve seen. It’s easy to finely tune settings in ways that other companies don’t offer, such as adjusting the recharging level from as little as one amp to 50 amps.

According to recent reports, if you’ve been eyeing power stations but aren’t sure if you want one more for portable power or more for home backup power, this is the model for you. It delivers a great amount of power for portable use, but lays the groundwork for building a more dedicated system in the future.

This is one of the most rugged power stations we’ve seen yet. The Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra features an IP65 weatherproof rating, molded rubber port covers, a shockproof enclosure, and a bottom drainage system and cooling structure that help keep water out of the enclosure. All work together to resist the elements better than most power stations can.

According to recent reports, the unique cooling system was particularly interesting. A titanium alloy plate within the structure helps dissipate heat without the need for multiple fans, and eliminates the need for any side vents (typical in most power stations) that could allow droplets of water in. Meanwhile, you can remove an external plate on the bottom and dry it if water does make its way in.

It has been revealed that the 1,800 watts of output power and 1,536 watt-hours of battery capacity are decent if you’re taking this camping for the weekend and need to recharge devices, run a low-powered small appliance or two, and plug in some lighting. But don’t expect to run something like a space heater for very long, though.

Full Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra Power Station Review.

The S5000 is the second power station in Anker's S-series, which features inverter efficiency technology that helps to reduce wasted energy when the inverter is idling or running lower-powered devices. We were impressed with how this technology performed in the S2000, and this model matched that performance.

Recent findings suggest that we ran this through several tests, and the battery efficiency proved to be around 97 percent (the industry average is around 89 percent). For example, we left the AC inverter idling for 18 hours, and the battery remained at 100 percent capacity. Meanwhile, another station we idled at the same time lost 19 percent of its available power. That was impressive.

The next most impressive attribute about the S5000 is its size. It’s at least half the size of other power stations that feature 5,000 watt-hours of capacity and includes just as many outputs, including a 240-volt, 30-amp outlet. It also has both high- and low-powered DC inputs that enable up to 3,000 watts of solar power input if you have the panels to generate that. You can also recharge at up to 4,500 watts using a direct DC connection to Anker's 5500 Smart Tri-Fuel generator.

With only 4,500 watts of total output, we wouldn’t call this a contender for true whole-home backup (Anker’s E-10 system is a better option for that), but the S5000 can deliver a decent amount to power an RV, run lights and appliances during an emergency, or even a couple of critical circuits.

Recent findings suggest that during our hands-on test, Goal Zero’s newest Yeti 1500 impressed us with its capable performance and sturdy construction. It’s the replacement for an older model and improves on its predecessor with improved weatherproofing, more outputs, and a better battery.

This 2,000-watt power station is clearly designed for outdoor use with an IPX4 water-resistance rating and upcoming outlet shields that cover the ports and inputs when you’re not using them. That’s great for dusty conditions. Each section is nicely illuminated by an LED light and can be individually turned on/off using a manual button or the mobile app (and will shut off if not used after a duration of time). These additions make it perfect for camping or other outdoor uses. You can’t leave it out in the rain, but getting a bit of water on it won’t be a concern.

Sources indicate that we loved the increased number of outputs on the Yeti 1500. There are now four 120-volt AC outlets and six USB ports: four USB-C (two are high-powered) and two USB-A ports, plus four 12-volt connections (though two of those are proprietary for Goal Zero accessories and not all that useful in our estimation). There are also inputs for AC power, 12-volt DC, and inputs for both low- and high-voltage solar power that can be used simultaneously. Theoretically, you could recharge this station with up to 900 watts of eco-friendly electrical current.

As part of our test, we simulated a blackout at home and managed to run a cable modem/Wi-Fi router, a lamp, a TV, and a tower fan, while simultaneously charging a phone and a laptop through the USB-C ports. Given the station’s output and capacity, there was enough power for over two days of use (conveniently shown on the main display), and there was plenty of room to spare for a few more devices.

The mobile app was easy to use and chock-full of great information on energy consumption. The only problem we had was maintaining a stable Bluetooth connection. It needed to be manually paired every time we went to use it, which was annoying. Wi-Fi is available, but that’s not so useful when you are off-grid.

It has been revealed that we should warn you that the Yeti 1500 is heavy at 53 pounds. If you’re taking it on a trip, you’ll need a bit of strength to lug it around. That aside, the 2026 Yeti 1500 is a well-designed power station that’s ideal for off-grid camping, especially when there are dusty or wet conditions. We’d happily take it on our next camping trip.

Full Goal Zero Yeti 1500 Review.

Sources indicate that though it’s no longer EcoFlow’s flagship backup power solution, the original Delta Pro is still a massive power station with a good amount of electrical output. The brand claims it powers nearly any appliance, and after testing, we’re inclined to agree. With an output of 3,600 watts, it can handle multiple appliances, and it’s possible to bump the output to 4,500 watts with its built-in X-Boost technology if you need more power.

It has been revealed that in testing, we ran it with a continuous 470-watt load for 6 hours and 57 minutes, as indicated on the Delta Pro’s display. Of course, in a home backup during a power outage situation, we would run only the bare essentials to conserve power. To that end, we used it to power a full-size, 25-cubic-foot refrigerator, which it did for a remarkable 51 hours and 24 minutes.

It has been revealed that recharging the power station from empty using a standard 120-volt home outlet, it recharged to full capacity in 2 hours and 36 minutes. There’s also an included adapter for charging the system at EV charging stations, with solar panels (sold separately), with a car charger, or combinations of these to speed things up.

The Delta Pro’s display screen provides all the notable information you need to manage your power consumption. We frequently checked the screen during testing to see the unit’s charge level, current load, and estimated run time at the current discharge rate.

All of this information is accessible through EcoFlow’s app, which was the most intuitive and easiest to use of those tested. We connected the app both locally using Bluetooth and remotely via Wi-Fi to monitor the power station from anywhere. We could also toggle outlets on and off remotely, which is helpful if you’re trying to manage power station output to extend the battery life.

We’ve tested the brand’s Whole-Home Backup Kit, which includes two of the power stations and a dual-voltage hub used to connect to your home service panel, via a transfer switch. We used this setup to power critical circuits in a Northeast Pennsylvania home in late winter.

The Delta Pro Whole Home Kit ran just over 24 hours, powering kitchen outlets, a full-size refrigerator, a chest freezer, a cable modem and wireless network, and a hot water boiler. Plus, having charged these two Delta Pro power stations previously, we found that they were able to hold a full charge over a full 8 months.

Testing was performed under normal usage conditions—run time could easily be extended by employing standard power-conservation strategies like lowering the thermostat, powering the fridge and freezer for four hours on and four hours off, and only opening them when absolutely necessary.

EcoFlow’s Delta Pro Whole Home Kit is a legitimate home backup system that can operate inside your home, with none of the risks or potential hassles of running a generator, such as dangerous carbon monoxide gas from exhaust fumes and dealing with fuel and oil.

A portable power station’s maximum output tells you the total watts it can produce, which determines what you can and can’t power with it. Look for a power station that can handle the combined wattage of the electronics you plan to plug into it.

Some power stations also have surge power that allows them to produce higher wattage for short bursts. This is designed specifically for appliances that draw more watts (known as starting watts) in the first few seconds that you first start them up, including power tools, refrigerators, blenders, and window air conditioners.

It has been revealed that A portable power station’s capacity, listed in watt-hours (Wh), determines how much energy a power station can deliver over time. Generally, power stations with more watt-hours can run for longer, but exactly how long depends on the amount of watts the devices connected to the power station draw. You can roughly estimate how long a power station will last by dividing the total watt-hours by the watts drawn (Wh ÷ W = Hrs).

For example, if you have a power station with 2,048 watt-hour capacity, and are consistently drawing 400 watts of power: 2,048 ÷ 400 = 5.12 hours of runtime.

Keep in mind that the usable watt hours are not the same as the watt hours listed on the power station’s label. You’ll typically get about 85 percent of the listed watt-hours due to power lost in connections and the electricity that the power station itself uses to power its inverter and display. Given those losses, expect to get about 85 percent of a power station’s listed watt-hours in usable power. So, a fully charged 2,000-watt-hour power station will typically give you about 1,700 watt-hours of usable power.

These days, most portable power stations, including all those we recommend here, use LiFePO4 batteries, which are capable of holding far more cycles, which is the number of times a battery goes through a complete discharge and recharge, than older lithium-ion batteries, while also being less likely to combust. Their one drawback is that they have a lower energy density, which means it takes more LiFePO4 batteries than lithium-ion batteries to produce the same amount of power. Still, this is the battery type of choice for portable power stations, both large and small.

Sources indicate that while all these power stations are portable, some are easier to transport than others. A power station’s portability is directly related to its power capacity and output.

Small power stations with around 300 watt-hours of capacity and a max output of 300 watts typically weigh under 10 pounds and are about the size of a lunch box.

Mid-size models like the Bluetti Elite 200 V2 portable power station, which have a max wattage of between 2,000 and 2,600 watts and a 2,000-watt-hour capacity, are about the size of the printer in your home office and weigh around 60 pounds, just small and light enough for one person to carry from one room to another.

According to recent reports, large portable models can weigh up to 135 pounds and are about the size of a suitcase. While these monsters are too large for one person to lift, they do sit on wheels that allow you to move them over flat surfaces, technically making them portable.

Portable power stations have an array of output ports, including USB-C, USB-A, car accessory, AC, and RV. Consider what types of appliances or electronics you’re planning to charge and the type of connections they use when choosing a portable power station.

Since the wattage of the output can vary, also consider the maximum charging output of each port to avoid disappointing recharge times. For example, a power station with a USB-C port that has a 15-watt max output will take a much longer time to charge a laptop than one with a 140-watt USB-C port.

If you’re looking for a large capacity power station that will back up critical circuits in your home or power an RV, you’ll need a station that features a single 30-amp connection that can connect to an RV input or transfer switch.

Portable power stations have control panels with LED displays and buttons that turn inputs off and on and display usage and remaining power. Most portable power stations are also compatible with Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, allowing you to monitor and control them remotely from a smartphone app.

In a recent development, often, what makes a power station great is the kind of software it includes and what features it offers to help you best manage your power station. For example, some stations that you leave plugged into a wall—so that they stay charged and at the ready—will automatically only recharge your station during low-peak hours when rates may be lower from your electric utility. Features like this one can be incredibly helpful when trying to get the most from your station.

Most large power stations, including the EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus and Anker F3800 Plus, can serve as a UPS (uninterruptible power supply) for your home. To use these power stations as a UPS, plug them into the wall, then plug whatever devices you want backed up into the station’s AC output ports. When the power is on, those devices use energy from the grid. When there is a power outage, the power station instantly switches these devices to battery power. If you live in an area prone to power outages, this can be useful to prevent data loss from a connected computer, keep medical devices running, or run the pump and filter on a fish tank.

Portable power stations heat up when operating for extended periods or when they’re providing power for multiple devices. Internal fans will kick on to keep the power station from overheating. While these fans are far quieter than the roar of a gas-powered generator, they do still create some noise. Smaller power stations are about as loud as a small fan, while larger ones produce about the same amount of noise as a refrigerator.

A portable power station’s lifespan depends on the type of battery inside. Most newly introduced portable power stations, including all the models we recommend here, feature LiFePO4 battery technology, which lasts far longer than older lithium-ion technology.

How much more? LiFePO4 power stations will last for more than 3,000 charge cycles, or about 10 years. That’s far longer than the 500 or so charge cycles and 3 to 5 years you’ll get from an older power station with a lithium-ion battery.

According to recent reports, that depends on the capacity of your portable power station, the wattage of your solar panels, and the weather. To figure that out, divide the station’s total capacity by the total input power of the solar panels (Wh ÷ W = Hrs).

Sources indicate that for example, a 1,000-watt-hour power station that’s receiving a consistent stream of 200 watts of power from a solar panel would take about 5 hours to recharge. Keep in mind, this is assuming uninterrupted, direct sunlight conditions, which, even then, may produce varied results.

Some power stations have ingress protection (IP) ratings, indicating they have been tested for water and dust resistance. The Bluetti Elite 200, for example, has an IP65 rating, which means it can withstand water sprays from all angles. However, other portable power stations do not have a weather rating, so it’s vital to check if you plan on using your power station outdoors. Regardless, it’s a good idea to protect your power station from any water or severe weather conditions as much as possible.

Recent findings suggest that last night, the 2026 Governors Awards served as the kickoff to award season, with some of the biggest names in Hollywood gathering at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles for the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences’s annual film gala. There, the stars gave us a taste of what to expect fashion-wise when ceremonies like the Oscars roll around in the coming months. Zendaya stunned in an archival Giles Deacon dress with a waterfall of golden fringe. Florence Pugh shimmered in bedazzled Valentino. Timothée Chalamet brought back his Call Me By Your Name-era curls.

One of the most show-stopping looks of the night though came courtesy of former Oscar winner Charlize Theron, who brought some heat to the high-profile ceremony in a straight-off-the-runway ensemble from the Tom Ford Spring/Summer 2027 ready-to-wear collection.

Recent findings suggest that the crimson fit consisted of a flowy maxi dress with a draping bodice that was constructed out of wide, slightly off-the-shoulder swathes. These diverging pieces created a plunging neckline so deep it nearly left Theron’s entire torso bare. Underneath, the actor wore a matching red leather bra, embracing the ongoing exposed-underwear trend.

A slight slit running up the side of the skirt revealed Theron’s pair of strappy black sandal heels that tied up her ankles, and she accessorized with crystal drop earrings from Anita Ko that dangled alongside her neck like daggers. To complete the look, she matched her dress with a bright red lip, while pulling her hair back into a slicked bun.

Now we can’t wait for awards season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that delish editors handpick every product we feature. We may earn commission from the links on this page.

No one wants to waste perfectly good food—I’m more likely to eat something slightly past its expiration date than throw it out prematurely—but some pantry items are just taking up space.

According to recent reports, dusty canned foods, old spices, expired baking ingredients, and more past-their-prime goods serve little to no culinary value. Getting rid of them will actually help you identify the pantry items that you can still use before they go bad. But how can you keep your pantry organized more regularly, and what exactly should you throw away?

According to recent reports, go through every item in your pantry at least twice a year, recommends Nicole Gabai, professional organizer, founder of B. Organized, and author of The Art of Organizing: An Artful Guide to an Organized Life.

According to recent reports, if a twice-yearly check-in feels too daunting, consider a weekly five-minute check-in to discard expired goods, notes Shaniece Jones, professional organizer and founder of Closet Therapy. “Organize by accessibility and intention,” she says. “Keep your daily go-tos at eye level, heavy items like large cans of oil and bottled water on lower shelves, and seasonal or rarely used items up high.” Labels, Lazy Susans, and drawer dividers are some of her go-to tools for organizing the pantry.

As you start cleaning, check off the following items—these are some of the most common pantry items our organizing experts find past their prime.

According to recent reports, while many shelf-stable foods, such as canned goods, are still safe to eat past their expiration date, you should still check for signs of spoilage. “You can tell canned goods have spoiled if they are rusted, or if you see the cans bulge or dent,” Gabai claims.

Industry observers note that labeling pantry items helps you check how long they’ve been open. For opened packages and bulk goods you’ve decanted into containers, write the date on the label so you know when you opened them.

Industry observers note that spices that have lost their smell? Time to go. “If it smells flat or just not aromatic, then it needs to be replaced since it will add very little, if any, flavor to what you’re cooking,” Gabai says. She also notes that ground spices typically last one to two years, while dried herbs can last up to three years.

“Baking ingredients like flour, baking powder, and baking soda can lose their effectiveness over time,” says Meaghan Kessman, founder of Meaghan Kessman Home Organization.

Eventually, flour will go bad, but how long it takes to get rancid depends on how it’s stored and the type of flour. In general, Gabai notes it will last at room temperature for six to eight months. She recommends storing it in an airtight container in the fridge or freezer.

Sources indicate that “Check for expiration dates and any signs of spoilage, such as clumping or an off smell,” Kessman notes. “If you’re unsure, test baking powder by adding a teaspoon to hot water—if it bubbles, it’s still good to use.”.

Industry observers note that we often buy cooking oils in bulk, but keep in mind that they eventually go bad. “Oils and fats, such as olive oil, vegetable oil, and shortening, can become rancid if stored for too long. Rancid oils have a sour or off smell,” Kessman states. “Always check the expiration date and store oils in a cool, dark place to keep them fresh longer.”.

Gabai recommends storing oils in a cool, dark place and disposing of them properly; freeze in a zip-top bag, then toss in the trash (never pour down the drain).

Recent findings suggest that these pantry staples are oil-rich, so they spoil faster than you might think. “They can last about 6 months at room temperature, but if you freeze them, they can last a year or more,” Gabai notes.

“Snacks and cereals can go stale quickly once opened,” Kessman says. She recommends checking expiration dates and signs of staleness, like an unusual smell or texture.

According to Gabai, grains, rice, and beans can last about one to two years, but brown rice and other whole grains will not last as long because of their higher oil content.

“Condiments like ketchup, mustard, and salad dressings often get pushed to the back of the pantry and forgotten,” Kessman claims. “Check for expiration dates and any signs of separation, discoloration, or off smells.”.

Honey is the rare exception that probably isn't spoiled. The National Honey Board states that honey has a shelf life of approximately two years, although it can last much longer if stored correctly in a sealed container.

“Honey was found in the tombs of kings and royalty as far back as 3,000 years in Egypt—and it was still edible!” Gabai notes.

If you notice crystallization, Gabai recommends gently heating the honey container in a pot of water.

The novelty of a wood burning fireplace wears off when you have to trudge outside to grab a bundle of logs. Installing a wood burning stove can be expensive, and once it’s running, it produces ash that needs to be cleaned out. Pellet stoves, however, are an efficient, convenient option for heating a room while appreciating the glow of a live fire.

According to recent reports, powered by compressed hardwood pellets stored in a hopper that can hold over 100 pounds, pellet stoves can provide a fire that burns for dozens of hours without needing to be tended. Those pellets drop into a combustion chamber where they are burned to produce heat. Exhaust is then vented through a flue pipe out a sidewall or your roof.

It has been revealed that A pellet stove offers consistent, reliable heat without a lot of fuss. More expensive models will cost several thousand dollars, but often come with programmable digital thermostats and larger hoppers that allow a fire to burn longer without the need for additional pellets being added.

Wood stoves require a bit more effort and knowledge—you’ll have to learn about the different burn rates of wood and clean out ash more regularly. Still, wood burning stoves are typically quieter and may last longer than pellet stoves because they don’t have electronic components.

As for installation, freestanding pellet stoves need an available outlet with an open plug and a vent to the outside, which may require the installer to cut a hole in the wall. If your power goes out often during storms, that means your pellet stove won’t work without a generator or separate power source. Pellet stoves that insert into your fireplace require a chimney liner, a pipe that vents gas outside.

In a recent development, pellet stoves are designed to warm up everything from your patio to your rec room. Different models can stand on their own, be mounted to the wall, or inserted into a fireplace. Here are the 10 best pellet stoves to buy now that bring the heat.

For a sizable pellet stove that can heat a large area, this model from ComfortBilt is a top choice. The EPA-certified design can provide heat for up to 2,800 square feet thanks to its 50,000 BTU output.

It offers a large window where you can watch the fire burning inside. With a 55-pound hopper, the ash from the fire falls down into a removable pan that only needs to be emptied every 2 weeks. The stove offers five power settings, and on the lowest setting, you can get up to 20 hours of continuous heat.

Industry observers note that the PelPro Pellet Stove is an efficient option that gives you plenty of heat for your buck. The EPA-certified stove has a large hopper (the manufacturer says the stove can run for 40 hours before needing to be reloaded) and convenient features like an automatic ignition at a lower price point.

The main compromises are a manually controlled dial thermostat and only a 1-year warranty on parts.

If you like the ability to control your appliances remotely, this pellet stove has built-in Wi-Fi that allows you to adjust its settings, create a heating schedule, and more, all from your smartphone.

In a recent development, the stove has a three-sided bay window that makes it a great focal point for your living space, and it can heat up to 2,500 square feet. It has a large hopper that can hold up to 66 pounds of pellets, providing a long run time between refills, and the unit’s quiet blower won’t disturb your family while it’s running.

Recent findings suggest that one of the downsides of pellet stoves is they require electricity to operate their augers and inner fans, and this means you’re left without heat when the power goes out. However, this pellet stove from US Stove Company is one of the few designed to work without electricity. Instead, it uses a gravity-fed hopper and manual start.

Sources indicate that with a tall, narrow form and a pellet feed that zigzags down to the burning chamber, this stove can heat up to 2,000 square feet. You can adjust its temperature by opening and closing the fresh air intakes on the front of the stove, and the 60-pound hopper holds enough fuel to run for up to 30 hours.

If you’re hoping to heat a large area or even your whole house, this pellet stove can warm up to 3,000 square feet when temperatures are mild.

The EPA-certified stove has a unique heat exchanger design and powerful blower that help to produce maximum heat from pellets, and there are five power settings and a programmable thermostat that let you adjust the warmth to your liking.

On the lowest setting, the 51-pound hopper has enough fuel to run for up to 19 hours, and the stove is reasonably priced considering its high heat output.

The Ashley Pellet Space Saver Stove is like a genie in a bottle—lots of power in an itty bitty living space. With a small profile thanks to thoughtful curves and an efficient design, this steel stove can heat up to 2,200 square feet for 32 hours.

Adjust the temperature and heat output via remote control and the side panels pop off for maintenance. A large glass window lets you enjoy a lovely view of the fire.

If you don’t have space for a freestanding pellet stove, this unique model can be mounted to your wall instead. It’s ideal for spaces up to 1,000 square feet and has a direct vent design that doesn’t require the traditional chimney installation.

It has been revealed that the unit comes with everything needed for installation, including the mounting bracket, and its 28-pound hopper delivers up to 35 hours of heat between refills on the lowest setting. It has digital controls and a remote control for easy adjustments, and it’s even approved for use in mobile homes.

According to recent reports, I’ve worked with pellet grills and wood stoves to get through Midwest winters, so I know the differences and potential benefits of different stoves. To discover popular pellet stoves, I dived into articles on Field & Stream, The Spruce, and Wirecutter. I considered which models did well in tests and cross referenced them with reviews on Amazon. Also, I delved into message boards and talked with pellet stove owners to understand what was frustrating and what was delightful about owning one.

I also weighed the cost and size of each model, as well as the warranty. Finally, I relied on some of the previous research done for this article by writer Camryn Rabideau. Here are the 10 pellet stoves that will warm your heart and your living room.

A pellet stove can be a major investment—multiple thousands of dollars to cover the stove and installation—so it’s vital that you find one that fits your room and heats it efficiently.

In a recent development, pellet stoves come in three main styles: freestanding, wall mounted, and insert. A freestanding stove—which can be larger or more powerful than the other options—evokes a classic cabin feel and sits on the ground or on feet. A wall-mounted stove hangs free of the floor and kicks out heat like the heads of a mini split. Inserts are meant to slot inside your fireplace and could take a non-functioning fireplace and make it a focal point of your room once again.

More Cozy Options to Consider: Best Electric Fireplaces • Best Space Heaters • Best Heated Blankets.

It has been revealed that pellet stoves are efficient, producing less creosote (the tarry byproduct of burning wood) and ash than wood stoves. The compact pellets—thanks to their small size and low moisture content—burn hot and promptly. Pellet stoves that receive certification from the United States Environmental Protection Agency typically offer between 70 and 83 percent fuel efficiency. In some cases, certification comes with a tax credit so check before you purchase a given model.

Pellet stoves often have multiple settings. Higher settings release more pellets so the stove can burn hotter, whereas the lowest setting will enable you pellets to last longer, but you might not get as much heat. A stove with a smaller hopper running outdoors may only last 6 hours per full hopper, like the Even Embers Pellet Stove, which is fine if you’re looking to gather in the backyard at night. Larger pellet stoves can burn unattended for more than a day, like the PelPro Pellet Stove which can run for 40 hours.

In a recent development, the larger the hopper, the longer the burn time, and the longer you can go between pellet refills. Most hoppers will need to be refilled once a day. But larger hoppers (60 pounds and up) typically mean bigger stoves, so you’ll have to consider whether or not it will fit your space. Likewise, it can be cumbersome to pour heavier bags—50 pounds at a time—into the hopper.

The heating ability of pellet stoves is measured in British Thermal Units (BTUs) per hour. The higher the BTUs, the easier it will be for a stove to heat a room or multiple rooms. If you’re considering heating multiple rooms or a whole home, a pellet stove rated at 60,000 BTUs can heat approximately 2,000 square feet.

Warranties typically cover parts and repairs for several years. A well-maintained pellet stove should last longer than the warranty—a decade or more if properly maintained; but it’s a comfort to have some financial coverage in the first few years after investing a decent amount of money in a pellet stove.

Industry observers note that empty your ash pan and clean the firebox once or twice a week. If your pellet stove has baffles, clean them every few months. And you’ll need to do a deep clean of the venting probably once a year.

Check your manual for the specific instructions, but cleaning can follow a simple rule—if you see ash build up, clean it out once your stove has cooled.

Pellet stoves heat up quickly—it’s one of their best features. They’ll be raising the temperature of your room often inside of 30 minutes.

Pellets may be more expensive; but they’re convenient. Pellets take up less space and produce less ash than firewood. Wood stoves can be used for cooking (even if it’s just s’mores) and require tending that you’ll either see as a nice part of the ritual or a chore that you’d rather not do.

The 2026 seating is currently sold out, but Resy offers the option to receive an alert should a table become available.

A reservation at 4 Charles Prime Rib is difficult any time of year, but this West Village townhouse restaurant becomes particularly appealing this time of year. Known for its intimate, clubby atmosphere and indulgent steakhouse fare, 4 Charles releases its reservations 21 days in advance, and they always seem to disappear within seconds. If all else fails, it’s offering At Home Packages for Thanksgiving, so you can enjoy its all-American cuisine without having to jockey for a table.

According to recent reports, L’Artusi has been a West Village fixture for two decades, and its popularity demonstrates little sign of waning. During the winter months, the restaurant leans into the season with festive décor, winter truffle dishes, and rotating chef’s specials that celebrate the season. Its relatively small dining room means tables are always in demand. There is good news for devotees, however: A second, larger location is slated to open in Rockefeller Center this spring.

In a recent development, few New York restaurants commit to the holiday bit like Rolf’s—a Gramercy institution that is known for its ceilings festooned with thousands of Christmas ornaments, twinkling lights, and garlands. The décor stays up all year round, but the holiday period is especially competitive to score reservations. You have to call to book. Good luck.

For those spending Christmas Eve in Manhattan, Chez Fifi offers a distinctly French alternative to your typical holiday dinner. The Upper East Side restaurant—known as one of the neighborhood’s hottest tables to book right now—offers French-Basque specialties, from steak au poivre to roasted chicken and baba au rhum, alongside foie gras terrine and seasonal specials. Pro tip for those having trouble scoring a reservation: the restaurant holds some upstairs seating for release the day before.

Recent findings suggest that west Village hot spot Galo is a new addition to the restaurant scene but has become a quick favorite for in-the-know diners. Housed in a historic carriage house on West 10th Street, it’s about as cozy as you can get—and is one of the few popular restaurants of its ilk to be open on Christmas Day. An ode to the chef’s native Portugal, the menu spans large-format heritage dishes and shareable petiscos, like bacalhau, wine-poached pears, and a variety of special port wines.

Housed in a historic Rockefeller Center townhouse once frequented by Johnny Carson and generations of Saturday Night Live cast members, Pebble Bar oozes authentic New York history. Its intimate dining room is particularly appealing during the holidays, thanks to its proximity to the Rockefeller Center tree, Radio City Music Hall, and Fifth Avenue’s windows. With just nine dining tables, availability is limited—but the restaurant does reserve some space for walk-ins, so a spontaneous drop-in might work out in your favor.

Few dining rooms offer a better vantage point for the holiday season than L’Avenue at Saks, perched on the ninth floor of the iconic Fifth Avenue department store. Its seasonal Le Chalet experience adds live piano, festive cocktails—including a must-try French Onion Martini—and views of the Rockefeller Center tree to the equation. Reservations go promptly in the month of December, when the restaurant can serve 600 to 800 guests a day. Reservations are available through Resy.

Tech Report: A Deep Dive Into Hailey Bieber’s Many, Many Face Masks

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1350 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that “Dealing with my problems one mask a time,” wrote Hailey Bieber beneath a recent Instagram carousel.
  • Industry observers note that there she is, covered in mustard-yellow paste, slathered in a thick white cream, encased in a glossy lavender-grey treatment, and illuminated by the electric-blue glow of an LED device.
  • According to recent reports, of course, we’ve long known Bieber as the reigning queen of glazed-donut skin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that “Dealing with my problems one mask a time,” wrote Hailey Bieber beneath a recent Instagram carousel. While she’s not elaborating on mentioned issues, her extensive collection of face masks have been exposed for every skincare obsessive’s over-analysis. Hailey Bieber has a face mask for every occasion and skin concern, it seems.

Industry observers note that there she is, covered in mustard-yellow paste, slathered in a thick white cream, encased in a glossy lavender-grey treatment, and illuminated by the electric-blue glow of an LED device. There are hydrogel sheets, eye patches, and a rather arresting cobalt-blue mask from a recent trip to Seoul. Bieber is clearly not afraid to cast the net wide in pursuit of good skin.

According to recent reports, of course, we’ve long known Bieber as the reigning queen of glazed-donut skin. But beyond the perfectly dewy complexion and the seemingly endless supply of Rhode products, she’s a genuine skincare fanatic. And, someone who has been particularly candid about the challenges of maintaining her skin. Bieber has previously described her skin as dry, sensitive, and easily irritated, particularly by fragrances, harsh formulas, and certain sunscreens. She’s also spoken about her ongoing struggles with perioral dermatitis, an inflammatory condition that can cause uncomfortable redness, bumps, and flaking around the mouth and nose. Frequent travel, stress, hormonal fluctuations, and unfamiliar products can all contribute to her flare-ups.

As she’s previously explained, her approach when her skin is irritated is minimal: rinsing with water, using prescribed azelaic acid and clindamycin, hypochlorous acid, and Rhode’s ceramide-rich Glazing Milk. In her 2025 Beauty Secrets video, she also revealed that she generally skips a full morning cleanse in favor of a water rinse, saving the heavier-duty moisturizing for nighttime.

It has been revealed that all of which explains a lot about her mask collection. Hydration, calming, barrier support, and a little depuffing appear to be the common threads. Although, importantly, a mask that hydrates dry skin won’t necessarily treat perioral dermatitis—and some formulas can aggravate it. So, what exactly is she using?

Recent findings suggest that the first one I can immediately pinpoint is the bright-blue mask Bieber wore during her recent visit to South Korea: PYDERIN’s Hydrovuster PDRN SOS Hyal Soothing Mask. Sold largely through Korean pharmacies and dermatology clinics, it belongs to a latest wave of PDRN-focused skincare products. PDRN, or polydeoxyribonucleotide, is derived from DNA fragments, commonly sourced from salmon, and has become a particularly buzzy ingredient in Korean regenerative skincare. The mask uses 10 forms of hyaluronic acid to attract and retain moisture, alongside ingredients such as panthenol, azulene, and barrier-supporting compounds. The distinctive blue tint comes from an azulene derivative, associated with soothing properties. The idea is to leave dehydrated, stressed skin feeling calmer, plumper, and more comfortable. It’s worth distinguishing topical PDRN from the injectable treatments offered in clinics, though: a sheet mask cannot promise the same regenerative results.

Then there’s Rhode’s Caffeine Reset Sculpting Cream Mask, which Bieber developed over approximately 18 months and more than 50 iterations. The rich, white rinse-off formula is designed as a morning pick-me-up for tired, puffy skin. “A cup of coffee for your face,” is what the Rhode copy says. Caffeine helps temporarily reduce the appearance of puffiness, while peptides, poppy extract, and phytosterols target radiance, surface hydration, and a firmer-looking complexion. Vanillyl butyl ether provides an invigorating sensation.

The brand’s other masking essential that I can spy in the IG carousel is the Peptide Eye Prep: cooling hydrogel under-eye patches. Formulated with caffeine, peptides, glycerin, and sodium PCA, they’re intended to hydrate the delicate under-eye area, temporarily minimize puffiness, and soften the appearance of fine lines. They are also super practical: Bieber has previously told Vogue Business that she wears hers to the gym or when heading out for coffee.

Hailey Bieber’s mask habit predates Rhode by several years. Among her earlier favorites are two treatments from Dr. Barbara Sturm. The original Face Mask combines aloe vera, chamomile, purslane, and kaolin clay for a combination of moisture, softness, and soothing care. Its Clarifying Mask, meanwhile, is more targeted towards blemish-prone skin, using zinc and kaolin to absorb excess sebum, alongside botanical ingredients intended to support the skin barrier. The latter is more of an occasional clarifying treatment than an everyday solution for reactive skin.

Recent findings suggest that she’s also previously expressed her love for Drunk Elephant’s F-Balm Electrolyte Waterfacial, an overnight hydration treatment packed with humectants, squalane, niacinamide, and barrier-supporting lipids. It basically extends your nighttime moisturizing routine, as it helps the skin hold on to water while you sleep.

It has been revealed that her more recent masking repertoire also encapsulates the ongoing collagen obsession. One slide looks like Medicube’s PDRN Pink Collagen Gel Mask, a long-wear hydrogel treatment designed to boost hydration and give skin a visibly plumper finish. The brand’s Collagen Night Wrapping Mask offers a different experience: a liquid treatment that dries into a thin film, worn overnight to help retain moisture before being peeled or rinsed away in the morning. Despite the collagen branding, these are principally about surface hydration, softness, and the temporary appearance of bouncier skin, rather than replacing the collagen naturally found deeper in the skin.

In a recent development, and let’s not forget LOOPS’s Double Take Glow Mask, another Bieber-approved hydrogel treatment. This one brings together sunflower seed oil, aloe vera, and hyaluronic acid for a quick hit of hydration and radiance. With a suggested wear time of just 10 minutes, it’s the kind of mask you could don pre-makeup and a night out.

Recent findings suggest that the assortment also includes treatments that are harder to identify from a selfie alone. The glossy, pale grey-blue mask pictured during what appears to be a professional facial resembles an alginate or rubberizing treatment, which is typically applied as a thick paste and allowed to set before removal. Such treatments can help retain moisture against the skin, although the exact benefits depend on their ingredients. The yellow and lavender-grey formulas remain mysteries for now.

Bieber’s carousel also features an LED light-therapy mask, another fixture of the increasingly high-tech celebrity skincare routine. Red and near-infrared light are commonly used to support collagen production and improve the appearance of fine lines and skin texture over time, while blue light is used for certain forms of acne. The precise device and light setting in Bieber's photograph aren’t clear (although we know her bestie Kendall loves her TheraFace Mask Glo), but the benefits of these treatments generally depend on consistency rather than a single session.

Sources indicate that bieber’s routine, of course, extends beyond what comes in a jar or compressed between plastic. She’s previously discussed PRP and PRF treatments, microneedling, and occasional laser sessions.

Industry observers note that for anyone inspired to amp up their own mask collection, the crucial thing is to choose according to what your skin actually needs. Hyaluronic acid, glycerin, ceramides, and other hydrating ingredients make sense for tight, dehydrated skin; caffeine-based treatments can provide a temporary depuffing effect; and clarifying clay masks can be useful for excess oil, provided they don’t leave the skin feeling stripped. Apply hydrating sheet masks after cleansing and before moisturizer, unless the product directs otherwise. Cream masks generally need rinsing, while overnight wraps are designed to be the final step of an evening routine. Follow the recommended wear time: leaving a mask on longer doesn't automatically make it more effective. Introduce new formulas gradually, especially if your skin is reactive.

And while Bieber makes the case for having a mask for every occasion, those with active perioral dermatitis should be more selective. Heavy, occlusive products and unfamiliar ingredients can worsen the condition, and the best approach during a flare-up may be to forgo extra masking entirely in favor of a simple, dermatologist-guided routine.

It has been revealed that ultimately, the lesson from Hailey Bieber’s collection isn’t that you need eight different masks to achieve good skin. It’s that skincare is rarely one-size-fits-all, even for the woman who helped turn a glossy complexion into a billion-dollar beauty business.

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Sources indicate that now more than ever, you should hold your TV to a higher standard. More and more streaming content is available in 4K UHD resolution, which has four times as many pixels as standard Full HD (1080p). Video games, including PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2, support higher refresh rates that only TVs from the past few years support.

It has been revealed that 4K TVs are the standard, and have been for some time. Technically, 8K TVs are available, but there’s no indication that anyone is making content to take advantage of them anytime soon.

While tech prices are abnormally high in 2026, the tech is still improving rapidly. And since most of us buy a TV every five to 10 years, even last year’s models will offer a huge upgrade and are generally much more reasonably priced. New TVs are out there for everyone, at every price point.

According to recent reports, I handpicked 4K TVs based on my testing and included options at various price points from current leading manufacturers: LG, Samsung, Hisense, and TCL. The selection process involved parsing through hardware specs, attending live demo sessions, and consulting with other industry experts.

Sources indicate that unless indicated otherwise, I usually test the 65-inch version of each TV, since it usually offers the best balance of price and capabilities as the primary home entertainment centerpiece in your space. Most sets are also available in smaller, less expensive versions. And many are available in even XXL formats, 75 inches and higher, for households with larger spaces and bigger budgets.

In a recent development, A note on these picks: Even though we’re well into 2026, we still primarily recommend TVs that rolled out in 2025, even when a newer version is available. From what my colleagues and I have seen so far, I believe that last year’s models represent the best possible value right now. In time, as last year’s models sell out, the value proposition will change. But trust me when I say that these TVs provide the best value and will make your reveals, movies, and games look great for years to come.

Now that the price has come down a bit, we’re prepared to recommend this year’s LG C-series TV, the C6 evo, as the best option for most people. Though it isn't dramatically different from its predecessor, this mid-range OLED maintains the line’s legacy as impressively slim, elegant, and capable of delivering a stunning picture. It also runs a feature-packed platform with deep smart home integration.

In a recent development, with millions of individually backlit pixels, the C6’s OLED display is a rock-solid contender for the best in its price range. The panel’s flawless black reproduction delivers perfect contrast and vivid colors, making any content—from a newscast to a blockbuster movie to an AAA video game—look its best.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of gaming, the C6 is also one of the best TVs on the market for the task. In addition to being a great companion for the latest gaming consoles, the TV can double as a top-tier gaming monitor, thanks to a 165 Hz refresh rate and support for AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync. It can also deliver high-powered cloud-based gameplay via an Nvidia GeForce Now subscription.

According to recent reports, as with previous years, the C6 also gets extra credit for its wide size range. Depending on your needs and budget, you can choose a compact 42-inch, a private movie theater-worthy 83-inch model, or one of several additional sizes in between. Keep in mind that larger screen models have brighter Tandem OLED screens.

With a price cut shortly after launch, the TCL QM8L is ready to replace its predecessor, the QM8K, as the top Mini-LED TV. It looks incredibly sleek sans top and side bezels, and the picture looks just as impressive. While OLED technology still broadly produces the richest and sharpest image quality, mini-LED TVs are no slouch, delivering great detail and a brighter screen that improves performance in less-than-stellar lighting conditions.

It has been revealed that with thousands of local dimming zones and an upgraded AI-powered processor to control them, the QM8L’s super quantum-dot mini-LED screen delivers a captivating picture with rich colors and deep contrast. The TV’s picture quality comes close to a top-tier OLED TV. Its higher peak brightness and lower cost sufficiently make up for its lack of individually backlit pixels.

If you are looking for a mini-LED 4K TV with SQD color proficiency on a tighter budget, I think this model’s more affordable cousin, the TCL QM7L, is also a very good choice. You lose some peak brightness and local dimming zones, but it still provides amazing performance for its much lower price.

TCL QM8L 4K SQD Mini-LED TV Review.

TCL QM7L 4K SQD Mini-LED TV Review.

Recent findings suggest that RGB Mini-LED TVs deliver a unique combination of high peak brightness and stellar color accuracy, with the latter made possible by separate red, blue, and green light diodes instead of a single one in their display panels. Of all the TV newcomers to offer this screen technology in 2026, the Hisense UR9 is the one I’d recommend to most buyers. Beyond the exceptional picture quality from its fresh display panel, the TV also delivers surprisingly powerful sound and a rich set of futureproof connectivity features.

In addition to producing a bright picture with vibrant-yet-accurate colors and deep contrast, the Hisense UR9 surprised me pleasantly by handling direct light reflections surprisingly well. Dubbed “Obsidian” by its maker, the standout glare-reduction feature results in a top-tier viewing experience in bright spaces.

The TV’s screen supports a high 180Hz refresh rate, cutting latency in video games and smoothing blurred movement in live sports. I’m also a major fan of its 4.1.2-channel speaker system tuned by Devialet — a French luxury audio brand — and its two-year warranty.

Sources indicate that consider the Hisense UR8 if you are looking for an RGB Mini-LED TV on a tighter budget. It is a step down in peak brightness and audio performance from the UR9, as its model number suggests, but the lower price makes up for the shortcomings. Unlike its flagship sibling, the UR8 is also available with a 55-inch screen.

Hisense UR9 RGB Mini-LED TV Review.

TCL’s QM6K is my favorite 4K TV on a budget. Spending less than $600 before additional deals and discounts, gets you a TV with a sleek design, superb picture quality, a feature-packed platform, and an abundant set of connectivity options. With a high-performance game mode and support for variable refresh rate, the TV is also a top-notch gaming console display.

Recent findings suggest that the TCL QM6K delivers superb picture quality and color rendering for a TV at such an agreeable price point. Its quantum-dot mini-LED display panel with hundreds of local dimming zones produces punchy colors and dramatic contrast that defy its price category. I can’t think of a better 4K TV for the money.

On the audio front, the TV is as impressive as it is in terms of picture quality. Its speaker system, tuned by Onkyo, has a built-in subwoofer, allowing it to deliver immersive sound with surprisingly powerful bass.

Industry observers note that TCL offers the QM6K in several screen sizes, with the 98-inch model as the largest. The biggest screen size costs a little over $2,000, which is quite a bargain for the full-blown private movie theater experience it provides. The 85-inch version at a tad above $1,000 is also a great value for money.

Recent findings suggest that the Samsung S95H is the 4K TV to get if you want stunning design and picture quality to match. The TV’s metal frame gives it a unique presence, especially when wall-mounted, and makes any rival look generic in comparison. Its super-bright QD-OLED display predictably produces vibrant colors and deep contrast. Plus, a sophisticated onboard processor with access to AI neural networks makes lower-resolution content look sharper than ever.

According to recent reports, most importantly, the Samsung S95H can effortlessly deliver this viewing experience from any angle, even in bright spaces. The TV’s screen has a glare-free finish, which makes it practically impervious to light reflections. This means its picture quality stays superb even when it’s facing a lamp, a window, or another light source. This quality alone makes the TV worth every penny.

In keeping with its price category, the Samsung S95H is also a bona fide gaming powerhouse, capable of delivering exceptional visuals when connected to a gaming console or a high-powered computer. Samsung’s Tizen platform also supports cloud gaming, so all you need is a wireless controller and a monthly subscription to enjoy AAA titles.

We like that the TV’s intuitive remote has a rechargeable battery that you can charge via a light source or a USB-C port, so you never have to swap batteries. Its multi-speaker Dolby Atmos audio system, meanwhile, defies its form factor.

The TCL X11L is the best major-screen TV on the market today, with an elegant design, outstanding picture quality, and immersive sound tuned by Bang & Olufsen. We often think of TCL as the bang for your buck, but this set demonstrates the brand can also deliver something out of this world for folks willing to spend big for the best possible picture.

The secret is the X11L's first-of-its-kind SQD Mini-LED display—that's "Super Quantum Dot"—which blends brightness-enhancing quantum dot technology with Mini-LED dimming zones to boost high-dynamic-range performance.

Sources indicate that at a $7,000 launch price, it was hard to imagine not insisting on an OLED TV over the TCL X11L, but things have changed dramatically since then. Now that it starts at $3,000 for a 75-inch version, the high-end TCL offering is a great buy. Its color accuracy and contrast are both top-notch, and the overall picture quality is tremendous. Frankly, I’d take the TV over any OLED on the market today.

TCL X11L 4K SQD Mini-LED TV Review.

TVs that double as home decor pieces by displaying artwork or photos became a thing when Samsung launched The Frame almost a decade ago. Since then, frame-like TVs have grown from a niche category into something with broader appeal and a surprisingly rich selection across the price spectrum. The Hisense S7 CanvasTV is the one I’d recommend to most buyers in 2026, because it strikes a fine balance between elegant design, stellar picture quality, and a rich selection of onboard features, all at a reasonable price and in multiple screen sizes.

Thanks to a quantum-dot display with a matte finish to reduce pesky reflections and an ambient light sensor, the S7 CanvasTV can display beautiful visuals in any scenario, whether it’s live sports or a vacation photo. Still, you should know the device’s picture quality can’t match that of similarly priced conventional Hisense TVs or rival brands with quantum-dot or RGB mini-LED screens. The matte screen, customizable frame, and slim wall mount make the S7 CanvasTV worth considering, since it will look great when not in use.

When it comes to alternatives, the first that comes to mind is Samsung's The Frame Pro. It offers a more polished design and a fancier quantum-dot mini-LED panel with superior glare resistance and artwork display capabilities. The Frame Pro will look much nicer as an art piece, but I’d still take the Hisense S7 CanvasTV for offering Dolby Vision HDR support and a full set of built-in connectivity features. Samsung has these essentials in a separate box for The Frame Pro.

Hisense S7 CanvasTV Series Review.

Industry observers note that though they all look like black slabs on the wall, the quality of the images produced by 4K TVs can vary dramatically from model to model. Many also have distinctive features that make them better for specific applications—like a high refresh rate for gaming. And, of course, all that impacts how much they cost. Here are the most notable things to keep in mind while shopping:.

According to recent reports, there is all manner of exotic formulae for determining the exact distance you should sit from a large screen TV—X-times the screen height, X-times the screen’s diagonal size—but there isn’t a right or wrong answer. The best rule of thumb is if the screen fills your frame of vision from where you’re sitting, and you don’t have to turn your head to see one side of the screen or the other, you’re fine. (Note: Sitting too close to a 4K TV won’t ruin your eyes despite what your mother may have told you.).

Industry observers note that what size TV you choose, however, may be predetermined by your room geography and/or furnishings, such as the interior of an existing TV cabinet, or dictated by a spouse’s objections to a larger-size set. If you plan to buy a new TV larger than your current set, measure the width, height, and depth of your home’s TV space, and then check the actual width and height of the TV with stand, not the diagonal screen size. A flat panel 65-inch screen 4K TV usually measures less than 60 inches wide, less than 36 inches tall, and about 15 inches deep with the stand.

Building a Home Theater? Check These Guides Next: Best OLED TVs • Best Wireless Surround Sound Systems • Best TV Wall Mounts.

Sources indicate that some TVs come with center stands, while many larger models have feet at either end of the set, which may be too widely spaced apart for your TV stand. Check the width of your TV tabletop and the space between the feet of your prospective TV purchase to make sure its feet will fit.

Planning to hang your TV on a wall? All TVs follow a version of the VESA (Video Electronics Standards Association) wall-mounting standard, including variations such as VESA MIS-D, MIS-E, and MIS-F, which mainly address a TV’s rear mounting-hole spacing, supportable weight, and size.

A VESA wall mounting kit can work with virtually any wall-mountable TV, but double-check your TV’s specifications to confirm any VESA variation.

Recent findings suggest that A 4K TV’s display is composed of 3840 x 2160 pixels, but that’s only the screen resolution. A dizzying array of screen technologies creates different levels of stunning 4K images. These technologies include:.

A TV screen's image speed is measured by its refresh rate, expressed in hertz (Hz). This equals frames flashed per second; for comparison, movie film is projected at 24 frames per second, while Normal TV broadcasts refresh at 60 Hz, or 60 frames per second.

If you’re a heavy gamer, you want a display that more accurately reflects the eye-blinking speed of the animated action, which means you’ll want a TV with a refresh rate of at least 120 Hz or higher, and a set equipped with VRR (variable refresh rate), which automatically adjusts the refresh rate depending on the content being displayed.

Another screen technology gamers want is low latency, or input lag, which is how promptly the display responds when you push a button on your controller or joystick. Many higher-end TVs include Auto Low Latency Mode (ALLM), which automatically switches your TV to a faster, more responsive mode measured in milliseconds (ms).

Yes, but you only need to concern yourself with the types your 4K TV includes. Nearly all bigger-screen 4K TVs are equipped with a type of HDR (high-dynamic range) that creates visibly punchier, higher-contrast images when viewing 4K content from Blu-ray or streaming channels.

Different HDR versions include the standard and most common HDR, as well as the more specialized HDR-10, HDR-10+, Dolby Vision, and HLG (Hybrid Log Gamma), designed to deliver HDR benefits to lower non-4K broadcast, cable, and satellite TV fare.

While there are subtle visual benefits associated with each type of HDR, and while some TV makers, 4K Blu-ray producers, and streaming channels opt to deploy some HDR versions but not others, compatibility really isn’t an concern since all include a plain and widely compatible HDR version.

Bottom line: Any set featuring any type of HDR will produce a visibly better 4K picture than a set without HDR.

8K TV makers may not want to hear this, but probably never. 8K TVs offer a display with a resolution of 7,680 x 4,320 pixels, or 33 million pixels, more than four times the 8 million pixels that comprise a 4K TV display.

In a recent development, prices are coming down to near 4K TV price levels for 8K models. But, for a variety of reasons, there is no existing 8K content—no 8K broadcast or cable, no 8K streaming, no 8K Blu-ray—and there isn’t likely to be for the foreseeable future.

In a recent development, the only benefits of an 8K TV are via upscaling or up-conversion of lower-resolution programming to 8K. But realistically you’ll need at least a 75-inch TV to appreciate the difference between 4K and 8K.

Imagine watching the movie "Jaws" without feeling that "bum-bum, bum-bum" bass in your gut, or not being able to understand character dialogue over a swelling orchestral passage, or subtle sounds that lend a dramatic scene its key ambience.

Recent findings suggest that A 4K TV may produce excellent picture quality, but most do not produce equally excellent sound, which can dull or ruin your viewing experience. There is a fix for this. Instead of relying on a TV’s poor audio, you may want to pair your 4K TV with a soundbar via an ARC (Audio Return Channel) or eARC (enhanced Audio Return Channel) HDMI connection.

An ARC-compatible soundbar connected to a TV via an ARC HDMI jack lets you control your TV’s picture and sound with a single remote, as if the soundbar were your TV’s speaker.

Just make sure to measure the space between your TV tabletop and the bottom of the TV display area so your prospective soundbar won’t block either the screen or the TV’s IR remote control sensor.

Now, the Prince and Princess of Wales have traveled to the Indian city for the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards, which are being hosted in Asia for the first time ever. The annual prize, founded by Prince William with an inaugural ceremony in 2021 and set to last until 2030, celebrates innovators who are breaking ground in the environmentalism space.

They began with a trip to the Ballard Estate, the business and shopping district of Mumbai. There, the Prince and Princess of Wales played a bit of gully cricket, took a ride on the metro, and visited local vendors and performers.

For the rest of their time abroad, the royals will be “celebrating innovation, sustainability, youth leadership, and the enduring connections between the United Kingdom and India,” per their office at Kensington Palace.

It has been revealed that in our Cooking With Friends series, friends of Delish visit the Test Kitchen to share their favorite recipes with you. Happy cooking!

Recent findings suggest that this is my mom’s recipe, and it taught me what simple abundance really looks like. She’d grate tomatoes and spoon the sauce over her native South African pap (a dish made from cornmeal, similar to grits or polenta), rice, ground beef, or almost anything that needed a little love. I couldn’t believe something so good could come from a handful of ingredients, and she showed me that with this dish it’s not about adding more, but how you handle what you have.

The magic is in the grating. It separates the sweet tomato pulp and leaves the skins behind, giving you the pure heart of the fruit. Please don’t skip the beef bouillon—it gives the sauce its deeper savory backbone. I love this tossed with freshly made spaghetti or tagliatelle, though dried pasta works beautifully, too—exactly like my mom makes it. You can enjoy this year-round, but it’s especially delightful in summer, when tomatoes taste like the sun.
