📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on Saturday evening at West Hollywood’s Pacific Design Center, Demi Moore asked a ballroom filled with Hollywood stars to take two deep breaths. The actress, who was being honored at Baby2Baby’s 15th anniversary gala, wanted everyone to consider the sense of relief that comes when a parent no longer has to worry about providing basic necessities for their child. It was one of the evening’s most moving moments, and a reminder of the mission behind a night that would go on to raise over $20 million dollars—the highest fundraising total for the nonprofit to date.

Presented by Paul Mitchell, the annual benefit drew a guest list that included Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau, Jessica Alba, Kerry Washington, Ciara, Chrissy Teigen, Paris Hilton, Sofía Vergara, Elsa Hosk, and Miranda Kerr, all gathering once more to celebrate the beloved organization.

In a recent development, before the massive night got underway, guests were treated to a luxe dining experience featuring 20 chefs and endless options. Jon Shook and Vinny Dotolo oversaw the hors d’oeuvres, which included tuna tartare and crispy rice with avocado, before attendees made their way to a dining area filled with stations from some of the most sought-after restaurants in Los Angeles and beyond. Carbone served its signature spicy rigatoni vodka, KazuNori rolled fresh hand rolls, Funke offered cannelloni bolognese, and Matū dished out Philly cheesesteaks en masse. Ensuring something for everyone, there were also oysters from Found Oyster, brisket from Moo’s Craft Barbecue, and crowd-pleasers by Mr. Chow, Holy Basil, and Saffy’s.

According to recent reports, once everyone settled in, Keke Palmer took the stage for opening remarks, bringing her comedic chops to the program while also speaking about her own experience as a mother. Between jokes, she emphasized the importance of ensuring that all parents have access to the fundamental basics. She then welcomed the Baby2Baby Angels—Alba, Washington, Ciara, and Teigen—who have supported the organization throughout its phenomenal growth.

It has been revealed that for co-CEOs Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein, the evening was an opportunity to reflect on just how much has changed since Baby2Baby’s early days. What began as a grassroots operation in Los Angeles has grown into a nationwide organization reaching 1.5 million children annually across all 50 states and distributing more than 850 million items over the past 15 years.

“We started from day one with our mission of providing basic essentials to children in need and knew we had a lot of work ahead of us,” Sawyer Patricof told Vogue. “We didn’t anticipate that our mission would naturally evolve into disaster relief because children living in poverty are the most vulnerable in every situation.”.

Recent findings suggest that the organization has now responded to more than 150 disasters nationwide, from the devastating Los Angeles wildfires to hurricanes in Florida and flooding in Texas. Another recent milestone came through its maternal health initiative. After piloting a program with the Biden administration to provide latest mothers with critical supplies immediately after giving birth, Baby2Baby secured a $9 million investment from New York State last year.

The funding, Weinstein told Vogue, will provide Maternal Health & Newborn Supply Kits to 100,000 mothers giving birth on Medicaid across Fresh York, along with millions of diapers for low-income families. “We lit up the Empire State Building in Baby2Baby green to celebrate this milestone,” she added, proudly.

Diaper access, however, remains at the center of Baby2Baby’s work. Over the years, the organization has successfully advocated for the elimination of sales tax on diapers in California and developed its own manufacturing system, allowing it to produce diapers for up to 80% less than average retail cost.

“Diaper need has been at the core of our mission, as nearly half of families in this country are struggling to afford them,” Weinstein and Sawyer Patricof noted. This year brought another major development with California’s first-in-the-nation Golden State Start program, which aims to provide 400 free Baby2Baby diapers to every newborn in the state through participating hospitals.

Back inside the ballroom, the evening’s lively fundraising efforts were already well underway. By the time Julie Bowen and Jenna Dewan stepped up to kick off the live auction, Baby2Baby had raised $7.5 million. Guests were encouraged to consider the huge impact of their donations: Every $1 million contribution will help to provide some 10 million diapers to children in need.

Sources indicate that andrew Garfield soon arrived on the podium to introduce Moore, who was presented with this year’s Giving Tree Award for her advocacy for children and families. A video montage featuring messages from Jon Hamm, Salma Hayek, Drew Barrymore, Jennifer Garner, and Moore’s daughters, among others, paid tribute to the actress before she addressed the room with a poignant speech. Moore reflected on motherhood and the importance of having a support system while raising children, pausing to look out to see her own daughters Rumer, Scout, and Tallulah Willis smiling back at her in the crowd.

Sources indicate that with the most emotive moments behind them and a record-breaking fundraising target achieved, the crowd was ready to let loose. Katy Perry and Kelly Rowland introduced Cardi B, who sent the room wild with a performance of some of her most famous hits. Within moments, there wasn’t a person left sitting down as the ballroom turned into a full-fledged concert.

And the party didn’t stop there. Guests continued on to an after-party where DJ D-Nice kept the music going, while another round of food awaited anyone who had worked up an appetite. Burger She Wrote served late-night burgers, Chainsaw offered sweet treats, and Henry’s Secret Ice Cream and Leora rounded out the dessert offerings.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that “We had all these big dreams when we were young,” Jones notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This summer, The Invite dropped audiences into a turbulent middle-aged marriage where only bitterness simmers beneath a thin, leftover layer of love and any sexual desire vanished long ago. The couple at the center of the story, Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela (Olivia Wilde, who also directed the film), live at each other’s throats, feigning a relationship for their daughter’s sake. This brittle romance is put to the test when a neighboring couple (Ed Norton and Penélope Cruz) come over for dinner and propose, well, group sex. Bottled-up emotions and memories fill the night as four dinner guests banter and battle, delivering the best sex comedy in years, elevated by witty, cathartic dialogue from screenwriters Rashida Jones and Will McCormack.

In a recent development, A great sex comedy relies on a great premise, whether it’s designed to shock or move its audience. Jones and McCormack reworked Spanish filmmaker Cesc Gay’s The People Upstairs (also known as Sentimental), crafting a script that balances both, exploring how romantic turmoil emerges from a culture of emotional suppression and what happens when this lifestyle rubs up against a more radically open approach to feelings and sex. Much of the realism in The Invite comes from Jones and McCormack closely studying their own relationships with love and loss.

It has been revealed that “We had all these big dreams when we were young,” Jones notes. “It’s a real embarrassment of riches. It’s when you get to 50, and you’ve had a lot of your dreams come true, and you have all the things that you dreamed about when you were 20, 30, and even 40. Here we are, and what now? The ‘what now’ is infused in the movie.”.

Decades of friendship have informed Jones and McCormack’s writing. They first met on a blind date in 1999, but the romantic relationship did not stick; in its place, a creative partnership blossomed. In 2012, they released their first full-length feature, Celeste and Jesse Forever, a bittersweet examination of divorce and friendship starring Jones and Andy Samberg.

“When we were young, we were writing about the heartbreak of love, and now we’re writing about the heartbreak of life,” McCormack states. “Marriage is not this triumphant experience. It’s a broken hallelujah; it’s one day at a time. That’s the beauty of it: the endurance of it and the longevity of it.”.

Bazaar sat down and spoke with the pair about tailoring their script around a quartet of legendary actors, the “accordion effect” of Olivia Wilde’s direction, and how the two screenwriters have bounced ideas (and sex jokes) off each other for three decades.

It has been revealed that rashida Jones: In 2022, we were approached by David Permit, one of our wonderful producers, and we were hired to write a script for a whole different version of this movie for different directors. It was probably the most fun I’ve ever had, writing that first draft with Will. We just had a great time because we saw the movie and it totally works and it’s culturally specific. We watched it at first, and we thought, “Wow, it’s perfectly executed. What can we contribute?” Then you watch it again and again and again, and you start having conversations about your own life and your own relationships and people that are on your mind. We started to feel like we might have something to say in this world and that could add value and be more culturally specific to being American. How we would have this conversation—this evening, in our country. It felt like the perfect combination of source material and then a place to grow.

RJ: I’ll take the easy part. We’re just immature, and we like to make sex jokes to each other because we’ve been best friends for 30 years, so that was easy.

It has been revealed that will McCormack: There’s no DP. We brought all the DP.

It has been revealed that WM: We were having fun with that stuff. Cesc Gay’s movie is so brilliant. When we watched it, you think, “Oh my God, this is so beautiful.” But then, as Rashida said, you start to think about it more, and you say, “Wouldn’t it be fun to do this?” And then you get the job, and you actually get to do that. It’s so rare. When we watched the original one, I remember halfway through, we said to each other, he’s going to go in the other room at the end and play the piano, and it’s going to wreck us. And he didn’t. I liked their ending, but we thought, this is going to be so fun to dive into: [Seth Rogen’s character] pulling up the piano lid, sitting at the keys, and there’s this Graduate-style ending where she’s going to walk in and the camera is going to end on her face, and [we’re left thinking], is she in or is she out? That was our entry point to this version. It’s how we got the job, because we opened the conversation with the ending.

RJ: Rhythm is so vital to us. The truth is, when you infuse a role with an actor, rhythms change because there are things that make sense coming out of people’s mouths and things that don’t. For us, this period before shooting was our rewrite period, which was insane because we were doing eight-hour days with the actors and getting a download of their ideas and concerns, then rewriting simultaneously. That period was really when the movie was the version of the movie on the screen. It was designed for these particular actors on the screen. Their cadences entered our heads, so we needed to rewrite with them in mind. We were trying our best Penélope Cruz and Seth Rogen impressions.

Sources indicate that WC: These actors are all prodigiously gifted and giants. They all brought their own pathos and idiosyncrasies. Penélope brought this incredible mystery and mystique and aura. Edward brought this radical honesty. Olivia brought a woman on the verge of a nervous breakdown at all times. Seth brought this profound simplicity. So it was such a gift to work with them and help tailor these parts to their voices.

RJ: Penélope had a really strong instinct. She’s one of our best. What can I possibly say about her? She really wanted to talk about perimenopause, which I too have that cross to bear at the moment. She wanted to get into it and was very conscious that her character has depth. She didn’t want her to have this wise, objective point of view. She wanted to have her own life and flaws. All that stuff comes out at the end, where she bites back at Hawk and tells him to shut the fuck up and then apologizes rapidly. You get a window into their relationship. That really came out of conversations of “How can we show how imperfect their very new relationship is? How can we show that everybody’s struggling with their version of an issue?” It’s not all perfect over there just because they have figured out a way to live in an open relationship.

WC: The magic of movie-making is that there are a million different versions of The Invite. This version could’ve only happened at this moment in time, in this city, with this director, with these four people. It’s magic. I was most surprised by Penélope, who was so smart and didn’t want to feel like this wise woman on the hilltop delivering sage advice to these people in the room. Because life is not like that. It’s messy and complicated, and she has her own problems. When actors are that good, they just surprise you over and over again. We’ve said it before, but the best element of storytelling and screenwriting is surprise—when you don’t know what’s going to happen next and you’re on the edge of your seat.

It has been revealed that WC: Edward is one of the best actors we have as well. He is so smart. Right from the very beginning of the rehearsal process, he wanted. He was adamant that we talk a lot about Hawk’s backstory and that his sexual expansiveness came from a place of real pain and trauma. We talked a lot about Hawk’s backstory. We talked about how he had massive regret and pain and that he had a moment in his life where he was going to fold or turn over a latest leaf and live without regret. It was incredible to talk to him about it. We never heard the final version [of the speech until the day we filmed].

RJ: He wanted to surprise the actors. We wrote him a template, a blueprint, so he had that. Then he could do whatever he wanted because he had something in mind. Coming out of that, it gave Joe another opportunity to be uncomfortable with feelings. He could just make a joke, and that would set off the next part of the interaction, so everybody could be mad at him for being immature.

According to recent reports, WC: We have Joe’s line slotted there, “I’m sorry that your dead wife couldn’t peg you,” which then detonates the entire thing again. Olivia did such a great job of orchestrating this accordion effect of quiet to blow up to quiet.

In a recent development, RJ: We have our go-tos. Nora Ephron. We’re always watching James L. Brooks for rhythm, pacing, and dialogue. Of course, Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? was a reference for us because it’s a movie we grew up both loving and a play we love. It has this chamber-piece tension that you need to keep. There are literal steals and direct references to that movie in our version, [such as including a character who works as] an associate professor. Movies like Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice and, in general, Paul Mazursky for the reality of being in a messy relationship.

Industry observers note that WC: [Ruben Östlund’s] Force Majeure and always Joachim Trier for the honesty of people being really vulnerable with each other. It’s never corny, and it’s really heartbreaking and true and admirable. The end of The Invite gets very real when she indicates, “We were best friends, and we had sex all the time, and it was incredible.” There is a moment where it really lands.

According to recent reports, RJ: Everybody’s so different. We talk a lot because, for us, theme is king. We want to make sure we know what we want to say. We identify how we want to feel and how we want other people to feel, and we write toward that. We’re not going to leave feeling like there’s a bad guy; we want to leave feeling like we root for them as people, separately and together. Whatever happens after this night, this was a necessary step in excavating the deepest emotions and truth that were never revealed, and they are left vulnerable with tenderness and gratitude for the relationship they did have. We talk in those terms, and then we get into structure, and then we can talk about which scenes are which and how we get there.

WC: Luckily, we’ve known each other for so long, and we’re so comfortable with each other. That’s so vital to a partnership. I’m not afraid to pitch any idea to Rashida and vice versa. I’m not afraid to write poorly. I feel total freedom of expression, which is an important thing in collaboration. Our lives have orbited each other in an interesting way as friends, but also creatively. We’re both really into loss, and life is a series of losses. There’s so much heartbreak and loss, but there’s so much hope and humor. The hardest moments of our lives have been the funniest, and it’s been a gift to write it all down with her. Hopefully, we can do it again!

In a recent development, after delivering a cliffhanger ending in season 6, fans of Slow Horses are wondering how the story could continue once season 7 rolls around. The fans are in luck—the MI5 agents of Slough House are clocking back in for another season, and the franchise doesn’t seem to be headed for an end anytime soon.

“I know that Gary [Oldman] has expressed a desire to play Lamb forever and that Mick [Herron] is still writing the books, so I hope it will go for as long as people want it,” the show’s executive producer, Will Smith, remarked in an October 2024 interview with TV Insider.

Here’s everything we know so far about Slow Horses season 7.

Yes! In July 2025, Deadline confirmed that Slow Horses would come back for a seventh season. The streaming platform greenlit the show’s seventh season before the fifth season of the show aired.

Gary Oldman, Jack Lowden, Kristin Scott Thomas, Jonathan Pryce, Hugo Weaving, Saskia Reeves, Rosalind Eleazar, Christopher Chung, Aimee-Ffion Edwards, Joanna Scanlan, Tom Brooke, Lucian Msamati, and Olivia Cooke are confirmed to return for season 7 of Slow Horses.

On October 19, Apple TV revealed that Varada Sethu (Andor, Doctor Who), Ethan Moorhouse (The Moment, Ludwig), Tuppence Middleton (Downton Abbey: A Upcoming Era), Merab Ninidze (Homeland), Joshua McGuire (Anatomy of a Scandal), and James Callis (Bridget Jones’s Diary)—who is returning—will join the season 7 cast.

According to an official press release, the season “is adapted from the Bad Actors novel in the Mick Herron Slough House book series, and sees Lamb and his Slow Horses on the hunt to find and neutralize a mole at the heart of the British Government before they can bring down the state.”.

The official synopsis for the book reads:.

Season 7 of Slow Horses has no premiere date yet. Season 6 arrived on Apple TV in September 2026, while season 5 aired in September 2025. Season 7 could arrive sometime in fall 2027, if it follows the same timeline as the previous seasons. We’ll have to wait until Apple makes an official announcement.

Recent findings suggest that thankfully, no. Slow Horses was already renewed for season 8 in September 2026, and then Apple TV confirmed seasons 9 and 10 in November 2026. Expect a lot more from Slough House in the future.

Taylor Swift’s Surprise Grammys Nomination Appearance Came With Easter Eggs

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Taylor Swift made Grammys history this morning, joining Kendrick Lamar as the only other artist to have five consecutive albums nominated for Album of the Year.
  • Swift has worn the horseshoe necklace multiple times before, including at the Toy Story 5 premiere in June.
  • The second necklace, featuring a horse’s head in a curved, horseshoe-shaped frame, is another nod to Jessie, who rides toy horse Bullseye in the movie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taylor Swift made Grammys history this morning, joining Kendrick Lamar as the only other artist to have five consecutive albums nominated for Album of the Year. But the singer also made a surprise appearance during the nomination announcement broadcast. In a video, she introduced the two biggest categories, Album of the Year and Song of the Year. She kept her look simple, wearing a black sweater. But fans homed in on her accessories, which included a large horseshoe necklace. Her second necklace continued the cowgirl theme with its horse charm.

Swift has worn the horseshoe necklace multiple times before, including at the Toy Story 5 premiere in June. The horseshoe seems to be an Easter egg for her Toy Story 5 song, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which is about the movie’s cowgirl character Jessie. The track was nominated for Song of the Year and Best Song Written for Visual Media this morning.

The second necklace, featuring a horse’s head in a curved, horseshoe-shaped frame, is another nod to Jessie, who rides toy horse Bullseye in the movie.

Initially, some fans thought the second necklace had a snake charm. The singer has drawn attention for wearing snake jewelry before. In March 2025, fans noticed one during her virtual appearance at the iHeartRadio Music Awards. Snakes have long been associated with Swift’s Reputation era, and Swifties have been waiting for years for her to release the rerecorded Taylor’s Version of that album.

When Swift bought back her first six albums’ masters in May 2025, she gave fans an update on that project in a public letter. “I know, I know. What about Rep TV?” she wrote. “Full transparency: I haven’t even rerecorded a quarter of it. The Reputation album was so specific to that time in my life, and I kept hitting a stopping point when I tried to remake it. All that defiance, that longing to be understood while feeling purposely misunderstood, that desperate hope, that shame-born snarl and mischief. To be perfectly honest, it’s the one album in those first six that I thought couldn’t be improved upon by redoing it. Not the music, or photos, or videos. So I kept putting it off. There will be a time (if you’re into the idea) for the unreleased Vault tracks from that album to hatch.”.

In her video today, Swift congratulated her fellow artists and playfully reflected on her own history with the two categories she presented. She noted, “Good morning, America, it’s Taylor. I’m very honored that the Grammys have asked me to be here to help reveal the last two categories for the Grammy nominations. And I first wanted to start off by saying congratulations to anyone who’s nominated for a Grammy this year in any category because what this means is that your peers—your fellow musicians, producers, engineers, artists, writers—they love what you made. And that’s the coolest feeling in the world. I hope you have a really wonderful day. The last two categories to be declared, one of them I’ve had a lot of luck in [Album of the Year, which she has won four times], and the other one I’m zero for eight. Here are the nominees for Album and Song of the Year.”.

Zendaya is no stranger to shutting down a red carpet—so did you really not expect her to deliver a major fashion serve at the 2026 Governors Awards tonight?

The annual ceremony serves as the official kickoff to the 2027 awards season, so it’s no massive surprise that the superstar and her stylist, Law Roach, started things off with a bang this evening—by cultivating a headline-worthy fashion moment worthy of the red carpet. The actor went for gold at the ceremony, choosing a shimmering metallic gown with three-dimensional padding at the hips. And better yet, the striking frock is vintage, too—from the late 2000s. Can you guess the brand and season?

According to recent reports, zendaya and Roach unearthed the fringed column gown from Giles Deacon’s fall 2007 collection, and it feels just as fresh and contemporary today (despite being almost a decade old). Of course. Zendaya and Roach are long known for turning throwback designs into modern-day hits: It’s one of their best fashion tricks. In the past, she has embraced everything from priceless archival Galliano to ’90s Versace to flashy Bob Mackie creations—and she has a knack for always making them feel just as relevant for today.

In a recent development, the substantial question is: Is this a preview into how Zendaya will approach red carpet dressing for the 2027 awards season ahead? Key Takeaways From Luxury’s Q3 Earnings

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • China’s macro environment has been a major drag on luxury’s third-quarter earnings, causing most companies to fall short of market expectations.
  • Analysts expected growth to slow in Q3, but conditions in China turned out worse than anticipated.
  • Industry observers note that kering stock plummeted 17%, following the announcement that growth at the tech giant had dropped to 1% in Q3 (vs +2% in Q2), including a 6% decrease at its largest brand, Gucci.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China’s macro environment has been a major drag on luxury’s third-quarter earnings, causing most companies to fall short of market expectations.

Analysts expected growth to slow in Q3, but conditions in China turned out worse than anticipated. The sector’s average organic sales growth ended at 4% in Q3 2026, versus 7.8% in Q2 (calculated by Goldman Sachs on the basis of a simple average of luxury companies, excluding currency impact).

Industry observers note that kering stock plummeted 17%, following the announcement that growth at the tech giant had dropped to 1% in Q3 (vs +2% in Q2), including a 6% decrease at its largest brand, Gucci. (Gucci retail sales declined by 9% on a comparable basis.) Kering and LVMH stock are each down 37% year to date, while the Hermès share price has fallen 36%.

Industry observers note that “Everyone is staying on the sidelines,” Goldman Sachs luxury analyst Erwan Rambourg says, referring to investors’ cautious stance. While he believes that Q3 marks the trough in the luxury downturn, he thinks that investors prefer to wait for tangible signs of an improvement rather than catch a falling knife.

It has been revealed that and after a stellar performance in the first half of the year, jewelry brands began decelerating in Q3. Sales at Richemont’s jewelry maisons, including Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels, rose 14% versus 24% in Q2. Sales at LVMH’s watches and jewelry division and Kering’s jewelry arm, the latter of which includes Boucheron and Pomellato, were up 6% and 11%, respectively (vs 11% and 18% in Q2). Sales at other Hermès sectors, including jewelry and home, were down 1% (vs 4% in Q2).

Sources indicate that “Richemont’s jewelry maisons growing 14% in the fiscal second quarter is a slowdown, but it’s still tremendously better than pretty much anyone else in the sector,” Rambourg flags. “That gives a first-half average of just below 20% top-line growth for jewelry, which is the core profit driver of the firm. For the first time in a while, margins have increased.”.

Here are the rest of the key takeaways from luxury’s Q3 earnings.

China’s slowdown deepened after three years of deceleration. Growth at LVMH decreased 5% in Asia, while Kering fell 8% and Hermès came in flat. “It should be noted that the macroeconomic environment [in China] remains unfavorable,” Hermès’s VP of finance Eric du Halgouët told analysts during the company’s earnings call on October 22.

While the broader picture in China remained largely unchanged, with continued weakness in the real estate market, two additional factors weighed on bottom lines: the decline in equity market performance, and China’s upcoming taxation of foreign assets. The law on taxation, which was announced in late July and applies to offshore trusts, a widely used vehicle among high-net-worth Chinese individuals, had a significant impact on the sentiment of affluent consumers; the rules have retroactive effect from 2023, and the deadline to declare and pay was just 90 days.

“The two growth engines of the industry for the past 20 years are the middle-income consumer and the Chinese consumer,” claims Morgan Stanley managing director Édouard Aubin. These two engines are now barely running.

Using LVMH as a proxy, the Chinese cohort was flattish in Q2 and down approximately 15% in Q3. Richemont also highlighted the challenges in the mainland China market, despite seeing a positive trend in Greater China. “ If anybody thinks we’re less affected by [market conditions in] China, on the contrary,” chairman Johann Rupert told reporters during a media call on Friday.

Industry observers note that some soft luxury brands are still doing well, including in China. Ralph Lauren’s Asia revenue saw 28% growth in Q3. Greater China led retail growth for Burberry (+5%), and the Greater China region was up 5.7% for Zegna Group. In the private space, Chanel and Longchamp are also understood to perform well in China.

According to recent reports, one category doing surprisingly well in China is prestige beauty. L’Oréal Group posted 7.8% growth in North Asia in Q3. “North Asia was back to high-single-digit growth for the first time since the first half of 2022. This marks a step change in L’Oréal’s growth algorithm in our view,” HSBC analysts, including Olivier Nicolaï, wrote in a note. Puig revenues rose 12.9% in Asia-Pacific. Does it suggest that Chinese customers are trading down — buying lower-ticket items like fragrances and skincare?

And is there a brighter outlook ahead for luxury brands in China? “There aren’t many hopes for things to improve in the short term,” Rambourg says. “I think China being very tough is probably going to be the case for the next two or three quarters. Visibility is quite poor. And if you leave aside bases of comparison, there’s no key underlying reason for China to do better.”.

“Q3 was a continuation of the K-shaped economy we’ve seen in recent quarters — where the top end grows, but the lower end lags as the middle-income consumer has been priced out. The brands at the top of the pyramid are doing well; the rest are not,” Aubin notes.

Zegna brand (+12.7% in Q3), Brunello Cucinelli (+13.5% in Q3), Loro Piana (“enjoying very strong growth,” according to LVMH CFO Cécile Cabanis) and Chanel (up double digits in Q1, Q2 and Q3, according to industry sources) are in the former category.

According to recent reports, at LVMH, Cabanis noted that Louis Vuitton sales came in just behind the group’s fashion division at -5%, while Dior was flat. Rambourg remains bullish on Dior. “One, Dior is more exposed to China than some other brands, so that’s painful. Two, they have a men’s business, which is not doing as well as women’s. Three, I think it takes a bit more time for [creative director] Jonathan Anderson’s products to gain weight within the brand, but it’s certainly coming,” he explains.

Louis Vuitton felt the repercussions of both its legal dispute with Chinese tea brand Molly Tea and an matter with a shipping partner — the latter weighed on quarterly growth by a little over one percentage point. Add to that a tough year-on-year comparison basis: Louis Vuitton opened a boat-shaped mega-store in Shanghai in June 2025, dubbed The Louis, which generated a surge in foot traffic. The brand is undergoing a change in strategy, according to Rambourg: “They’re in the process of moving under the influence of deputy CEO Damien Bertrand, from what Louis Vuitton was 15 months ago, which was colorful, cheerful, fashion-driven, to something more institutional, more focused on the origin of the brand, which is the art of travel.”.

A Shanghai Fashion Week attendee wears a full Louis Vuitton look.

Kering’s recent creative changes were on the agenda of the group’s earnings call. Shortly before its Q3 earnings, Kering announced the departures of Anthony Vaccarello from Saint Laurent and Seán McGirr from McQueen. And on November 5 and 6, the group announced the departure of Pierpaolo Piccioli from Balenciaga, with Martine Rose to succeed him.

While still outperforming the sector, Hermès’s growth decelerated in Q3 (+4.3% in Q3 vs +6.7% in Q2). “While Hermès’s leather goods category re-accelerated to nearly 11%, some investors questioned whether the weakness in other categories, such as ready-to-wear and accessories, could foreshadow a similar slowdown in leather goods,” Barclays director Carole Madjo says. Risk of [handbag market] saturation in China and the increasingly structured secondhand market could potentially weigh on demand over time.”.

After years of Miu Miu outperforming Prada, the trend reversed in Q2, with Prada (6.3%) surpassing Miu Miu (2.6%), and continued into Q3, as Prada grew 1% while Miu Miu contracted 3%, likely due to a higher exposure to China and the Middle East  relative to the average of the sector.

Rambourg also stressed the important polarization across brands: “In the soft luxury space, we consider Chanel is now the biggest brand — bigger than Louis Vuitton — and growing very quickly. And so that’s taking a bit of the air from the others, notably adjacent brands like Hermès. In hard luxury, Cartier is continuing to do very well and is also taking a bit of air away from their competitors. So in both soft and hard luxury, you have one dominant brand which counterintuitively is growing very quickly.”.

Industry observers note that the US might remain a luxury growth driver, but things began to decelerate this quarter, partly because of a tougher comparison basis. Hermès was up 8.8% in the Americas in Q3 (vs 13.7% in Q2), and Kering’s North American retail revenue rose 1% (vs 10% in Q2). “Investors are questioning whether this signals the beginning of a normalization in the US, and whether it will be confirmed in Q4 and beyond,” Barclays’ Madjo states.

According to recent reports, goldman Sachs’s Rambourg dismissed concerns: “I do believe that the little softness in Q3 is temporary. I foresee a re-acceleration in Q4 linked to the easier comparison basis and the reality that holiday campaigns, newly introduced products and more thoughtful pricing should motivate people to buy. Not to mention that you had a lot of wealth creation from equity markets. Luxury demand has been a bit lagging, but I think it’s bound to pick up.”.

It is unclear whether the US midterm elections — which saw the Democrats take control of Congress for the remainder of Trump’s presidency — impacted the third quarter. Some customers possibly adopted a wait-and-see approach to spending ahead of the results, which could now be released and influence Q4. “Midterm elections typically have less impact than presidential elections,” Madjo notes. Asked what impact the outcome might have on Richemont’s business, CFO Burkhart Grund remarked: “We’re just a few days after the midterm elections and we haven’t really picked up anything meaningful.”.

Recent findings suggest that europe was up 4% for LVMH, down 5% for Kering’s fashion and leather goods division (including a 9% drop for Gucci), and up 7.2% for Hermès. “It is Europeans who are spending in Europe,” said Hermès’s Eric du Halgouët. Hermès’s sales in France decreased in Q3 to 3.6% from 6.2% in Q2, as the heatwave impacted footfall in the Parisian stores.

In a recent development, as brands began gearing up for the crucial holiday season, protests erupted across France, Italy, Spain, Belgium and Portugal. France and Italy are significant European markets. France accounted for 8% of LVMH’s total revenue in the first nine months of 2026 and 9.6% of Hermès’s nine-month revenues. “The comments on the impact of the protests in Europe were quite vague. It’s too hard to say and hard to quantify,” Madjo states.

LVMH’s earnings call took place before the so-called Act I, the day of major urban unrest on October 17. On October 22, Hermès’s du Halgouët noted it was too early to assess impact on local stores’ business and tourism. (The Hermès store in Marseille was looted and store windows in Paris, Nantes and Lyon were broken.) “It’s not just a China problem. Now, you have a French-Italian problem on top of that,” Aubin notes, referring to the possible effects on Q4.

Recent findings suggest that despite the lack of visibility in China and Europe, Goldman Sachs’s Rambourg anticipates a progression in Q4 and next year. “Because we see the US re-accelerating, and importantly, we see self-help measures — product launches and better pricing — motivating consumers to come back,” he says.

Ayo Edebiri is one of the best-dressed people in Hollywood. In 2024, GQ named her a rising star in menswear. At our 2026 Men of the Year party, she made an even stronger case for herself as a style icon for the ages. Walking the red carpet at the Chateau Marmont in West Hollywood, the Emmy-winning actor continued her winning streak of power suiting in a navy chalk-stripe ensemble, a bright emerald-turquoise dress shirt, and a burgundy geometric tie. Her bob was styled in a side part, with a pronounced curl sweeping across her forehead. It’s a look that’s become a staple among Hollywood’s best-dressed men this year, a callback to Superman’s signature swoop, minus the Spandex tights and cape.

In the 1920s, the playful wisp of hair was known as the kiss curl: a deliberately placed lock of hair that sat on the forehead, even amid an otherwise carefully sculpted ’do. (As Seth Rogen helpfully pointed out on Instagram after we noted the kiss curl’s 2026 resurgence: “It’s called a Forelock.”) Its prominence in men’s grooming can be traced back in part to the French-American entertainer Josephine Baker, whose iconic curl ushered in an era—and now a century—of rogue forehead curls.

Recent findings suggest that the kiss curl was so emblematic of the era that it made a triumphant return at the 2025 Met Gala, themed “Superfine: Tailoring Black Style.” A host of women paired the look with impeccable tailoring, including Simone Biles, Taraji P. Henson, Teyana Taylor, and, yes, Ayo Edebiri.

In a recent development, the modern appeal of the forehead curl is easy to understand. As hairstyles have grown longer, looser, and less structured, the curl lends an air of studied nonchalance—as if you didn’t spend too much time getting your hair just right. It’s sexy in a just-got-out-of-bed kind of way, especially when everything else—from the rest of the hair to the outfit—remains crisp, clean, and pristine.

As Edebiri once told Vogue of dressing for the red carpet: “One of the fun parts of getting to do this sort of thing is that you get to transform and be these different permutations of yourself.” At GQ’s Men of the Year party, she once again understood the assignment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, with the wellness industry still booming, we’re inundated with products and devices that promise a shortcut to total health. Now, there’s a long list of gadgets, apps, topical creams, and ingestible supplements designed to clear your mind, calm your nervous system, boost energy, and improve sleep.

Industry observers note that one supplement class that continues to reign in the mainstream is greens powders, more than just green juice in powder form. Below, the experts unpack everything you really need to know about the new generation of greens supplements.

These supercharged green food powders aren’t just specialty items at vitamin shops; you can now find them everywhere—from drugstores to Amazon. But according to Philippa May, co-founder of women-first greens powder brand Naere, the big players have one glaring problem: they’re created by men, for men.

“We created Nectar 01 as an antidote to the male-dominated market,” she says. “The highly successful green powders already in the category were built around male-focused language: performance, optimization, stronger. And supplements aimed at women often leaned into insecurities: de-bloat, anti-aging, fixing your skin, helping you ‘bounce back.’ We felt there was nothing truly speaking to women as they are, beyond problems to be solved, and instead as modern individuals navigating the natural flux of daily life, in need of support rather than correction.”.

In a recent development, this is where the next generation of greens powders comes in. Sitting alongside Naere is the much-hyped LymaID²: the biohacking superbrand’s latest launch (and its most accessibly priced offering, too). Founder Lucy Goff enlists the most revered specialists in a field to power her revolutionary debuts, so she created ID² in collaboration with Professor Paul Clayton, a clinical pharmacologist and senior scientific adviser to the U.K. government.

Recent findings suggest that similarly, Catherine Hurley has focused on organic powdered fruits and vegetables, rather than a long list of trendy ingredients that may appeal to the world’s biohacking bros. Her Newroad 30 powder contains a megadose of polyphenol-rich fruits and berries, alongside vegetables and pulses to support the gut microbiome. In short, it’s not a hack for superhuman fitness, but a real-food supplement to boost your existing diet.

Industry observers note that most of these powders contain greens—from common produce like spinach and kale to specialty greens like alfalfa grass and chlorophyll. These powders often also include fiber-rich foods, probiotic sources, and digestive enzymes to help further reduce bloating.

But what do the experts really think? Nutritionists largely agree that greens powders can support wellness, but only when paired with a healthy, varied diet. (If your core food groups are Pret sandwiches and cortisol, mainlining a glass of greens each morning won’t save you.).

“The starting point for me is always food,” says Jessica Shand, a naturopathic nutritionist and author of The Hormone Balance Handbook. “No powder will ever replace the benefits of eating a wide variety of vegetables, fruit, legumes, nuts, and seeds because whole foods provide so much more than individual vitamins and minerals alone. They contain fiber, polyphenols, phytonutrients, and thousands of interactions that we simply cannot fully replicate in a supplement,” she says.

That noted, we also have to be realistic about how people live. “Busy schedules, frequent travel, limited access to fresh produce, or simply not consuming enough plant variety are all situations where a greens or plant powder may be helpful,” Shand adds. “However, I would only ever recommend a high-quality product, and, in my opinion, those are relatively few and far between.”.

In a recent development, so, which greens powders are really worth investing in? Below, see the Bazaar breakdown of the supplements to stick to this year, all editor-tested.

Lyma is a brand known for moving the goalposts with its innovative (albeit investment-level) products, and ID²—the brand’s probiotic powdered supplement—is no different.

Industry observers note that “The modern diet leaves most of us less than what we could be,” claims Paul Clayton, a professor who worked with the brand on the launch. “Lyma ID² was built to put those elements back into place—the ones that the science of the longest-living people in human history told us matter most.”.

Based on the philosophy that longevity begins with a healthy gut, ID² contains a diverse range of prebiotic fibers, since no single strain benefits every section of the gut, along with bioavailable omega-3s and a range of minerals and vitamins.

Personally, I saw a huge difference after drinking the formula religiously for six weeks, especially with bloating. By the one-month mark, my midafternoon brain fog had all but subsided. And thanks to the genuinely pleasant grapefruit taste, I’ve stuck with it for several months now.

In a recent development, newroad 30 is a gut supplement containing 30 organic powdered fruits and vegetables. Rather than focusing on greens, which can be an acquired taste, founder Catherine Hurley has placed red fruits and berries at the center of her formula. “They provide a rich source of polyphenols and antioxidants that support gut health, skin health, and healthy aging,” she explains. “We still include vegetables and pulses, but their flavors sit behind the berry profile. The result is a product that delivers the benefits while tasting genuinely great, making it much easier to enjoy every day.” Indeed, if you’ve struggled to commit to an earthy greens powder before, this black-currant-tinged powder is the one to choose, delivering vitamins and minerals to support a healthy gut microbiome without the unpleasant taste.

Industry observers note that another benefit is how Newroad 30 is made. “We freeze-dry every ingredient. Most powders are spray-dried, and this method doesn’t preserve nutrients, fiber, and polyphenols as well as freeze-drying, which also preserves flavor,” says Hurley. Everything is organic here, too—an important consideration because, as Hurley explains, “the process of drying the ingredients concentrates any pesticides present.”.

It has been revealed that lastly, what’s not in this plant-powered powder is as important as what is. “I would not want to take a powder with additives, such as sweeteners, flavorings, colors, emulsifiers, and binders,” Hurley adds, and Newroad 30 is free of them.

One of the longstanding powdered supplements on the market, Elle Macpherson’s The Super Elixir Daily Greens is particularly beneficial for those navigating hormonal shifts, such as perimenopause. Alongside prebiotics, four probiotic strains, adaptogenic botanicals, and powdered greens, it includes a cocktail of vitamins and minerals—from ginseng and glutamine to B vitamins—designed to boost energy and reduce brain fog. For the skin challenges that often come at this time (think: loss of laxity and dryness), it also includes biotin and zinc.

In a recent development, while this power cocktail won’t directly balance your hormones, it will provide a strong nutritional foundation to support the body through such a seismic shift. The taste is distinctly “green” (if you’re picky about flavor, expect a challenge), but the energy-boosting potential is real.

Industry observers note that the original green powder, AG1, was made with athletes in mind but is for anyone who needs extra physical energy and mental clarity. Essentially, it’s a potent, well-rounded multivitamin that provides 100 percent of the RDA for key nutrients, including vitamins C and E, energy-providing B vitamins, two strains of gut-boosting probiotics, plant superfoods, and stress-reducing adaptogens.

In a recent development, anecdotal praise for this one isn’t hard to find: Chances are, you already know one loyal devotee. However, the formula notably lacks iron, which, since women generally need more iron than men, points to the brand’s male-leaning marketing. Also, keep in mind the formula is a proprietary blend, so the brand doesn’t disclose the exact amount of each ingredient.

Built by women, for women, Naere brings ingredient transparency to the supplements space with its online Integrity Index™—a digital service that analyzes any supplement, from any brand, and delivers a detailed breakdown of its safety and efficacy based on your personal needs.

In a recent development, this uncompromising focus on quality over quantity naturally follows through into its debut launch, Nectar 01. This powdered supplement contains 30 ingredients—four of which are patented—significantly fewer than many competitors.

You can delve into every ingredient on the brand’s website, but the headliners are marine-derived hydrolyzed collagen peptides and sodium hyaluronate to support skin and joints; algae-derived astaxanthin for antioxidant protection; selenium for immune function; and a patented black pepper extract to improve the bioavailability of the other ingredients.

Recent findings suggest that “Ultimately, the best supplements aren’t about including everything, but about choosing well-dosed, bioavailable ingredients that genuinely deliver,” says co-founder Philippa May. “And most importantly, consistency always wins. One supplement you take daily will always beat the supplement stack you forget.”.

Sources indicate that this is another one I found easy to stick to. The slightly sweet, green taste is peculiar but not unpleasant, and after finishing my first package, I saw real improvements in my bloating and digestion, plus steadier energy levels.

Inside the Upcoming La Perla

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1292 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, la Perla’s comeback story isn’t a nostalgia play.
  • According to recent reports, “I want to do the best new lingerie ever.
  • Vannetti, who became CEO of La Perla on September 1, is bullish on the lingerie brand’s prospects.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, la Perla’s comeback story isn’t a nostalgia play. CEO Alessio Vannetti recognizes that while people love vintage La Perla robes and bras, and past iconic brand moments like Halle Berry’s orange bikini in Die Another Day and Margot Robbie’s silk camisole in The Wolf of Wall Street, he’s on a mission to make modern-day La Perla just as famous.

According to recent reports, “I want to do the best new lingerie ever. I want new generations looking at La Perla, not just for the vintage. I want the new generations purchasing totally brand new styles,” Vannetti says, speaking over Zoom from the brand’s Bologna, Italy, headquarters. “I think creativity should always lead.”.

Vannetti, who became CEO of La Perla on September 1, is bullish on the lingerie brand’s prospects. Introduced in 1954 by Ada Masotti, the brand became synonymous with luxury lingerie and was known for its handcrafted lacework, made by artisans in Bologna. By the 2010s, however, focus drifted as management changed hands. In 2023, La Perla was declared insolvent, and its factory went dormant. But its lace-trimmed lore lived on in pop culture: in the past few years, the brand got mentions in episodes of Emily in Paris and The Gentlemen, and Rosalía released a song called “La Perla” on her album Lux.

Industry observers note that in 2025, La Perla was purchased by a white knight investor: entrepreneur and former Expedia CEO Peter Kern and his wife Kirsten swooped in to purchase the brand, its atelier and its former factory. They rehired all the artisans, and put a strategy in place to bring La Perla back. That led to the hiring of Vannetti –– who has spent his career in brand and communications roles at houses like Gucci, Valentino, Zegna and Prada –– and a return to Milan Fashion Week with Collection #00 in September.

A new swimsuit collection will be shown later this month, to be available just in time for next summer. And La Perla’s e-commerce site is up and running, while Vannetti is scoping out revived wholesale partnerships with department stores and specialty boutiques, as well as potential store locations in the US, a top-priority market.

“Everything is fresh, and at the same time, everything is about reclaiming our original positioning,” claims Vannetti. “How many times can you say that you are running a kind of startup, but with a brand equity as big as La Perla’s?

Where did La Perla go wrong? In part, Vannetti says, the manufacturer had pushed the brand to move faster than a high-luxury lingerie brand should. “My ambition is to create a profitable company, growing at the right speed, without compromising on quality or innovation,” says Vannetti. “In the first interview Ada Masotti gave when she founded the brand, she said that La Perla does not compromise on these two points. This is exactly what we are doing.”.

Expansion at all costs is where compromise tends to happen. The brand is taking a slow approach: opening in new markets and with retail partners in order to contain that. Because lingerie is such a personal garment, he states, customers will immediately clock when the quality has gone down. “And they stop purchasing,” he says. “This is what happened in the past.”.

It has been revealed that la Perla’s production quality, after all, is its competitive edge. When the Kerns bought the organization, they also bought the atelier and the factory, reviving the technique that Masotti created, on machines specific to La Perla. “She modified the machines in order to get a different stitch, and those modified machines are what have been preserved today,” Vannetti states. To keep that savoir-faire part of the brand’s secret sauce, La Perla will launch an academy in Bologna, where workers will train a new generation of sewers on techniques like frastaglio (where lace is inlaid on delicate silk or tulle) and macramé, as well as to maintain the machines should they need repair.

“We are not a public company, so we can really go at our speed, and our speed is not going to be extremely fast. It’s going to be La Perla speed,” Vannetti states. The brand has already designated the number of pieces it will produce for the next year, and it won’t exceed that. (He won’t say how many.) “I am 100% sure that by July, we will have the temptation. And that is the moment where I have to say, ‘OK, let’s stick to the plan.’ Because if you stick to the plan, and you build a brand on solid foundations, that’s where you’re healthy.”.

It has been revealed that until then, the brand will test demand via its e-commerce store. Over the summer, the brand invited more than 200,000 former clients to shop the new collection on a private e-commerce platform ahead of the full dot-com relaunch in October. Bras started selling out, and Vannetti notes a brand might be tempted to refill stock to capture sales that would otherwise go unfulfilled by switching production to a shorter-lead model — three weeks, say, rather than La Perla’s typical three months.

The brand is also testing the waters via one retail partnership with Harrods. The brand hosted a trunk show at Harrods for 19 clients — “the revenue generated was astonishing,” Vannetti indicates, though, again, he won’t disclose any figures as it’s too soon after a three-year shutdown. Now, he says, Harrods is pushing the brand to reopen its concession with the store. “We are running after that; we are trying to be as fast as we can, but that is the power of a desirable brand — the feeling that clients are missing it.”.

Stores are also part of the strategic plan, though Vannetti says it will only open in specific markets, starting with Newly introduced York and Los Angeles. The brand once had 135 stores at its peak. “We will never be in that situation again.”.

Industry observers note that while the history of the brand is paramount to this newly introduced phase, Vannetti is adamant the future of La Perla is not steeped in its past. “We all want to stay away from nostalgia,” he notes. “When memories become nostalgia, there is the feeling that you cannot create new memories.”.

What will the upcoming cultural touchpoints for La Perla be? Vannetti states he is in conversations with Hollywood stylists and studios to get celebrities wearing La Perla or to have La Perla mentioned in more indicates à la Emily in Paris. He’s also considering collaborations with other brands or designers if it feels right. Newness is part of the blueprint: in the next year, 60% of revenue will come from the brand’s icons, or recurring pieces, while 35% will be from new or one-off products.

The brand is also benefiting from the halo effect of the bra trend that dominated runways during the Spring/Summer 2027 season, perfectly in sync with its return. “Our mantra is inside by tradition, outside by choice, which is basically saying that we don’t want to and we will never become a ready-to-wear brand. But today, the bra is becoming the upcoming top.”.

But don’t expect La Perla to fully embrace ready-to-wear. That’s another wrong step past ownership took, Vannetti notes. “They went in the direction of trying to aggressively become a ready-to-wear brand.” It worked best when it partnered with designers like Jean-Paul Gaultier or Dell’Acqua. “Those two moments were very good examples of how to preserve the brand identity. When they tried to expand to many different categories, it didn’t work. I really just want to do the best lingerie ever. It’s kind of the art of lingerie, the way we are approaching the future.”.

Industry News: Robert Pattinson Is the James Bond Millennials Deserve

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The news is finally out: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond.
  • For the last few weeks, I’ve watched the rolling news coverage of the casting process with trepidation, because the concept of a machismo-fueled, womanizing killing machine feels tired and outdated in 2026.
  • Sources indicate that from the beginning, Pattinson, who first emerged as a teen icon in the Twilight movies, has represented a counter-argument to traditional, protein-based masculinity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The news is finally out: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond. After weeks of speculation and an almost algorithmic audition process that played out on our social feeds, Pattinson has triumphed over a list of peers that reportedly included Nicholas Hoult, Callum Turner, and Josh O’Connor.

For the last few weeks, I’ve watched the rolling news coverage of the casting process with trepidation, because the concept of a machismo-fueled, womanizing killing machine feels tired and outdated in 2026. But that’s exactly why the choice of Pattinson made me breathe a sigh of relief. Since breaking out in the 2000s,Pattinson’s career has been defined by his willingness to subvert traditional masculine archetypes, crafting them instead into slightly twisted leading-man roles. From his starring role in 2022’s The Batman to the 2026 rom-com The Drama and most recently the disturbing Oscar-tipped biopic Primetime, he has often looked for ways to subvert our expectations of the classic leading man. If there’s one actor who just might be able to make 007 feel aspirational and relevant again, it’s him.

Sources indicate that from the beginning, Pattinson, who first emerged as a teen icon in the Twilight movies, has represented a counter-argument to traditional, protein-based masculinity. “Team Edward” and “Team Jacob,” the franchise’s central romantic rivalry (and marketing ploy), offered two very different visions of male desirability. Jacob, played by Taylor Lautner, was part man, part wolf, and was muscular, physically imposing, and (thankfully) almost always shirtless, which today draws more of a visual parallel with the sort of hypermasculinity that has flourished in online gym-bro culture and the so-called “manosphere.” And then there was Edward, Pattinson’s pale, brooding vampire who was more sensitive and emotionally tortured. With the selection of a newly introduced Bond, it feels like we’re once again seeing this masculine power struggle play out—and again, it’s Pattinson who has come out on top.

According to recent reports, in the packed field of chiseled, handsome, talented actors who were vying for this role, whoever snagged it was always going to have his work cut out. As an archetype, 007 is a relic of generations gone by. The flashy gadgets, the signature martini, the expensive cars, and the ability to charm almost any woman belong to a very particular, nostalgic vision of masculinity. Through a more contemporary lens, Bond is the ultimate masculine drag act: an exaggerated, prop-heavy performance that is just as likely to be viewed as regressive and cliché.

In a recent development, we see the same trend in Bond’s dwindling romantic appeal. In our grandparents’ generation, when the character was at peak aspiration, a man arriving in a nice suit, carrying flowers, and driving a flashy car was considered a catch. But today, the dynamics have changed. I recently read The Project, the debut novel by British Vogue columnist Annie Lord, where she makes the observation that many of the most common dating “icks” now stem from men trying too hard: putting themselves out there too much, making an overt display of their interest, or seeming too confident. Lord notes that we’ve become accustomed to viewing these qualities as undesirable or embarrassing, which draws clear parallels with Bond, whose entire appeal has rested on this sort of performance. The spy’s extravagance and his carefully cultivated image were once what made him attractive, but can you imagine going on a date with a guy who seriously asks for his martini to be “shaken, not stirred”? You’d probably tell your group chat about it and endlessly mock him.

Looking more widely, there is also the question of whether the Bond franchise’s particular type of escapism can still work in the fraught world we’re currently living in. The franchise once offered a fantastical vision of evil, with megalomaniacs plotting world domination in ways that felt almost comically removed from reality. (Remember Bond’s “invisible” car in 2002’s Die Another Day?) But now, the real world feels uncomfortably close to that fantasy. Billionaires wield the kind of influence once reserved for nation-states, and the increasingly overt relationship between money and power makes it harder to distinguish the Bond villain caricature from what we’re encountering in day-to-day life.

Industry observers note that part of the reason Pattinson landed this role, I suspect, is that he already has experience in navigating nostalgic expectations and present-day anxieties. In The Batman, for example, he proved his ability to bring fresh dimensions to an old-school character with his tortured take on Bruce Wayne. And as a versatile actor who can move between action blockbusters, rom-coms, and critically acclaimed projects like Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, he has the star power and the credibility to give Bond a millennial makeover.

It’s worth saying that during Daniel Craig’s tenure as Bond, considerable effort was made to turn Bond into a deeper, more considered character. Craig’s films explored Bond’s childhood trauma and alcohol dependence, and they also introduced female characters who were more than just a sidekick or a throwaway romantic interest. But in the five years since Craig departed, a loud and unrepentant misogyny has taken hold in corners of the internet. And from the Epstein files to the Cornell University rape allegations and, most recently, the conviction of Russell Brand, so many stories come back to the central glitch of toxic masculinity.

Recent findings suggest that the wider conversation about male behavior has made casting the next Bond feel strangely high-stakes, which is probably why every screen test seemed to be leaked and endlessly dissected online. And it’s also why I’m relieved that they’ve picked an actor who might be able to make Bond a little more strange. Pattinson presents the opportunity to take Bond in a different direction—one that finally frees the character from the fantasies of the past.

Recent findings suggest that first came an Alexander McQueen dress, its paisley print drawing on the textile traditions of India and Persia, followed by a pink-and-pistachio tunic dress by Mumbai-based designer Anita Dongre, worn to play cricket at the Oval Maidan with children supported by local charities. Catherine, the Princess of Wales, at the Oval Maidan in Mumbai, 2016.

The annual Earthshot Prize gives £1 million ($1.3 million) each to five winners tackling some of the world’s most pressing environmental problems, and India has produced more finalists than any other country since its founding in 2020. It will be Catherine’s first appearance at the event since Boston in 2022, while the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards should provide familiar territory for the princess, whose charitable work has long focused on the next generation.

Sources indicate that beyond the prizes, though, the Prince and Princess will undertake a series of engagements across Mumbai (and Upcoming Delhi), highlighting the cultural ties between Britain and India, including cricket, film, and, of course, fashion. Industry observers note that if there’s one Bond girl who has influenced the course of 007 history more than anyone, it’s Dr. Madeleine Swann. Played by French actor Léa Seydoux, who is this month’s ELLE UK cover star, psychotherapist Dr. Swann disrupts the James Bond narrative in a way that no previous lover has done: She challenges his misogyny.

Appearing in the last two films in the series—Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021)—Dr. Swann has a long-term relationship with secret agent 007, eventually telling him that he’s the father of her daughter, making Seydoux’s part in the legendary franchise unique.

According to recent reports, asked whether she would consider a return to the franchise, now under the creative direction of Amazon MGM Studios and without Daniel Craig as 007, the actor mentioned: “I really loved working with Barbara Broccoli and her brother Michael [G. Wilson]. It was one of the best experiences, a pure delight. And I don’t know, it will be different.”.

Recent findings suggest that she has already worked with Denis Villeneuve, the director attached to the next Bond film, in Dune: Part Two. “He’s a great choice, let’s see. I’m curious how they will reinvent it. But for me, it will never be the same because it was Barbara’s father who initiated the Bond movies. Now, I don’t know,” she told ELLE. “It became American….I hope they will keep the British spirit.”.

Recent findings suggest that as for casting Seydoux in the role, former Bond producer Barbara Broccoli said that her scenes in No Time to Die still move her to tears. “When we were filming the goodbye scene at the Italian train station, Léa approached it with such subtlety—she grasped her stomach to express her pain, but also the secret heartbreak that she was carrying James’s child. It moved me to tears then and continues to move me each time I watch it.”.

As for the question of who will play Bond, she won’t be drawn into the speculation. (This was before Robert Pattinson was announced to take on the mantle on November 16.) Seydoux admits that finding the right person to replace Daniel Craig is difficult. “He needs to be layered, you know? And that is something that’s hard to find in young actors.”.

Léa Seydoux appears next in Gentle Monster, which begins streaming on Netflix on November 18.

Lily James shimmied into the Governors Awards in a sparkly silver flapper-style Tamara Ralph dress that dripped with crystal fringe. Silver was a big theme at the event’s starry red carpet, and yet the Rebecca star’s gown stood out for its lively silhouette.

After the Oscars were handed out—honorees includes Glenn Close, Ridley Scott, and Floyd Norman—and the champagne was popped, attendees headed out to the official after-party, held in Los Angeles’s historic Chateau Marmont.

For the occasion, James performed a quick change, trading her electric gown for something a little more subtle (but just as hot): a little black dress.

According to recent reports, the mini had a little bow up top, and was layered under an oversize leather blazer for a cool touch. James slipped her legs into sheer black tights and dipped her toes into a pair of Miu Miu’s strappy patent-leather slingbacks with tiny buckles.

She shaded her eyes with skinny black sunglasses, while another Miu Miu staple—the mini Arcadie bag in cherry-red crocodile-embossed calfskin—infused the monochrome look with a welcome pop of color.

In a recent development, another great part of her look? Her arm candy, beau Lucas Bravo, who was stylish in his own all-black outfit. A classic black T-shirt was layered under a zip-up hoodie and paired with loose trousers. Brown leather loafers broke up the inky color scheme, while chunky black sunglasses with red-orange lenses mirrored James’s pop of red.

The actors began dating just this summer, but as they’re already coordinating looks, we’ll bet the romance is going well.

Latest Update: Prince William and Kate Middleton’s Full Relationship Timeline

📅 30 Jan 2023 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
