  • The last few years have seen a lot of enormous changes in the British Royal Family, an entity known more for tradition than rapid growth.
  • William and Kate have had what appears on the outside to be a bit of a fairytale romance, from the storybook wedding to the picturesque family of five they have now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

The last few years have seen a lot of enormous changes in the British Royal Family, an entity known more for tradition than rapid growth. After the loss of Queen Elizabeth II, who ruled over the U.K. for most of the 21st century, some people may be looking for some stability. If there’s any couple in the family who offers that, it’s Prince William and Kate Middleton.

William and Kate have had what appears on the outside to be a bit of a fairytale romance, from the storybook wedding to the picturesque family of five they have now. While they’ve faced hard times like everyone else, there’s something about them that has captivated people since the beginning of their relationship. Here’s a look back at their journey, from college sweethearts to royal power couple.

Recent findings suggest that prince William and Kate Middleton met while both studying at St. Andrews University in Scotland. Rumor has it that William was won over after seeing Kate modeling at a student fashion show for charity (a show for which he reportedly paid £200 for a front-row seat).

In a recent development, other rumors suggest that her reason for being at St. Andrews was entirely related to meeting her future husband.

The Crown historian Robert Lacey wrote in his 2020 book Battle of Brothers: William and Harry—The Inside Story of a Family in Tumult, that Kate was trying to manifest her future relationship with William when she was only 19.

“Kate was very strategic,” Lacey remarked. “She gave up her place at one of Britain’s premier universities, Edinburgh, and opted for another one [St. Andrews] that probably didn’t have the same academic standard. She had already been to Edinburgh to get her flat accommodations sorted out but switched universities and switched her courses to history of art because that was William’s. She delayed her own education by a year and even takes the chance she won’t get into St. Andrews.”.

She was not the only person making these choices. Applications to the school reportedly went up by 44 percent after it was confirmed that was William’s choice of university. They might not all have been marriage hopefuls, but some probably were like Kate.

According to recent reports, hello! magazine reported that Prince William was moving from his dorm into a flat with three college friends, one of them “a pretty 20-year-old brunette” who turned out to be Kate Middleton.

He allegedly started out as just her friend, before seeing her walk in a fashion show in this see-through dress on March 26, 2002.

“She’s there and about to walk down the runway on the fashion show, and she strips off an extra layer of clothing,” Lacey explained. “Here is a very strategic lady who knows what she wants and has got it.”.

Recent findings suggest that william and Kate were photographed together for the first time during a ski trip in Klosters, causing then-Prince Charles to threaten to sever ties with The Sun, the outlet that published the photos. Charles was mentioned to have been “very disappointed” by the breach in an agreement between the press and Buckingham Palace that ensures royal children can continue their education without having their privacy intruded upon.

Both William and Kate graduated from St. Andrews. The Middletons later shared a photo of them together on the day.

It has been revealed that the couple attended Camilla’s daughter Laura Parker-Bowles’ wedding, marking one of their first big public appearances together. It also sparked speculation that they were serious enough to one day walk down the aisle themselves.

In 2007, William and Kate took a time-out and broke up for a couple of months. Kate took a vacation to Ireland with her friends afterwards, while William awkwardly fielded questions about “how things are going” with Kate.

Kate later stated in a 2010 interview after their engagement that in hindsight, she thinks it was healthy for them to have time apart.

“I think I at the time wasn't very happy about it, but actually it made me a stronger person...You find out things about yourself that maybe you hadn’t realized,” she noted. “Or I think you can get quite consumed by a relationship when you’re younger. I really valued that time for me as well although I didn't think it at the time, looking back on it.".

By July of that same year, rumors began to swirl about a possible reconciliation as Kate was seen attending a Princess Diana tribute concert—though she sat two rows behind William with her sister, Pippa.

The two were seen together again, back where it all began: the ski slopes. Photos show Kate and William together in Klosters as sources told newspapers that they were very much back together.

William graduated from his RAF training, with Kate at his side.

William proposed to Kate while on a trip to Kenya, with Princess Diana’s sapphire engagement ring. “We had a little private time away together with some friends, and I just decided it was the right time really,” William later noted in their engagement interview. “We’d been talking about marriage or a while, so it wasn’t a massively massive surprise, but I took her up somewhere nice in Kenya.”.

Industry observers note that william and Kate got married in a fairytale ceremony at Westminster Abbey witnessed by nearly 72 million people worldwide. The bride did her own makeup, the groom wore sweat pads so that he wouldn’t sweat out of his uniform, and Ellie Goulding performed at the reception.

In marrying William, Kate gained the title the Duchess of Cambridge, the Countess of Strathearn, and Lady Carrickfergus.

After the wedding, the married couple settled in Wales and adopted a dog, an English cocker spaniel named Lupo.

It has been revealed that st. James’ Palace announced that Kate was pregnant with the couple’s first child. During her pregnancy, she was hospitalized for hyperemesis gravidarum, or severe morning sickness.

Kate gave birth to Prince George on July 22 and stepped out for post-baby photos.

Recent findings suggest that kensington Palace announced that Kate was pregnant with her and William’s second child. Kate had not reached the 12-week stage, but the Palace made the announcement because they felt they couldn’t keep the pregnancy under wraps from the press for much longer. Once again, Kate suffered from extreme morning sickness.

According to recent reports, kate gave birth to Princess Charlotte on May 2, who was then fourth in line for the throne after Charles, William, and her older brother, Prince George. She was also the first to take up the title of princess in 25 years. She is the highest-ranking female in line for the throne.

Industry observers note that the couple made their red carpet debut at the British Academy Film Awards on February 12, where Prince William presented a BAFTA Fellowship award to Mel Brooks. Kate wore an off-the-shoulder tiered Alexander McQueen gown in a floral print.

In a recent development, kensington Palace announced that Kate was pregnant with the couple’s third child. As with her previous two pregnancies, she suffered from hyperemesis gravidarum.

Industry observers note that kate gave birth to Prince Louis on April 23, who was then fifth in line for the throne. Though tradition dictated that Louis, as a male, would overtake Princess Charlotte for a place on the throne, the policy was amended prior to George’s birth with the Succession to the Crown Act 2013. That made Charlotte the first female royal to trump a younger male sibling.

Kate and William were front and center at the marriage of his little brother, Prince Harry, to Meghan Markle on May 19.

According to recent reports, the couple helped Harry and Meghan celebrate on their wedding day at their nuptials at St. George’s Chapel in Windsor, England. “William was in a jokey, wonderful mood at the party,” a wedding guest told People at the time, adding that Kate was also in “great form.”.

They added, “She and William were saying how thrilled they were to have their children there taking part.”.

At Princess Eugenie’s October 12 wedding, Kate and William are seen showing each other a little affection. Eugenie was marrying her husband, Jack Brooksbank, when the royal couple were spotted holding hands in the pew.

Kate and William tend to be hands off when out in public.

After lockdown began in the U.K., the couple spoke with the BBC in a rare joint interview, discussing what it's like to parent through a pandemic.

“It's been ups and downs, like a lot of families self-isolating,” Kate said. “The children have got such stamina, I don't know how. Honestly, you get to the end of the day and you write down the list of all the things that you've done in that day. So, you pitch a tent, take the tent down again, cook, bake. You get to the end of the day—they have had a lovely time—but it is amazing how much you can cram into one day, that’s for sure.”.

It has been revealed that nine years after welcoming their cocker spaniel, Ludo, into their lives, the couple announced they had bid him farewell. They shared a portrait of the dog on Instagram with a heartfelt goodbye.

Industry observers note that “Very sadly last weekend our dear dog, Lupo, passed away,” the post read. “He has been at the heart of our family for the past nine years, and we will miss him so much. - W & C.”.

April 29, 2021 marked the 10-year anniversary of the couple’s marriage, otherwise known as the tin anniversary. To celebrate, they shared some fresh portraits taken by Chris Floyd at Kensington Palace.

They also posted a video of themselves with their children walking through the sand dunes in Norfolk, England. They thanked everyone for the well wishes.

According to recent reports, on September 28, the couple got dressed up for the No Time to Die premiere in London, posing with William’s father and stepmother. The royal family members were guests of honor at the event.

Kate wore a Jenny Packham capelet gown covered in gold sequins.

On October 20, Kate and William enjoyed their first Earthshot Awards at Alexandra Palace in London. The environmental initiative was introduced by William, and he was tasked with giving a speech at the ceremony. A photo reveals them sharing a sweet moment together behind the scenes.

Also at the event was Emma Thompson, Emma Watson, David Oyelowo, and Mo Salah. Ed Sheeran, Shawn Mendes, KSI, and Coldplay performed.

Enjoying another fun premiere, the couple hit the May 19 red carpet for Top Gun in the U.K.

Kate wore a black Roland Mouret gown, with an off-the-shoulders, white wraparound detail.

The couple’s first official portrait was unveiled at the University of Cambridge’s Fitzwilliam Museum on June 23. Originally commissioned in 2021 by the Cambridgeshire Royal Portrait Fund, it was painted by Jamie Coreth. Coreth is an award-winning portrait artist.

The Duke and Duchess take their three children to visit the Lambrook school, where they will be newly attending. The September 7 preview day offered the family a chance to get to know the facilities and teachers.

Prince George, Princess Charlotte, and Prince Louis were all wearing their school uniforms.

It has been revealed that queen Elizabeth II died on September 8. The then-Duke and Duchess of Cambridge became the Duke and Duchess of Cornwall and of Rothesay. On September 9, William’s father conferred the title of Prince and Princess of Wales.

In his address to the nation following the news of his mother’s death, King Charles III said, “With Catherine beside him, our newly introduced Prince and Princess of Wales will, I know, continue to inspire and lead our national conversations, helping to bring the marginal to the centre ground where vital help can be given.”.

The Princess of Wales was a title once held by William’s mother, Princess Diana.

Along with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, William and Kate visited Windsor Castle to view flowers and gifts left by citizens to honor the late Queen.

The couple attended Queen Elizabeth’s funeral at Westminster Hall after escorting her coffin from Buckingham Palace.

They posted their farewells to her on Twitter with a photo of the procession.

Kate and William attended the Festival of Remembrance on November 12, a ceremony dedicated to the day the Allies and Germany signed the armistice that ended World War I in 1918 for Europe.

Later that evening at a Royal Albert Hall concert, Kate paid tribute to the late Queen by wearing some of her famous jewelry: her Japanese pearl choker necklace along with her Bahrain diamond and pearl drop earrings.

It has been revealed that harry and Meghan’s docuseries was released on Netflix. It was reported that Kate and William refused to watch it.

Vanity Fair wrote, “While aides will be watching the series closely, along with the royals’ lawyers, the palace are reluctant to comment on the show because they don’t want to feed what has become a media frenzy.”.

According to recent reports, after the docuseries, Kate and William were hit with another wave of bad publicity when Harry’s memoir Spare was released. A source who knows both couples told Entertainment Tonight in a report published January 12 that “[their] relationship has completely broken down.”.

A separate source said Kate felt “hurt and disappointed” over what Harry shared about her in Spare because she believed “private matters had been made public.”.

Kate and William marked British Mother’s Day on their Instagram, sharing newly introduced photos of Kate with the couple’s three children. “Happy Mother’s Day from our family to yours ❤️,” they wrote.

The couple celebrated their 12-year anniversary with a photo on Instagram in which they’re sitting on matching bikes.

“12 years ❤️,” they captioned their post.

In an interview with ELLE, Endgame author Omid Scobie debunked past tabloid reports that Kate and William were having trouble in their marriage. “I think partly, rumors take on a life of their own online, and so there will be a bigger hunger for things that aren’t even true about someone,” he stated. “I think William and Kate have largely been protected from that with the British tabloids who often do lean on these very lazy rumor spreading and whatnot. But with Kate and William, particularly with their great relationships with a lot of the vital newspaper editors and publishers, they managed to be kept out of that.”.

It has been revealed that “But of course, there is no control over things in the U.S., and we have seen them become fodder for a lot of the supermarket tabloids for stories about their marriage being in trouble and all the rest of it,” he continued. “I’m not here to comment on someone’s marriage. I can only go by what I have heard from people that are much closer to the situation that I’d imagined a source for InTouch magazine is. I’ve not heard anything about a marriage being in trouble.”.

“I’m always very careful with that stuff as well,” he noted. “Just as much as I will disregard that story, I’ll also disregard the stories of Harry and Meghan's marriage being in trouble. I think it’s very lazy tabloid journalism at times because you can’t make money off people just being happy all the time. You need them to be in crisis for their lives to be more interesting, and I think sometimes two people can just be in a very safe and perhaps slightly dull marriage and that’s okay.”.

As they do every year, the Prince and Princess of Wales shared a family portrait for the Christmas holiday.

Industry observers note that in the black-and-white photo by Josh Shinner, the family is dressed casually in matching button-up shirts, pants, or jeans. The two youngest children have on black sneakers with white toes. Charlotte is seated in front, her parents behind her, and her brothers standing on either side.

On Thursday, January 18, Prince William was photographed driving away from the London Clinic in a black BMW following Kate’s abdominal surgery.

The planned operation was revealed on the couple’s Instagram.

According to recent reports, “The surgery was successful, and it is expected that she will remain in hospital for 10 to 14 days, before returning home to continue her recovery,” the Palace shared on Instagram. They added that the Princess of Wales was “unlikely to return to public duties until after Easter.”.

They explained that only “significant” updates on her condition will be shared with the public in order to “maintain as much normality for her children as possible.”.

According to recent reports, “The Princess of Wales wishes to apologize to all those concerned for the fact that she has to postpone her upcoming engagements,” the statement concluded. “She looks forward to reinstating as many as possible, as soon as possible.”.

According to recent reports, on January 29, Kate was released from the hospital. It was unveiled she would return to official royal duties after Easter on March 31.

Recent findings suggest that on March 10, 2024, Kensington Palace celebrated U.K. Mother’s Day with a photo of Kate and her three children. The picture was attributed to William. In the caption, a message from the princess remarked, “Thank you for your kind wishes and continued support over the last two months. Wishing everyone a Happy Mother’s Day. C.”.

Recent findings suggest that followers noted some obvious Photoshop edits in the picture, causing a bit of controversy around the image. This was exacerbated when several news agencies, including The Associated Press, pulled the photo over image manipulation.

Kate then added to her message, admitting to editing the picture herself in a post on X.

“Like many amateur photographers, I do occasionally experiment with editing,” she claimed. “I wanted to express my apologies for any confusion the family photograph we shared yesterday caused. I hope everyone celebrating had a very happy Mother’s Day. C.”.

A source told Entertainment Tonight that the princess “wanted to be transparent,” adding that “the intention with the photo was to thank the public for their support during her recovery and provide a lovely picture of the children.”.

On March 22, the Princess of Wales shared a video explaining that she has been diagnosed with cancer following her abdominal surgery and is undergoing treatment.

“This of course came as a huge shock, and William and I have been doing everything we can to process and manage this privately for the sake of our young family,” she mentioned. “As you can imagine, this has taken time. It has taken me time to recover from major surgery in order to start my treatment.”.

The next day, the couple released another statement to thank people for their support. They said in their message, “The Prince and Princess are both enormously touched by the kind messages from people here in the U.K., across the Commonwealth and around the world in response to Her Royal Highness’s message. They are extremely moved by the public’s warmth and support and are grateful for the understanding of their request for privacy at this time.”.

Kate did not make an appearance at Easter services at St. George’s Chapel at Windsor Castle. According to People, she spent the holiday with her family at home.

The couple celebrated their 13th wedding anniversary in private. They publicly shared a previously unreleased photo from their nuptials to mark the occasion. “13 years ago today!” they wrote on April 29.

Recent findings suggest that on June 13, Kate shared an update on her treatment and recovery on Instagram, assuring her fans that she is seeing an improvement. She also shared a photo taken by Matt Porteous.

Then, she made a public appearance at Trooping the Color with William and all three of her children.

In a recent development, on June 21, Kate shared a rare message to Prince William in honor of his 42nd birthday. “Happy birthday Papa, we all love you so much! Cx,” she wrote on their Instagram alongside a photo she took of him with their three children.

Kate attended Sunday service at Crathie Kirk, marking a rare public sighting. For the occasion, Kate wore a checkered brown coat from Holland Cooper, accessorizing with a brown fedora hat adorned with orange and brown feathers. She let her brunette hair flow freely and finished off her look with a pair of gold earrings. See photos here.

Besides her immediate family, Kate was also joined by King Charles and Queen Camilla, as well as the Duke and Duchess of Edinburgh, James, Earl of Wessex, and Sir Tim Laurence.

On September 9, Kate Middleton shared news on Instagram that she had completed her chemotherapy treatment.

“Doing what I can to stay cancer free is now my focus,” she wrote. “Although I have finished chemotherapy, my path to healing and full recovery is long.”.

Recent findings suggest that she continued, “Life as you know it can change in an instant and we have had to find a way to navigate the stormy waters and road unknown. The cancer journey is complex, scary and unpredictable for everyone, especially those closest to you. With humility, it also brings you face to face with your own vulnerabilities in a way you have never considered before, and with that, a fresh perspective on everything. This time has above all reminded William and me to reflect and be grateful for the simple yet notable things in life, which so many of us often take for granted. Of simply loving and being loved.”.

According to recent reports, on Sunday, September 22, Kate and William appeared in photos published by The Sun, heading to Sunday service near the Balmoral estate in Crathie. It was one of her first public outings since she announced the end of her chemotherapy treatment. Both King Charles and Queen Camilla were also seen heading to the service together.

On November 7, during the last day of his Cape Town visit, Prince William opened up about how Kate and Charles’s cancer diagnoses affected him.

Industry observers note that “It’s been dreadful. It’s probably been the hardest year in my life,” the Prince of Wales stated, per People. “So, trying to get through everything else and keep everything on track has been really difficult...But I’m so proud of my wife, I’m proud of my father, for handling the things that they have done. But from a personal family point of view, it’s been, yeah, it’s been brutal.”.

After being asked about the Princess of Wales, William stated she is “doing well.”.

He was told he looked relaxed by a reporter. William responded, “I couldn’t be less relaxed this year, so it’s very interesting you’re all seeing that...But it’s more a case of just crack on and you’ve got to keep going. I enjoy my work and I enjoy pacing myself and keeping sure that I have got time for my family, too.”.

In a recent development, on November 9, Kate joined William at the annual Festival of Remembrance at the Royal Albert Hall, marking her fourth official outing of the year. For the event, the Princess of Wales wore a black wrap dress with long sleeves and a V-neckline, a Nura pearl necklace from the Monica Vinader collection, and a pair of pearl and diamond drop earrings from Collingwood that once belonged to the late Princess Diana.

She had on semi-sheer black stockings, black pumps, and wore a red poppy pin in her lapel to honor veterans and fallen soldiers.

On Thanksgiving weekend, a source told People that the couple is planning their first Christmas together with King Charles at Sandringham in Norfolk.

As expected, the whole family attended the Together at Christmas carol service on December 6.

On December 19, Kate and William shared their 2024 holiday card, featuring a photo of them together. They wrote, “Wishing you a very Happy Christmas and Latest Year.”.

For Kate’s birthday on January 9, William wrote a tribute that he shared on the couple’s joint Instagram. “To the most incredible wife and mother. The strength you’ve shown over the last year has been remarkable,” he stated. “George, Charlotte, Louis and I are so proud of you. Happy Birthday, Catherine. We love you. W.”.

According to recent reports, the couple made an appearance at Meadow Street Community Garden and Woodland on February 26 in Pontypridd, Wales, after the area was hit with severe flooding when Storm Bert and Storm Darragh came through in December 2024. The Prince and Princess met with residents to discuss recovery efforts and the issues they’ve faced since the storms.

On March 10, Kate wore a brilliant red coat and matching hat to celebrations for Commonwealth Day at Westminster Abbey, with William by her side in blue.

Sources indicate that on March 15, the Prince and Princess of Wales headed to Cardiff, Wales, for the Wales vs. England rugby match at Principality Stadium. William is patron of the Welsh Rugby Union, while Kate supports the Rugby Football Union, creating a friendly rivalry. The pair came together, however, to meet with injured players supported by the Welsh Rugby Charitable Trust at Sir Tasker Watkins Suite.

They both wore long navy coats to the game over seemingly coordinated dark ensembles.

In a recent development, on July 8, Kate and William took part in the welcome ceremony for French President Emmanuel Macron and First Lady Brigitte Macron’s state visit, joining King Charles and Queen Camilla at Windsor Castle. The couple shared a few romantic moments during the event. In one photo, Kate was seen smiling as she placed her arm around William’s waist.

Later, William offered his hand to guide her down the royal dais steps.

That evening, the Prince and Princess of Wales stepped out for a state banquet at St. George’s Hall, where they were photographed exchanging smiles while arriving in formal attire.

A rep speaking with Us Weekly on August 16 confirmed the couple’s prepares to move houses. They currently reside in Adelaide Cottage in Windsor Home Park, close to Windsor Castle.

“The Wales family will move house later this year,” remarked a spokesperson for Kensington Palace.

As Kate continued her gradual return to public life following her cancer remission, People gave an update on her dynamic with William. Those close to the couple said that the challenges of the past year have strengthened their bond.

“What they have been through over the last few years has been so terrible,” royal historian Amanda Foreman told the outlet. “That either drives couples apart, or, in their case, it brings them together. It irons out the kinks and enables them to see each other clearly.”.

Kate and William traveled to Mumbai for the annual Earthshot Prize Awards.

The Prince and Princess of Wales began their visit with a stop at Mumbai’s Ballard Estate, where they met cricket stars Sachin Tendulkar and Poonam Raut and played street cricket together.

Following their arrival, William shared a message about the trip.

Recent findings suggest that “Catherine and I are delighted to be in India for this year’s Earthshot Prize,” he said. “India has made an extraordinary contribution to Earthshot over the past six years and is home to more Earthshot Finalists and Winners than any other country.”.

“It has also become one of the most exciting places in the world for environmental innovation, with people across the country developing practical solutions to some of the greatest challenges we all share.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cashmere sweaters and leather jackets may be in full rotation right now, but with snow season just a whisper away, we’ll all be swapping for puffer coats and thick socks before we know it. Usually that also means pulling out chunky boots that do more for warmth than they do for an outfit. But Gigi Hadid’s Guest in Residence and Moon Boot are here to make finding non-hideous winter boots a lot easier. Launching November 17, the two brands will release a second collaboration of five special-edition boots, each one pairing Guest in Residence’s colorful hand-knit textures with Moon Boot’s cushy soles and weatherproof materials, fully built for any chilly-day adventure—in the city or the mountains.

Industry observers note that the two brands are putting forth the notion that a snow boot can look just as good as your favorite sweater, and this round further homes in on that idea. “Each silhouette tells a story that feels nostalgic and familiar yet entirely fresh at the same time,” Hadid shares. The new styles hark back to vintage themes—think alpine motifs and old cabin textiles. The Icon Knit Postcard features a custom knit landscape of snowy pines that looks like a walk through the woods and comes in an ice and red colorway or dark brown and sand. The Nolace Fair Isle is low-profile and pairs a classic Fair Isle pattern with a fuzzy fleece texture. For something more pared back, the Icon Low Signature comes in suede with pastel laces, blue on the pale pair and pink on the brown. The Ltrack Cable Knit adds wool and alpaca cable-knit. Every style has its own playful vibe.

Hadid started Guest in Residence in 2022 and it swiftly became the place to get really good colorful cashmere sweaters. She’s also been wearing Moon Boots for years, so teaming up with the brand was a no-brainer. “We’ve brought our vibrant palettes and retro influences to Moon Boot’s futuristic silhouettes, and it’s been fun to explore new expressions of our partnership,” Hadid claims.

Recent findings suggest that and no, you don’t need to be a prolific skier to put them to use. Built on Moon Boot’s signature soles, they’re as useful on a slick sidewalk as they are on the slopes. Moon Boot itself was never strictly for the snow either. It started in 1969 as an après-ski boot inspired by what the astronauts wore on the moon. If you are venturing out to the slopes this season, Guest in Residence just released an eight-piece ski capsule with Halfdays, the label cofounded by former Olympic freestyle skier Kiley McKinnon, so you can match your boots to your bib. The line is featured within the brands’ joint campaign, shot in faux airport terminals and cabins, with all manner of cable knits, cozy thermals, and necessary footwear for a trip to the mountains.

Sources indicate that whether you’re looking for a statement shoe to complete your ski suit or a low-profile ankle boot to polish off your winter wares, there’s a pair that fits the bill in the collaboration. Prices range from $395 to $495, and the collection is available starting November 17 at Moon Boot and Guest in Residence. Vogue readers can shop the drop exclusively 24 hours before the rest on Vogue Shopping.

Like this is a real movie worthy of the fans’ respect, but there [are] a few things we need to figure out before we can get that really going. But it’s exciting and I’m really, really excited about it.”.

He added that he wants to give fans “the best version of what the next chapter for Spider-Man looks like.”.

According to recent reports, “I think that’s really vital and I think the creative integrity for something like that is really important,” he mentioned. “And the studio is on board and supportive and really collaborative, and I’ve been so blown away by how welcoming they’ve been into that creative room, but we’re working now with the pedal to the metal. We’re trying to get it going as soon as possible. Things are looking great but there’s still a lot of moving pieces that need to come together for us to hit the ground running.”.

On October 24, Zendaya joined Holland to celebrate the launch of his nonalcoholic beer brand, Bero. She wore a burgundy Louis Vuitton dress, which complemented his top. They held hands while leaving the event.

At the very end of October, Holland admitted on the podcast On The Menu, hosted by Samah Dada, that the last thing he “Googled” was his girlfriend’s name as a way of checking up on her since he left social media.

According to recent reports, dada asked about his Googling habits and Holland replied, “The last thing I Googled was actually Zendaya. I’m not on socials and I delete it when I’m not using it. So sometimes like—it’s more of a bit of an anxiety thing...I’ll check to see if everything’s good and to make sure we’re all cool. So I just give her a little Google and look through the news and I’m like, ‘she’s good.’”.

In a recent development, shortly before Thanksgiving, Holland shared several Instagram Stories from the couple’s night out at Foxhole bar in Boston. They enjoyed his nonalcoholic beer brand, Bero, which he tagged in the photos. He was sure to post several heart-eye emojis on his pic of Zendaya in the November 24 snaps.

On December 17, the Spider-Man star opened up on the Dish from Waitrose podcast, sharing his holiday looks with Zendaya.

According to recent reports, “I’m going to be in America this year,” Holland noted, when asked about Christmas. “I’ll be with my girlfriend’s family, which is fun.”.

“I think what we’d like to start doing is, rather than like spending it with each family, each year is bring the families together,” he said. “That’s what I think we want to do next time. This time, since we’re both actors, we’re terrible at organizing things, so it hasn’t happened yet.”.

He then talked about doing the cooking at home for them both.

“I’m starting to venture into a lot of vegetarian cooking,” Holland claimed. “My girlfriend’s vegetarian. So, I’ve been in Boston these past few weeks, and she’s been working, so I’ve been doing a lot of the dinners, and they haven’t been great.”.

He added, “I actually love Zendaya’s spicy vodka fusilli thingamagigy. And it is delicious.”.

The actor explained a bit more about their dynamic and how it works for them after all these years.

It has been revealed that “I think that’s where Zendaya and I have been such a strong couple, as in the spirit of being able to relate with one another on something that is very, very unique,” he shared. “And I think it’s just relying on the people around you. It’s about being a little bit more organized knowing where you want to go, and there are restaurants that have little back rooms and stuff where you can have a more private night. But at the end of the day, it’s no hardship.”.

He added, “It’s a saving grace.”.

Sources indicate that on the day of the episode’s release, the couple were spotted in a Nordstrom in pics shared by TMZ. They were dressed casually for the outing in Topanga Mall at Canoga Park and Zendaya had her dog on a leash.

Men’s Health published a upcoming interview with Holland on January 2. In the piece, the star revealed why he doesn’t walk red carpets with Zendaya during her premieres: “Because it’s not my moment, it’s her moment, and if we go together, it’s about us.”.

He also shared what he aims to do in his career once he has a family someday. “When I have kids, you will not see me in movies anymore,” he mentioned. “[It’ll just be] golf and dad. And I will just disappear off the face of the earth.”.

At the Golden Globes on January 5, Zendaya sparked rumors she and Holland could be engaged when she debuted a diamond ring on her left ring finger that wasn’t from Bulgari like her other jewelry.

Recent findings suggest that the morning after, TMZ reported that Zendaya and Holland are indeed engaged. Holland proposed “in one of Zendaya’s family homes in the United States” between Christmas and New Year’s, sources close to the couple said. It was a “very romantic” and “intimate” proposal between just them.

On January 6, she attended a special screening of Challengers wearing the ring.

A few days later, Holland’s father, Dominic, released more details about the engagement in a Patreon blog post. The English actor and author shared in his post that he knows some of the people following him are doing so to glean more details about the celebrity couple. Dominic wrote it “amuses” him, but he was happy to have something to report this time.

Sources indicate that “The significant news this week is a good example of just such an opportunity for me—are they aren’t they engaged?” he wrote. “Zendaya wearing a ring and Tom nowhere to be seen adding to the intrigue.”.

Dominic then stated that he would not be “adding anything new and juicy like a date, venue, guest list,” but he would be sharing “the different approaches of father and son to proposing marriage.”.

According to recent reports, “Tom, as you know by now was very incredibly well prepared. He had purchased a ring. He had spoken with her father and gained permission to propose to his daughter,” Dominic explained. “Tom had everything planned out… When, where, how, what to say, what to wear.”.

Dominic shared that when he proposed to his son’s mom, Nikki, it was “nothing like my eldest son who has obviously watched all the slushy movies because growing up I never saw him reading a book.”.

He added, “For most blokes, the stress of purchasing an engagement ring is being able to afford it. I suspect that this was the least of Tom’s worries, more concerned with the stone, [its] size and clarity, its housing, which jeweler.”.

The Spider-Man star’s dad mentioned how he does not “envy those who are gawped at wherever they go,” adding, “I do fret that their combined stardom will amplify their spotlight and the commensurate demands on them and yet they continually confound me by handling everything with aplomb.”.

He continued, “And even though show business is a messy place for relationships and particularly so for famous couples as they crash and burn in public and are too numerous to mention… I am completely confident they will make a successful union.”.

In an interview, Spider-Man co-star Jacob Batalon, who plays Peter Parker’s best friend Ned Leeds in the films, was jokingly asked if they’d be one another’s best man at their respective weddings.

Laughing, Batalon replied, “Maybe, you know, I really—he’s a lot to deal with, so probably not.”.

On April 8, Zendaya’s longtime stylist and creative director, Law Roach, shared that the actress and Holland are in no rush to tie the knot. Roach told E! that “of course,” he’ll be involved in dressing Zendaya on her substantial day.

According to recent reports, but “it’s far away,” he revealed to the outlet at the Fashion Trust Awards. “They’re both doing a bunch of movies this year, and there’s a lot of premieres next year so you’ll see a lot of red carpets.” He teased, “I’m resting up for 2026.”.

She had her hair down in loose curls, some tucked into her top. The pair reportedly hung out in Zendaya’s trailer for a bit before Holland headed home with the puppy.

In an interview with GQ, Holland was asked about his favorite Wimbledon looks.

“Zendaya wore that Ralph Lauren suit a couple of years ago,” he said. “She just looked so beautiful and so at home. It meant so much to me for her to be in a place that I call home and look like such a part of our community.”.

In a recent development, zendaya actually wore two Ralph Lauren suits to Wimbledon in July 2024. The first, worn on day 13, was a khaki blazer over a light blue button-down shirt with dark-wash oversize denim pants. She accessorized with a knit blue and white striped tie and large pearl earrings.

The second look, which she wore the following day, was a white blazer over a blue and white striped button-down shirt, and she topped it off with another knit blue tie.

That same month, Zendaya’s longtime stylist, Law Roach, revealed the couple is holding off on planning their wedding despite getting engaged over six months ago.

According to recent reports, “The process hasn’t even started yet,” he told E! at the Las Culturistas Culture Awards’ red carpet last month. “Zendaya is working on so many movies. She’s now filming the next iteration of Dune [Part Three in Hungary], so she’s away doing that. It’s so many movies, so we have time. The couple began production on Spider-Man: Brand New Day and were seen in London throughout August. The Marvel film was shot in Glasgow, but Holland and Zendaya recently enjoyed some downtime in London’s Richmond Park.

In some pictures, her five-carat engagement ring could be seen as she raised her hand to her face. In one photo, he appears to lean against her in a sweet moment of PDA.

Sources indicate that on September 20, the couple stepped out for a rare public appearance in support of Holland’s nonprofit, The Brothers Trust. The actor and his family hosted a fundraising event for the organization at Christie’s London auction house. Holland dressed in a classic tuxedo while Zendaya wore a black Valentino minidress with a wide ruffle detail, tights, and a pair of black pumps.

Sources indicate that holland, who was recovering from a head injury suffered on the set of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, shared a highlight reel from the gathering. “What a night! Another huge success. The Brothers Trust means more to me than I could possibly say and I have to say a huge thank you to my Mum and her wonderful friends for putting on another incredible night. Raising money for fantastic causes and having fun doing it!” he wrote. “I’m sorry I had to leave early but I’m feeling better and on the mend. A huge thanks to my Dad for taking over after I left. The show got considerably funnier 😂.”.

Shortly after, on September 29, Holland had the internet abuzz after an X user posted a clip of the actor participating in a panel discussion to promote his nonalcoholic beer brand, Bero. During the chat, the moderator referred to Zendaya as Holland’s “girlfriend,” which the husband-to-be kindly corrected, saying, “Fiancée.” The moment originally happened in April at the Beverage Forum, a gathering for executives in the beverage industry, but the full panel discussion was posted on YouTube on September 3. Zendaya and Holland made a rare public appearance at “The Traitors: Live Experience,” in London, enjoying a family game night with Tom’s parents, siblings, and close friends. Zendaya was photographed wearing a gold band on her left ring finger instead of her engagement ring on February 18, sparking questions about her relationship status with Holland. In July, her stylist, Roach, had told E! that when the pair do get married, Zendaya would be “a secret bride.”.

While I was, like, just out and about in real life, and people were like, ‘Oh my god, your wedding photos are gorgeous.’ And I was like, ‘Babe, they’re AI.’”.

Four days later on March 20, the couple was photographed holding hands in Los Angeles. The actress was in a long white skirt and long-sleeve black shirt. Holland wore a striped T-shirt and navy slacks.

In a recent development, on March 21, Holland made a rare public post on Instagram to celebrate Zendaya’s fresh film, The Drama, in which she stars with Robert Pattinson. In her ELLE summer 2026 cover story, Zendaya opened up about working alongside Holland again on Spider-Man: Brand Latest Day, as well as what it was like to watch Holland film The Odyssey. “I could have cried, I was so proud,” she noted of seeing Holland on set for the Christopher Nolan-directed film. We bring our dogs to work; it’s like a family affair. We grew up on those movies! It’s like coming home.”.

The interview also revealed that the couple recently adopted another dog together while visiting Zendaya’s hometown of Oakland. “Logistically, it wasn’t probably the smartest idea,” Zendaya noted. “But emotionally, it was. He’s a wonderful addition to our family. I saw his little face and I was like, ‘I can’t leave you behind.’”.

When asked about speculation surrounding their relationship status after she was photographed wearing a gold band on her ring finger, Zendaya declined to comment directly.

On June 15, Holland and Zendaya made their first official red carpet appearance together since 2021 at the Spider-Man: Brand Upcoming Day photo-call in Madrid.

For the event, Holland wore a black jacket and trousers layered over a bright red shirt and coordinating tie. Zendaya opted for a strapless black Christian Cowan dress featuring a dramatic fringe-trimmed skirt paired with pointed-toe pumps.

The couple shared a few affectionate moments while posing for photographers. They exchanged smiles, looked at each other, and held hands.

A day later, Esquire UK released its cover story with Holland. The actor spoke glowingly about Zendaya though, telling the outlet, “Our business can present very stressful situations and it’s really nice to have a bedrock of a relationship that will stand the test of time. We can support each other in ways that only we can, because only we understand really what it’s like to live this life, and I think that is such a luxury, because I just don’t understand how I would be able to have anything like that with anyone else. So, for me, I found my person. She’s my best friend, and I’m the happiest I ever have been when I’m with her, but I also have never felt so supported and safe, ever. Period.”.

Holland and Zendaya continued their Spider-Man: Brand Fresh Day press tour with several appearances across Europe. On June 17, they posed together at a photocall in Amsterdam. Holland wore a navy suit with a striped tie, while Zendaya paired a black high-neck top with a bright red miniskirt and white pumps.

In a recent development, later, they attended another Spider-Man: Brand Fresh Day event in the city. Holland wore a dark suit styled with a red shirt and matching tie, while Zendaya chose a black two-piece ensemble featuring a cropped top and a floor-length skirt with a dramatic train.

On June 24, Holland shared photos from the Spider-Man: Brand Fresh Day press tour stop in Rome on Instagram, captioning the post, “When in Rome! Spider-Man Brand New Day.”.

The images demonstrated him and Zendaya walking hand in hand and smiling together. For the event, Holland wore a burgundy Louis Vuitton suit with a coordinating shirt and tie, while Zendaya opted for a shimmering archival Giorgio Armani dress featuring an intricate web-inspired design. Zendaya reposted Holland’s Instagram to her own Instagram Story.

He said, “To be honest, when I got home after our meeting, I sat down with Z and was like, ‘I’ve been offered this movie.’ And she was like, ‘By who?’ And I was like, ‘It’s the massive one.’ And she was like, ‘Chris?’ I was like, ‘Yeah, it’s Chris Nolan.’”.

It has been revealed that “And then we had Spider-Man that was literally scheduled to go the same day that we would start shooting,” he continued. “Z remarked, ‘I’ll leave you if you don’t do The Odyssey.’”.

Zendaya also revealed that Holland was the one who told her Christopher Nolan wanted her to play Athena. “He was...allowed to be the one to tell me, and that was really special,” she told the Associated Press. “I was already on cloud nine. The fact that I was even got to be involved as well was like just this cherry on top.”.

At the film’s Upcoming York premiere on July 14, Zendaya told Extra that Holland’s presence helped calm her nerves on her first day of filming. “You know, some locations he wasn’t at, but he was on my first day, which I was very grateful for, because as you can imagine, something like this is quite a daunting task,” she said. “It’s the scale, the scope, it’s absolutely extraordinary. So walking onto a Chris Nolan set for the first time is no small feat, so I was happy to have some support.”.

Holland was equally enthusiastic about sharing the experience with her. “I mean, it’s awesome,” he told the outlet. “We still, to this day, cannot believe we got to go through this together and experience this epic movie on the same set, on the same days. You know, she’s fantastic in the film. She had a really tough job. I think when you see the movie and you see what she has to do, it’s really difficult, and as always, she nailed it.”.

15 Best Colognes for Men in 2026, Staff-Tested and Reviewed

📅 01 Jul 2021 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4543 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in 2026, the best colognes for men go beyond just smelling good, though first things first: They should smell incredible.
  • My work in the fragrance field has also taught me that while some guys find one signature scent and ride with it for decades; others prefer a variety for different moods, seasons, and days where first impressions matter.
  • Le Labo has no shortage of heavy hitters, from the omnipresent Santal 33 to newer standouts like Eucalyptus 20, but few recent debuts have built buzz quite like Thé Matcha 26.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in 2026, the best colognes for men go beyond just smelling good, though first things first: They should smell incredible. A great fragrance nowadays tells a story, and if you choose wisely, can become part of your personal lore. I, for one, am a fragrance obsessive and will spritz a cologne at home with nowhere to be, purely for morale. What's more, years of testing and writing about fragrances has taught me just how effortlessly a stellar composition can lift your entire day, whether it’s a mainstream designer release, a niche luxury creation, or something decidedly indie.

My work in the fragrance field has also taught me that while some guys find one signature scent and ride with it for decades; others prefer a variety for different moods, seasons, and days where first impressions matter. To help you figure out where you stand, I tapped the GQ staffers who wear more fragrance in a year than most men do in a lifetime. Collectively, we put old-money classics, cult favorites, and new heat through their atomizers, looking for scents that feel distinctive and deserve repeat wear. The final cut includes a bevy of choices for all occasions, from heritage heavyweights like Acqua di Parma Colonia to future signatures like D.S. & Durga's I Don't Know What. Here's to the sweet smell of success.

Le Labo has no shortage of heavy hitters, from the omnipresent Santal 33 to newer standouts like Eucalyptus 20, but few recent debuts have built buzz quite like Thé Matcha 26. Much of its insider appeal lies in its earthy yet fresh, smoky yet subtle, almost Zen-like character. Green fig leads the opening, paired with a calming tea accord, while bitter orange adds a bright bite. As it settles, the fragrance takes on a woodier, herbal edge, with a soft, green haze that runs throughout. A skin scent at heart and undeniably hip, it’s become a modern staple for Le Labo’s more discerning devotees.

Staff Notes: “I’ve been wearing Le Labo’s Thé Matcha for a few years now, and it has become my go-to. As someone who has a hard time finding a scent that doesn't give me a headache or feels too strong throughout the day, it’s one of those rare scents that just works. It has a clean, almost airy quality to it that immediately settles into something effortless and fresh.” —Bowen Fernie, senior visuals editor.

Malin+Goetz is one of the few names that began in skincare and went on to make genuinely excellent, indie-cool fragrances, all at very accessible prices. The apothecary vibes run deep, from the formulas to those glass deco bottles that ooze medicine-cabinet chic. The brand's Leather EDP—like my favorite from the line, Cannabis—doesn’t smell exactly like its name. In classic M+G fashion, it plays more of a supporting role here, blended with pepper and clove for a bit of kick. Lily and orchid create a fresh floral heart, while violet adds a velvety depth, all grounded by creamy sandalwood and cedar. And of course, that warm, comforting leather note wears like a Perfecto. It’s a gorgeous spring-ready daily driver, with a grassy floral vibe that plays beautifully against the grain.

Recent findings suggest that staff Notes: “From the perfect broken-in leather jacket to a leather sofa that's been with you move after move, there's something about the smell of well-loved cowhide that's so damn captivating. Malin+Goetz captured that feeling in a bottle with its Leather EDP. The cologne brings in cedarwood and sandalwood with orchid just to avoid any possibilities of your scent being compared to a vintage store.” —Tyler Chin, associate commerce editor.

Is there any cologne more synonymous with men’s cologne, period, than Polo Ralph Lauren? Since 1978, it has helped define what “classically good” smells like and sits firmly planted in the pantheon of modern perfumery. Anything that iconic will have its detractors, but it’s embedded in the culture for a reason, and few colognes today are as recognizable. Even with reformulations over the years, that signature woody aromatic structure still hits, with juniper berry and bergamot up top for brightness, coriander and a blend of herbs bringing spice, touches of florals, and leather for depth—along with that unmistakable pine accord humming throughout. Woody, aromatic, and classic, it’s a cologne guys will always rock.

Staff Notes: “Smelling good is paramount to success as a modern man. (Just ask my close personal friend Ralph Lauren.) Woody, aromatic, and a little spicy, this is a classic scent that's always on top of my dresser.” —Matthew Roberson, staff writer.

Sources indicate that it’s a household name, a modern icon, and still one of the most sophisticated yet approachable colognes you can wear pretty much anywhere. Created by Chanel’s famed nose, Jacques Polge, more than 15 years ago, Bleu de Chanel remains as singular and versatile today as ever. It opens bright with grapefruit and lemon, sharpened by a hint of fresh mint, before a heart of spicy ginger, warming nutmeg, and heady jasmine. Then comes the MVP lineup of woods: cedar, vetiver, sandalwood, patchouli, and labdanum, all working together in the citrus-spice harmony that defines this blue-hued gem. Flankers have followed, but the OG Bleu de Chanel is inimitable.

Recent findings suggest that staff Notes: “I keep a travel-sized bottle of this in my Dopp kit at all times. It's classic, great for every season, and super versatile when it comes to occasion—its citrus notes and woody base make it equally good for work dinners, poolside piña coladas, and stoking the fire outside your glamping cabin.” —Ian Burke, senior commerce editor.

Industry observers note that baccarat Rouge 540 is now an olfactory cultural landmark. You’ve absolutely smelled this socialite-signature wafting through the night, whether from the backseat of an Uber Black or across a dimly lit dinner table downtown. Some fragrances get so popular they tip into fatigue territory, but 540 earned its status for a reason. First, it comes from one of the most meticulous noses in the game. Second, the scent speaks for itself: an intoxicating, sweet floral amber, with saffron adding a subtle spice, jasmine bringing warmth, and a heavy dose of amberwood creating that signature glowing aura, all balanced by soft woods. Polarizing, yes, but anything that moves the needle tends to follow its own rhythm, and 540 is a modern classic via its own design.

It has been revealed that staff Notes: “Francis Kurkdjian's reputation-making Baccarat Rouge might not be the buzziest scent on the market anymore, but it's definitely the ritziest. If you don't want to smell like a perpetually fapitzed Upper East Side doyenne, you, friend, should reconsider a lot more than just your scent profile.” — Avidan Grossman, senior commerce editor.

YSL has no shortage of effortlessly elegant colognes, from more mainstream, accessible options to elevated releases in the Le Vestiaire Des Parfums collection, all infused with that unmistakable YSL panache. On paper, Trench reads as a citrus floral, but in wear, it’s laced with soft, musky undertones that give it an airy, slightly edgy feel. It opens with tangerine and bergamot, layered over heady iris and fresh neroli, before settling into a warm base of musk and cedar. A fig note threads through it all, adding a subtly sweet, verdant hue. Citrusy and floral but grounded in musk, with a slightly funky undertone (the good kind), it’s a chic fragrance you can wear from sun-soaked afternoons in the park straight into date night and out into the cool, tastefully debaucherous night beyond.

Staff Notes: “If you were to bottle the feeling of a perfect Parisian night, it would smell like YSL Trench: heady, sleek, and just a little dangerous.” —Tyler Sparling, contributing market editor.

In a recent development, eau de Minthé is one of the more distinctive entries in Diptyque’s GOAT-level catalog, a cooling blend of mint and patchouli that reads as a fresh, green fougère with a retro ’80s and ’90s edge, albeit very au courant. The mint is fresh and slightly spicy, far from anything toothpaste-adjacent, layered with warm nutmeg, sweet geranium, and a soft, velvety rose. It’s a cologne I wouldn’t have immediately associated with the house, until the drydown, anchored by that signature Diptyque patchouli, brings depth and candle-flickering craftsmanship the brand does so uniquely well. Fresh, aromatic, and with a bit of nostalgia baked in, this is a layered gem to wear for all your mint julep-fueled warm-weather soirées.

Sources indicate that staff Notes: "Diptyque's Eau de Minthé is what I imagine Michelin-level mixologists aspire toward when they're crafting their cocktails. At first sniff, it's garden-fresh floral notes are uplifted with subtle minty notes before settling into deep patchouli notes that give it a well-rounded experience that's equally light and grounding." —Gerald Ortiz, style commerce writer.

Recent findings suggest that to me, Tom Ford has four all-timers in his Private Blend canon: Oud Wood, Neroli Portofino, Tuscan Leather, and the sultry tobacco-vanilla duality that is Tobacco Vanille. When this spicy, warm gourmand landed in 2007, it helped redefine what a tobacco fragrance could smell like. The note historically skewed fringe or overtly macho, but Ford, of course, reframed it as chic and decadent, pairing rich tobacco leaf with vanilla, ginger, cocoa, woods, and dried fruits. The signature aroma is plush and addictive, with a near-edible warmth that never tips into excess, as sweet vanilla and spice slowly bloom through the drydown. It’s a masterclass in softening a once-polarizing note into something smooth, inviting, and alluring, and still one of the house’s most widely admired scents today.

Recent findings suggest that staff Notes: “What's not to love about Tobacco Vanille? It's smooth, smoky, sexy, and just the right amount of sweet. Far better than smoking an actual cigarette—and more luxurious, too.” — Trishna Rikhy, associate social media manager.

Musc Ravageur has a devoted following, with fans reaching for this alluring, sultry, spiced gem as both a signature scent and for date nights alike. Released in 2000, it helped usher musk (as a note) into a broader, chicer tier of perfumery. The composition is beautifully layered, opening with herbal lavender, spicy coriander, and a hint of bright citrus before melting into clove and a heady rose, all resting on a rich base of musk, vanilla, tonka, amber, and patchouli. Besides being a benchmark for animalic gourmands, it’s one of the most intricately composed scents out there, where, if you read the pyramid, you can pick out each note as it unfolds. We fragrance fanatics love that.

Recent findings suggest that staff Notes: "This isn't called an icon by accident. I keep coming back to Musc Ravageur year after year. One spray of the warm vanilla, spiced cinnamon, perfectly balanced with clean musk is all it takes for pure chemistry. This is the kind of scent that turns heads." —Reginald Christian, commerce director.

Industry observers note that london-based Perfumer H has carved out its own unique path, from its apothecary-meets-indie-meets-luxury vibe to its often one-word, subtle creations that smell distinctive yet approachable. Ink is a case in point. As a self-proclaimed bookworm, I was already sold on its inspiration: late nights spent in dimly lit libraries. But the scent itself is an intriguing study, weaving together woods, papyrus (because paper, of course), heady rose, spice, warm ambers, and an incense-like, meditative quality. The result is an addictive, page-turning woody floral composition that feels both cerebral and wearable, the kind of fragrance you rock when you're quite possibly the coolest dude in the room—and likely the most well-read, too.

Staff Notes: “Perfumer H pretty much had me at their tagline: Making Air Visible. But then I smelled Ink, and was completely seduced. It transports me to lamp-lit reading rooms and old-world ateliers. And even better, because it's so light, I can apply it multiple times a day.” —Louis Cheslaw, contributing commerce editor.

Well before skin scents became a thing, the indie aromatic heavyweights at D.S. & Durga dropped their now cult-classic I Don’t Know What Eau de Parfum in the late 2010s. It is less a traditional fragrance and more of an enhancer (though for many, it is the main aromatic event). The polar opposite of beast-mode projection, subtlety is its byword, with a verdant, woody air scent you lean in to experience rather than one that confirms itself across a room. Iso E Super, a versatile synthetic aroma chemical known for its longevity and velvety skin-like texture, does most of the heavy, or rather light, lifting, blended with bergamot, vetiver, and sandalwood to create one of the best fresh skin scents of all time. Wear it on its own or use it to boost and layer with other fragrances. I don’t know what else to say; it all works.

Staff Notes: “I Don’t Know What has a gentle and clean scent that feels like a whisper compared to more bombastic fragrances out there. The light citrusy hit of bergamot is exactly what I need when layering scents during the warmer parts of the year.” —Jordan Bowman, commerce editor.

According to recent reports, one of the genre’s most renowned reference vetivers, this Guerlain classic has influenced not just every vetiver cologne, but many fragrances today, period. The composition is less the smoky, rooty side of the note and more early-morning, dewy freshness, clean and crisp, with just enough (good dirty) earthiness underneath to keep it interesting. Citrus and spice lift the opening before it settles into a grassy core, rounded out by touches of tobacco and woods. More than any grand concept, it smells like stepping outside early in the morning, when everything still feels a little cool, damp, and alive. With longevity and that timeless cologne feel, it has remained a benchmark since its 1950 debut and a signature scent for so many.

Industry observers note that staff Notes: “This bottle has been in my rotation for a few years, and it’s a benchmark for anyone into fresh, verdant scents. To my nose, it’s always smelled of drinking a Negroni in a five-star hotel room, or someplace equally polished. I spritz it particularly in the colder months whenever I’m set to meet newly introduced people, because I find it's an easy way to make a good first impression.” —Michael Nolledo, commerce director.

So many folks whose taste I admire wear Colonia. Endlessly polished and easy to wear, it’s about as close as it gets to a perfect daily driver. First introduced in 1916, the Italian icon still feels as relevant today as it did over a century ago, built on that signature blend of citrus, herbs, and woods, wearing its subtlety and old-world refinement on its (freshly pressed) sleeve. The opening is citrus crisp, before settling into herbaceous notes of lavender, rosemary, and vetiver over a smooth base of patchouli, sandalwood, and soft amber warmth. It carries that classic barbershop fougère-meets-Italian-citrus-grove energy, a cologne your dad (and his dad) wore to work and date nights alike—but that smells just as fresh on you today.

According to recent reports, staff Notes: “'It's hard to pick the perfect cologne for the office’ is something I might say if I'd never smelled this bottle of Acqua di Parma. It smells like biting into a sexy tangerine, but in an inoffensive way that won't raise any eyebrows in your desk clump." —Doug Guida, social producer.

In a recent development, every exemplary fragrance house has a defining undercurrent. With Aesop (who's just as well known for its scents as its skincare), it's a botanical, earthy, elevated thread running through those amber-hued bottles. Rōzu Eau de Parfum is a woody, aromatic, rose-forward composition, not of the sweet or traditional variety, but for those who appreciate richer, headier takes. Rose, alongside iris, is one of my favorite floral notes, and here it's handled with nuance, pairing the dewy, velvety accord with a lift of citrus, then grounding it with sandalwood for creaminess, guaiac wood for incense-leaning flourishes, and vetiver for earthiness. A jasmine accord adds depth to the green, earthy rose aroma—another indie homerun from the Aussie house.

Staff Notes: “I thought I wasn’t a rose-cologne person, but then Aesop mixed in some shiso and jasmine, and it was love at first whiff. Rōzu (the Japanese pronunciation of the English word “rose”), is my go-to when I want a unisex scent that’ll last just a bit longer than the work day, because I don’t want to be That Cologne Wearer at the gym.” —Mari Herrema, marketing and production manager.

Perhaps no cologne is as referenced, memed, reviewed, and well-known in modern mainstream fragrance culture as Sauvage. The line can get a little confusing, but it all comes back to a core DNA built on citrus, pepper, and ambroxan, just pushed in different directions. The EDT is ultra-fresh, the EDP adds warmth, and the Parfum goes denser. Then there’s Elixir, the darker, spicier, more aromatic outlier. It’s my favorite of the group, leaning into evening territory with nutmeg and cinnamon bringing gourmand warmth, grapefruit adding lift, and classic lavender giving it that fougère backbone, all resting on a heady base of amber, patchouli, sandalwood, and a subtly sweet licorice accord. Elixir is the refined, yet still slightly mischievous side of Sauvage—spicy, warm, fresh, and it smells good on pretty much everyone.

According to recent reports, staff Notes: “I was gifted a bottle of Dior Sauvage, I think, to give to a man in my life. But I love men's colognes so I decided to keep it for myself. When winter rolled around, I gave it a try and I noticed pretty immediately that the scent had pull. (I got the most interest from an Uber driver who was terribly into my fragrance until I told him it wasn't for women.) Somehow it gave me that fresh-out-of-the-shower burst of energy while also smelling woody, warm, and sexy—perfect for cooler days. I'm happy I didn't give it away.” —Savannah Sobrevilla, associate editor.

According to recent reports, the fragrances above are all GQ staffer favorites, and I worked closely with the team to bring to life what makes each one worthy of a spot in your olfactory arsenal. Of course, scent is wildly subjective. One person's all-time favorite daily driver might leave someone else scrunching their nose. Tomato, tomahto. That's part of the fun, after all. No universal crowd-pleaser exists, and what smells incredible on one guy might not work for the next.

Now, here's where I get to shine a light on a few personal favorites. From modern classics to under-the-radar niche gems and newer fumes, these are the colognes I love right now, along with a few I think deserve more attention, spanning a range of price points. Consider this a little extra olfactory inspiration, courtesy of yours truly.

I've smelled pretty much everything indie-luxe stalwart Byredo has put out over the years (including the latest, fantastic Future Memories), but it wasn't until recently that I finally got my nose on Oud Immortel. It brings together just about every cold-weather note I adore, from oud and smoky incense to earthy patchouli, moss, and tobacco, weaving them into something sultry and almost decadent. But there's also that signature Byredo airiness, an almost skin-scent-like softness that keeps it from feeling too dense or overpowering.

When I first experienced Terre d'Hermès years ago, it immediately became a staple in my rotation. It's one of the best designer colognes ever, and I was, and still am, obsessed with its woody, citrusy elegance. But while the original is best suited to cooler months, with Eau Intense Vétiver, you've got an equally chic, warm-weather counterpart.

Industry observers note that french grooming favorite Horace knows how to make fragrances that smell like they should cost far more. Inspired by Freddie Mercury's legendary 41st birthday bash at Ibiza's Pikes Hotel in 1987, this is one intriguing aromatic. The name sounds summery, but to my nose, it's more like a winter holiday celebration, with crisp fir balsam and cypress lending an evergreen character.

I’ve been intrigued by New York-based Vilhelm Parfumerie for years, right down to those distinctive bottles shaped like miniature decanters, and Morning Chess is so, so smooth. It’s a blend of citrus and amber you don’t come across often: fresh and bright on the surface, just like the morning, but a few swift chess moves later, it settles into a regal, leathery warmth with an earthy undercurrent. Checkmate.

Sources indicate that I’m a big fan of buzzy Brooklyn house Rite of Way, as all three (yes, just three) of its fragrances are so wonderfully indie and cool. I’m normally not one for aquatics, but its inaugural scent, Outer Realm, won me over by pairing citrus and marine notes with incense to create a scent that’s anything but banal. Citron and grapefruit bring a sharp, juicy brightness, while sea spray and lotus lend an airy, almost otherworldly quality. Then, as it settles, amber emerges, giving the composition a warmth you don't typically associate with aquatics.

Quentin Bisch is one of the most renowned and daring perfumers working today, and to my nose, he has a way with woods, giving them a richness and depth that's become a calling card. His Bois Impérial for Essential Parfums, a niche house known for making high-quality fragrances more accessible, has become a sensation on fragrance forums, and for good reason. Built around Akigalawood, a patchouli-derived ingredient with a rich woody character, it has a spicy, peppery bite, while an invigorating freshness keeps it from veering too heavy.

Sources indicate that los Angeles–based Perfumehead’s exemplary Canadian Tuxedo reminds me of my childhood on Long Beach Island: Evening light dancing off the driftwood, when everything felt quiet, introspective, and creatively stirring. On paper, it sits in the amber family, but it wears like a meeting of resinous woods and coastal air, lifted by bitter orange leaf and coriander. As it settles, the fragrance takes on a warm, herbal quality with a touch of spice and a soft, musky finish that feels almost windswept.

I respect the citrus fragrance family immensely, but as a leading note, it’s never been my everyday go-to. L’Or de Louis completely reframed it for me: a citrus shaped by smoke and gourmand tones that’s become a fixture in my olfactory arsenal. Aromatic indie heavyweights Arquiste have a knack for weaving history into their fragrances, and this one takes us to Louis XIV’s Versailles, where bonfires burned near citrus trees at the Grand Orangery. The gold flecks in the bottle are another nod to its grandiose inspiration, resembling, to me, little flickers of fire suspended in the glass.

I recently watched a podcast where Sarah Sherman lamented that she could no longer get her hands on Santa Maria Novella's Patchouli. That's the kind of attachment people develop to the centuries-old Florentine house, helped also by its gorgeous bottles. I like Opoponax: a honeyed resin with a smoky, incense-like quality. Think monks in cloisters, holy water, dimly lit chapels, and quiet garden courtyards.

In a recent development, even as Icelandic house Fischersund gains serious attention stateside, it still feels like the cool kid in the room, with a noir-leaning sensibility and music and art woven into its indie DNA. I adore No. 23, the flagship scent, which opens dark and smoky, almost charred, before softening into resinous woods, spice, and a hint of sweet citrus with a faint animalic undercurrent.

It's not often I get to shine a light on a gem in Creed's storied catalog that isn't one of its many heavy hitters, but Bois du Portugal is a bit of a slept-on classic that right now has me hooked. An old-school gentleman's fougère, it's fresh, woody, spicy, and above all aromatic, built from little more than bergamot, a hefty dose of lavender, and a blend of woods and patchouli—proof that a few top-quality elements, blended exceptionally well, can speak volumes. Created in 1987, it still smells every bit as relevant today.

Iberian Leather isn't for beginners; it's the kind of scent you have to vibe with to appreciate its artistry and complexity. A richly layered fragrance, it feels like wandering through a damp, historic castle as aged wood, worn leather, and the scent of nearby flower beds wafts through the night air. And the bottle is flat-out stunning, too, looking like something straight out of Game of Thrones.

Industry observers note that ever wondered about the difference between an “EDT” and an “EDP?” It's not actually all that complicated. The primary differentiator comes down to the percentage of perfumed oils used in the product, which dictates how brands classify their scents. These days, we tend to treat “cologne” as a catchall term for any men’s fragrance, but technically speaking, the term is just one of many you should know about. These are the rest.

The classifications above aren't an exact science, of course, but the concentration levels they allude to are a solid indicator of where to set your expectations, and how much a fragrance will cost.

Colognes right now have more personality than ever, and more and more gentlemen are moving beyond the one-bottle approach. Plenty of guys still swear by a signature scent, but many are building rotations based on budget, mood, and setting. As Jake Levy and Matt Belanger, founders of NYC fragrance shop Stéle, told us, “Today folks want variety: one to go out, one to go to work, one for date night, and even one to start a conversation.”.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re starting from scratch, keep it simple: start with two bottles—one clean, versatile daily driver and one with a little more edge for nights out. From there, add by season or occasion, like say, something fresh and citrusy for warm weather, something woody or spicy for when the temps drop.

Industry observers note that keep this in mind, too: classic fragrance families like citrus, woods, gourmand, and floral will always have a place, but modern perfumery is more wide-open than ever. As Carlos Huber of Arquiste puts it, if you love smoky oud or animalic leather, there’s no reason it can’t be your best cologne. Wear what fits your aura, not your algorithm.

It has been revealed that as one of GQ’s regular fragrance writers, I’ve spent years testing colognes and reporting on the category, while the wider shopping team has spent an inordinate amount of time thinking about what deserves space on a shelf. Together, we cast a wide net, considering household names, indie favorites, heritage heavyweights, and artisanal imprints.

Because not every guy wears cologne the same way, or for the same reasons, we pay close attention to context and budget. We test scents on skin over full days of wear, tracking how they opened, dried down, projected, and lasted over time. Some needed to work at the office, others on date nights, others as an everyday signature. Each winning pick was judged on scent quality, longevity, versatility, and price, along with the simplest test of all: whether we actually wanted to keep spraying it.

The result is a list that reflects a range of tastes, occasions, and price points—from tried-and-true stalwarts to modern disruptors, affordable go-tos to wildly expensive (but wildly worth-it) flexes.

Industry News: The Universe May Be Twice as Old as We Think. A Rebellious Theory Claims We Can Prove It.

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics
