Industry News: Buying Your First Pair of Selvedge Jeans? Start Here

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, we’ve got bad news for white couches: Crunchy, indigo-dyed, raw selvedge jeans are back.
  • Recent findings suggest that but while it, ahem, faded from the public eye, the raw denim market was still tended to by the true believers among us.
  • According to recent reports, so available, in fact, that the selection can be overwhelming.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we’ve got bad news for white couches: Crunchy, indigo-dyed, raw selvedge jeans are back. People might say they never left, but as someone who literally edited a daily web series about denim fades from 2015 to 2018, I can assure you that across the almost-decade since, the category has taken something of a back seat as jeans with interesting washes and nostalgic cuts (Our Legacy’s Third Cut, GAP’s 90s Loose) surged in popularity.

Recent findings suggest that but while it, ahem, faded from the public eye, the raw denim market was still tended to by the true believers among us. And we owe them a great debt, because their stewardship means we’re not just picking up where the last trend left off. Instead, we’re jumping into an elevated timeline. The best makers in the world have only gotten better, the cuts have gotten more diverse, and a whole bunch of stuff that was once incredibly hard to find in the United States is now readily available.

According to recent reports, so available, in fact, that the selection can be overwhelming. Which is where I come in! Because while there are now thousands of pairs of raw denim jeans to choose from, I can tell you that only a precious few specific cuts have consistently dominated Subreddits, YouTube roundups, and my text message history for the best part of this century. Ten of them are below, starting with five approachable icons, and moving through to five more legendary deeper cuts. Let’s get faded.

Recent findings suggest that the manufacturer behind Sugar Cane, Toyo Enterprise, has been making hard-wearing garments since the mid-’60s, but Sugar Cane didn’t come around until 1975. Ever since, they’ve been making some of the most considered, sturdy and timeless jeans and workwear on the planet in Japan, all of it aging more beautifully than a fancy barolo.

If you’re looking to dip your toes into the Sugar Cane pool, the 1947 model brilliantly recreates one of the most well-loved iterations of the most well-worn model on the planet (we won’t name names, but they’re in here too), and comes in a four-season, 14.25oz. selvedge denim fabric that will produce some preposterously good fades.

For anyone who’s fallen in love with a pair of old old vintage jeans, and wondered what they felt like when they came off the production line, it’s hard to get closer than a pair of Fullcounts. The brand was started in 1993 in Osaka, Japan, with the express purpose of reverse engineering the wonder of those vintage pairs, down to the all-cotton threads and long-staple cotton.

Recent findings suggest that they sure figured it out, and still make everything in Japan. And while the classic 0105 is an absolute knockout, the Wide Straight iteration gives you a little more comfort with the same break-in potential. And if you’re just getting yourself into the raw selvedge game, a little comfort never hurts.

It has been revealed that the only Canadian entrant on this list—partly because Henry’s hasn’t restocked yet—Naked & Famous has been around since 2008. And as you might expect from a brand whose hallmark fit is called the Weird Guy, they’re a little quirky. In a good way! For not only are they rigorously dedicated to sourcing the sickest raw denim on the planet, but that denim often has some funky detailing as well, like a green weft or some galaxy-like imperfections.

The True Guy cut is technically a relaxed straight (don’t confuse that for baggy) and this particular pair has kevlar woven into the fabric, for those into literal bulletproof denim.

If you’ve ever spent time on denim message boards, you’ve probably seen the name “Iron Heart” associated with some of the heaviest denim known to man. (If you’ve never been, steel yourself before entering.) And while it is true that the Japanese brand pushes the definition of heavyweight to its absolute limit, it also makes a damn good pair of regular jeans.

According to recent reports, in fact, the mid-weight fare is as good as any on the market, will produce some HOF-worthy fades, and won’t require a title fight to soften up. Within that weight class, the straight leg of the 634S-142 is the kind of timeless silhouette that should outlast most trend cycles. (Also, for the record, “mid-weight” is a relative term. This is the lightest-weight denim that Iron Heart will entertain.).

It has been revealed that while the US quite literally invented jeans as we understand them (denim as a fabric is another story, for those keeping very detailed score), you’d be forgiven for thinking otherwise, considering the lack of US-made options on this list. But thankfully, 3Sixteen is doing the work of like six companies at this point, sourcing the world’s finest denim—we don’t really make that here anymore—and stitching the 5-pockets up back home in the USA.

Every cut they make has a legion of fans, but the semi-recent, semi-baggy RS is the one tearing up the charts at the moment. And for great reasons. It’s got the aforementioned room, has a top block (re: the area that houses the waistband, fly and pockets) that doesn’t get all bunched up and funky, and a higher rise that’s flattering on just about everyone. As a result, it’s a pair that both denimheads and denim rookies appreciate with the same kind of zeal.

When it comes to details that will turn a denimhead into a living meme—Vince McMahon Progression, Guy Turning Around, you pick—few brands can execute them like Oni can. From the denim itself, which is milled in Japan and feels more handmade than small-batch sourdough, to the period-accurate details like flat-felled seams and linear bar tacks, every pair starts as a work of art and develops into a wholly separate work of art as they’re worn.

According to recent reports, the only issue, really, is finding them, because hand-making just about everything isn’t exactly a scalable process. When they’re around, (and they right now are!) they’re worth more than just a gander, particularly the Wide Straight, which has a loose, straight leg and a healthy, fairly forgiving rise. This pair in particular is made with lighter-weight 12oz. denim, but don’t mistake that for lightweight denim—it’ll hold up year round, and could always handle some longjohns during a cold-snap, if you feel so inclined.

Those familiar with the Osaka 5—the loose collection of denim brands that sprouted up in Osaka in the ‘70s, ‘80s and ‘90s and redefined the very notion of raw denim specifically and the idea of what “jeans” could be, more broadly—will know that Warehouse was the fifth and final member, founded by two alums from a different member, Evisu. And for roughly 30 years the brand’s pumped out intricately detailed, vintage-indebted jeans that some of the pickiest people on the planet have sworn by, even going so far as sourcing American cotton to keep the look and feel as close to the source material as possible.

This pair in particular is based on one of the most popular pairs of 501s Levi’s ever made, the 1966 model, which had a straight leg and a high rise and a slightly twisted seam after a few washes, giving it a slow-developing signature—all present and accounted for here in 2026 via Warehouse.

In a recent development, these aren’t for the faint of heart. Let’s get that out of the way. 21oz. denim is almost armor, especially if your previous denim reference point is something with a wash, a rinse or some stretch. But for anyone looking for a challenge, absolutely electric fades and a pair of jeans that might outlast horseshoe crabs, look no further.

In a recent development, that’s because Samurai, another Osaka-based brand (but not part of the Osaka 5, for whatever it’s worth), makes some of the hardest-fading, hardest-wearing, most-revered jeans anywhere, and that includes the ultra-heavyweight numbers. And who knows, all that extra (fabric) weight might be nice with winter incoming.

Industry observers note that levi’s offers some great raw selvedge 501s at a pretty reasonable price, a pair that will age well and (with proper care of course) last for years. The 501, however, isn’t a standardized cut. In fact, it’s tweaked every few years to reflect the prevailing sentiment of the time a little bit better. And as a result, different eras have different hallmarks—for instance, the 1947 is a bit slimmer, the 1954 is the first pair with a zipper and the 1901 is the first pair with two back pockets.

Levi’s Vintage Clothing, a sub-label under the broader umbrella, still makes a bunch of these pairs and while the aforementioned are killer, the 1933 feels paradoxically relevant to 2026: it’s got a healthy, wide leg, a healthy rise and a couple cheeky details to differentiate it from the rest of the pack, like a back cinch and suspender buttons.

We couldn’t make this list without including a pair from the first member of the Osaka 5, in part because it’s hard to imagine any of this would be possible without Studio D’Artisan and in part because the brand still makes some of the best jeans in the world. Founded in 1979, Studio D’Artisan kicked off the obsession surrounding raw selvedge denim and bygone detailing, doubling down on craftsmanship and material quality in an era defined by synthetics and acid-washing. And they never really strayed, ultimately adding some more timeless staples to the denim assortment, all of it made in Japan with commensurate care. The SD-801 is a classic straight leg fit, made in Japan from a rope-dyed natural indigo 15oz. denim fabric and armed with a host of cheeky details, like a selvedge hit at the coin pocket and a goat leather patch at the back.

Of course, trying out any upcoming look comes with the eternal question: How do I style these things?

Well, one of the best things about raw selvedge denim is that it wears well with pretty much everything. With that in mind, don’t overthink it. But if you do grab yourself a pair of elite-tier jeans and feel like upgrading the supporting cast around it, we have some recommendations for you. For instance, a pair of sturdy leather shoes—whether some Tyroleans, a work boot, or the like—has a multiplying effect beneath some rope-dyed indigo. The same goes for a vintage-inspired, well-proportioned t-shirt or hardy flannel. Of course, as is the case with the jeans above, not all of these items are created equal. The below eight, however, have the GQ seal of approval.

The 8 Best Outdoor Pizza Ovens That Deliver Delicious Homemade Pies

📅 09 Mar 2021 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3155 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Just like tending to the grill and gathering around a firepit are inherently enjoyable, enjoying a fresh, piping-hot pizza is similarly rewarding, and it’s just a bit more special when it’s homemade.
  • Sources indicate that stand-alone and countertop outdoor pizza ovens reach much higher temperatures than regular ovens, and in less time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Just like tending to the grill and gathering around a firepit are inherently enjoyable, enjoying a fresh, piping-hot pizza is similarly rewarding, and it’s just a bit more special when it’s homemade. Baking a pie in the oven can yield good results, but there’s nothing like the crunchy crust and smoky flavor of a pizza made in a proper hearth. If you’re hoping to replicate your favorite restaurant’s pie, an outdoor pizza oven can take your homemade slices from decent to genuinely artisan.

Sources indicate that stand-alone and countertop outdoor pizza ovens reach much higher temperatures than regular ovens, and in less time. That high heat is exactly what you need for a perfectly cooked pizza crust—and several of the models we tested can cook up a pie in as little as 60 seconds.

Plus, many of the best outdoor pizza ovens we write about are suited for cooking other tasty foods, just like a real hearth. You can make fish, meat, roasted vegetables, and even bread in these wood-fired and gas-fueled models.

It has been revealed that to find the best pizza ovens, we looked at models with good features and designs and called in a handful to try out for ourselves. We selected pizza ovens that use a variety of fuels, including gas, charcoal, and wood. Outdoor pizza ovens all pretty much come with a learning curve, but we identified models best suited to beginners and pizza aficionados alike to offer a range that caters to different skill levels.

For testing, we heated each oven for 30 minutes to season them and burn off any oils or contaminants from manufacturing, then let them cool completely. Fifteen minutes after firing up each oven on high using propane burners, we measured the temperatures on the pizza stones with an infrared thermometer.

Then, we made pizza, using the same dough each time, with propane and oak firewood as our fuel. During cooking, we noted how well each oven performed, different features, and its ease of use. Finally—and most enjoyably—we assessed (a.k.a. ate) the pizza. We recommend the following pizza ovens based on our hands-on experience, their specs, and quality.

It has been revealed that over a decade ago, Ooni built its first portable pizza oven with a design that many have mimicked. Our previous pick for the best pizza oven, the Karu 16, has been replaced by the Karu 2 Pro. It’s the exact same as the Karu 16 with three new features: an air vent, Bluetooth-connected thermometer, and an even larger window on the oven door.

Like the Karu 16, the Karu 2 Pro makes 16-inch pizzas fired either with propane or wood. In testing, we liked the locking door with a glass window, which helped maintain a consistent temperature and allowed us to keep an eye on our pizza while it cooked.

Ooni also added a digital thermometer to this model that monitors air temperature in the oven via a wired probe. That info is sent to your phone so you can be in the kitchen prepping more pies or enjoying company instead of babysitting the oven.

Using the propane burner is easy and gets the job done, but we appreciate the large firebox for wood, which provides a lot more flame across the top of the oven. The large capacity also had us refilling it less frequently than smaller wood-fired ovens.

It has been revealed that the Karu 2 Pro also doubles as a capable charcoal grill if you want to cook meat or veggies. While we like a dedicated grill for burgers and steaks, the Karu 2 is a do-it-all outdoor kitchen if you have limited outdoor space. The addition of the newly introduced air vent even gets it down to a consistent 200 degrees Fahrenheit for low-and-slow cooking.

Full Ooni Karu 2 Multi-Fuel Outdoor Pizza Oven Review.

In a recent development, the Ninja Artisan is the only electric outdoor pizza oven we've come across that's worth a double take. It needs to be covered if left outside because of the electrical components, but the body is made of weather-resistant steel.

Sources indicate that our tester, Danny Perez, didn’t have to hassle with pellets or propane to get things started—he simply plugged it in, preheated, and started cooking. It has a max temp of 700 degrees Fahrenheit, which is less than most gas and wood-fired ovens, but it's not necessarily a bad thing.

It has been revealed that while a 1,000-degree oven that makes pizza in 90 seconds sounds easy, there's a lot more to it. Shredded mozzarella starts melting in seconds, the dough crust needs a minute to bake, and toppings may require a different cooking time. Electric temperature controls and a lower max heat offer more runway before taking off on your pizza-making journey. Another plus of an electric outdoor pizza oven is even cooking because there's no need to turn the pizza when it's in the oven.

The Ninja has built-in preset pizza modes to cook different styles of 'za: Neapolitan, New York, thin crust, and pan. It preheats to respective target temps for each and then prompts you to add the pizza. Hit start and it starts counting down for a perfectly timed cook.

He tried the thin crust setting, which cooked the pizza at 550 degrees Fahrenheit for four minutes. When the timer went off, out came an evenly cooked pepperoni pizza.

The Neapolitan setting worked great as well. It cooked the pizza at 700 degrees F for two and a half minutes yielding an impressively crisped crust with some leopard spotting.

Full Ninja Artisan Outdoor Pizza Oven Review.

Sources indicate that A lot of outdoor pizza ovens are portable enough to pick up and move, but they aren't designed with transportation in mind. Fair—most of us park them in the backyard. Gozney put more thought into portability than its competitors with the Tread pizza oven.

It weighs 30 pounds, has two handles on top, and has a manageable square shape. It can go from home to tailgate with ease. We tested the Tread with the collapsible Venture Stand, which gives you a cooking space wherever you take it.

Getting the Tread fired up only takes a few seconds when using the control dial on the side. The flames instantly extended across the roof of the pizza oven, and we wanted things to get hot, so we preheated for about 20 minutes. Once it reached an optimal temperature, we were ready to pitch the first pizza.

In a recent development, the compact size can fit up to 12-inch pies, which is plenty substantial for personal pizzas. In testing, we found that the oven has great heat retention, so you can cook them one after another. We also found the opening offered enough wiggle room to rotate the pie with a pizza peel for even cooking.

The Tread comes with a built-in thermometer on the side, but we still used an infrared thermometer to measure the temperature of the pizza stone itself. The quick-release gas hose and regulator make for quick setup, too. For those who proposal to take the Tread on the go, Gozney also has a handy carrying case.

Full Gozney Tread Portable Outdoor Pizza Oven Review.

Industry observers note that you'd be hard-pressed to find an electric pizza oven that gets the job done like the original Ooni Volt, but the Ooni Volt 2 is an honorable step up. This model has a smaller carbon footprint than its predecessor, and it's even easier to use.

In a recent development, messing with temperatures can get complicated rapidly, but the Volt 2 has three presets for cooking Neapolitan, New York, and Chicago Deep Dish-style pizzas to perfection. We usually use an infrared thermometer to gauge the temperature of pizza stones, but we trusted the presets and weren't disappointed.

Recent findings suggest that while this electric pizza oven doesn't exactly mimic a wood-fired or propane-fueled model, it has its place in the kitchen. The Volt 2 can be used all year long, is capable of cooking plenty of your favorites, and is much easier to manage. Even if you already have an outdoor model, we'd go so far as to say that you might need this indoor version, too.

Full Ooni Volt 2 Electric Pizza Oven Review.

Typically, rotating pizza stones are a gimmick you find on budget pizza ovens to make up for a low temperature range, especially for an electric model. GreenPan’s Stanley Tucci pizza oven, however, has both firepower and a surprisingly effective rotating stone for indoor and outdoor use.

The controls on this model go from 350 to 850 degrees Fahrenheit, so you can use it for more than just cooking pizza. The oven also has a temperature boost feature that allows you to “boost” the top, bottom, or both heating elements. During testing, Ford used this to crisp up the top crust and brown the edges, and this feature offered more flexibility for cooking his pizza exactly how he liked it.

In a recent development, the Stanley Tucci pizza oven uses a round stone, which sometimes can make it harder to accurately pitch your creation onto the stone. With this model, the oven door has a mechanism attached so that when you open it, the stone is lifted and pulled out, making it easier to toss in your pizza and avoid accidental spills and messes.

Overall, this is the best electric rotating pizza oven that Ford has tried yet, though he noted that this design is limited to 12-inch pizzas only.

Full GreenPan Stanley Tucci Pizza Oven Review.

The Gozney Dome Gen2 is definitely a luxury pizza oven, but it's chock-full of features that could potentially make it a worthy investment for those who are dedicated to perfecting their pizza and baking crafts.

Sources indicate that A 14-inch flue sits atop the roof of the oven, and this was helpful for maintaining airflow and flames. The Dome Gen2 comes with a standard propane burner, and the wood kit is optional. This helps simplify the process for newer pizza-makers, since wood-fired cooking takes some time to master.

It has been revealed that one of the highlights we appreciate the most is the size of the oven itself. After preheating, we had no problem cooking two midsize pizzas side-by-side, and we could move the pies around if we needed to slow the cook time.

Sources indicate that it takes a little longer for the oven to heat up when using wood, but luckily, changing the fuel mode doesn't make the burner obsolete. We were able to fire up the oven with the burner first, then switched to wood when it reached the right temperature and turned off the propane.

Recent findings suggest that we tested the Dome Gen2 on a somewhat windy day, and the propane burner blew out a few times. To offset this, we kept the temperature a little higher than usual and burned charcoal on the wood tray for better control.

The digital display is a very convenient feature. Instead of using an infrared thermometer, we could monitor levels in real time right on the pizza oven without worrying about accuracy.

Full Gozney Dome Gen2 Dual Fuel Pizza Oven Review.

A pizza oven from the smokeless firepit folks? Sign us up. The ease of cooking with a propane burner is tough to beat.

It took us about 20 minutes to heat up the oven using propane, though you should expect a bit more time when it’s relatively cool out and less when it’s hot. In testing, the average cook time was about 90 seconds and required turning the pie every 20 seconds or so.

The Pi Prime’s manual not only had thorough assembly instructions but a lot of helpful notes and tips to get started, including suggested target temperatures for different styles of pizza.

Industry observers note that we found that managing oven and stone temperatures didn’t take too much time, although like other ovens without a door, breezy or windy days could make it more challenging. The oven opening on the Pi is 13 inches wide, so 12-inch pies are about as big as this oven can handle.

According to recent reports, similar to Solo Stove fire pits, ventilation holes line the bottom of the pizza oven for plenty of airflow. The Pi Prime is also constructed with durable 304 stainless steel to withstand high temps and different weather conditions.

Full Solo Stove Pi Prime Outdoor Pizza Oven Review.

In a recent development, the Arc Lite is about as analog as it gets, equipped with only a pizza stone, ignition knob, and stainless steel insulated housing to bake your favorite pies. While this model is smaller and less features-heavy than the Dome Gen2 we’ve tested, that doesn’t mean it’s any less effective.

It didn’t take long for us to get the Arc Lite up and running. We just connected the hose to the propane tank then pressed and turned the knob to ignite. It took about 20 minutes for the pizza oven to warm up on a cooler spring day, and we maintained an internal temperature of 800 degrees Fahrenheit. The Arc Lite reaches 950, but that high heat requires more attention so you don’t overcook your pie.

The pizza we made was ready in about 90 seconds and had the crunchy crust and bubbly cheese we desired, and the only downside we really came across during testing is that the Arc Lite is limited on size and can only cook up to 12-inch pizzas. Great for everyday bites, but not ideal if you’re looking to host and make multiple pies at once.

Full Gozney Arc Lite Outdoor Pizza Oven Review.

Our resident pizza oven expert, Brad Ford, is regularly trying new models to consider for this roundup. In cases where we remove a model we’ve tested in favor of something new, we still like to highlight it here.

The All-Clad Rotating Stone Outdoor Pizza Oven was our previous pick for the best rotating design. It runs on four AA batteries and only requires a push button to start. But for this particular feature, Ford prefers the GreenPan Stanley Tucci Indoor and Outdoor Pizza Oven. It had clear benefits during his testing experience, and the unique lifting mechanism under the round stone made it easier to pitch pizzas into the oven.

Outdoor pizza ovens use gas or wood to create flames across the top that radiate intense heat downward, warming the pizza stone—like preheating an oven in your house. However, unlike your home oven, outdoor pizza ovens can reach up to 950 degrees Fahrenheit.

In a recent development, once the outdoor pizza oven hits cooking temperature and your pizza is placed inside, it only takes a couple of minutes to cook. The pizza stone or oven floor gets to the same temperature as the roof so the pizza cooks fast and evenly. While it cooks, those flames up top produce a golden crust that’s crispy on the outside and soft and airy on the inside. Because the pizza only takes a minute or so to cook, you can make a few with different toppings one after another.

Wood is the traditional fuel of choice for pizza ovens, favored for the smoky flavor it imparts in the crust and toppings. However, wood (or charcoal) fires take longer to heat up and require more attention to maintain the right temperature. That may not be an issue if you’re only making a couple of pies, but it can become a hassle if you’re cooking multiple pies for a large group, or entertaining a party while you cook.

Propane fuel can heat a pizza oven up rather swiftly. Since it only takes around 15 to 20 minutes to preheat, it's hard to deny the convenience of being able to cook a pie in a relatively short time frame. Plus, cleanup is easy when there’s no ashy firebox to empty. Just keep in mind that a propane oven won't give you that unique, wood-fired flavor.

Sources indicate that luckily, you don't have to sacrifice one for the other: A few of the brands we recommend offer extra accessories you can buy to accommodate a different fuel type. There are even some options with combined fuel, so you can heat up your oven fast with the propane and imbue the pizza with wood-fired flavor, too.

According to recent reports, the oven’s size determines the maximum temperature output the unit can reach, as well as the size of pie you can cook. Most outdoor pizza ovens are designed for 12- or 14-inch pies. Our Best Overall pick, though, can accommodate pizzas up to 16 inches for oversized, restaurant-like slices.

Industry observers note that pizzas are typically cooked between 450 and 600 degrees Fahrenheit. Classic Neapolitan pizza requires temperatures around 900 degrees—these are the ones with golden crusts, mottled with dark leopard spots. High-end models top out at around 950 degrees Fahrenheit.

The pizza ovens we recommend have max temperatures that far exceed 500 degrees, but note that an oven with a relatively low maximum temperature still gives you a delicious, cooked-through pie—it just may not look quite as picture-perfect.

In short, yes. Outdoor pizza ovens are incredibly versatile. Beyond pies, you can cook meats like steak and chicken, roast veggies, bake bread (like sourdough or focaccia), prep seafood, make cast-iron dishes, and bake desserts. Since it's essentially a super-hot wood-fired oven, you can use plenty of different methods to whip up your favorite foods.

Accessories aren't necessarily a requirement for operating your pizza oven, but they can make the process a lot smoother and safer. We recommend using tools such as a pizza peel to move and adjust your pie, an infrared thermometer to check stone temp accurately, heat-resistant gloves, and a brush or scraper for cleaning the stone.

In a recent development, outdoor pizza ovens are generally easy to clean and don't require a ton of maintenance since their high temperatures naturally burn off a majority of food residue. Usually, you can just brush off ash and debris after the oven has cooled down. You can also occasionally run it at high heat to get rid of any extra stubborn bits, and wipe down the exterior as needed. Avoid using water or soap on the pizza stone to prevent cracking.

Recent findings suggest that so you’ve been invited to a black-tie wedding. Before descending into a formalwear-induced anxiety spiral, consider the benefits—this is your chance to go all out with a statement evening look you’d never otherwise get the chance to wear. (Plus, the people-watching is guaranteed to be incredible.).

The main thing to keep in mind is the definition of the dress code. Put simply, “black tie” means floor-length hemlines, so leave the midi dress at home in favor of something ankle-sweeping. From there, you’ll find there’s a lot of variation within the black-tie wedding guest dress options.

If you’re stuck on where to start, begin by considering the setting. A black-tie event in an upscale city venue requires a different sort of formal dress than a black-tie event in a bucolic setting. Think about fabrics and the season, as well as silhouette: Do you go light and dreamy, with layers of tulle and pleated chiffon? Or moody and sophisticated with luxe silk and embroidered jacquard? When in doubt, a classic A-line or halterneck style offers just enough formality. And for winter weddings, anything in rich tones, from golden saffron to oxblood to inky navy, is a safe bet.

From simple black dresses to beaded sequins, shop our edit of the best black-tie wedding guest dresses, ahead.

You can’t go wrong with a satin dress. Elegant and polished, these slinky gowns feel like the ideal canvas for all sorts of accessorizing. SIR’s short-sleeve dark plum dress calls for minimalism with sculptural gold jewelry; something sleeker, such as Amsale’s liquid gold gown, is an opportunity to play with semi-precious gemstone jewelry (like amethysts, citrines, tourmalines, and aquamarines) to enhance the richness of the hue.

Sources indicate that come winter, velvet is hard to beat. Its plush texture and light-catching sheen add instant depth to a simple silhouette, as seen with Bernadette’s embellished column dress and Liberowe’s halter maxi. Just be sure to pair your look with minimal jewelry to let the fabric take the lead.

Sources indicate that it’s in the name: If you’re not sure what to wear for this dress code, black is generally a safe bet. Experiment with the shape to bring interest to a restrained palette. Industry observers note that take inspiration from the champagne toast with your black-tie gown. If you’re searching for after-hours glamour, look no further than Aje’s feather-trimmed sequined gown or Taller Marmo’s radiant gold mockneck.

There’s something especially sculptural about a draped dress. Whether it’s expressed throughout the silhouette, as on Tory Burch’s design, or shows up in the one-shoulder asymmetry of Simkhai’s dark spruce gown, the fluid finish feels undeniably artistic.

It has been revealed that no one remarked long-sleeve formal dresses had to be frumpy. Try a sleeker silhouette, like Victoria Beckham’s black twist-waist gown or Kallmeyer’s minimalist burgundy maxi. For a looser fit, Proenza Schouler’s cold-shoulder piece with an open back is just what you need.

Can I wear colors other than black to a black-tie wedding?

Sources indicate that yes! This dress code has more to do with length and style than color—and while wearing a black gown is certainly a shortcut to looking put-together, sometimes your host will actually prefer color. A summer destination wedding is the perfect occasion for bright hues, for instance, while a fall event calls for a moody, autumnal palette.

Can I wear a jumpsuit instead of a dress?

Industry observers note that it all depends on the jumpsuit. Something in a luxe fabric, like silk or taffeta, with sharp tailoring is probably alright (though to be safe, you can always double-check with the couple). And if you’re unsure, the staunchly anti-gown guest can opt for a polished suit in similarly upscale materials for a sophisticated twist on the dress code.

Should I choose my black-tie dress depending on the venue or season?

When in doubt, take context clues from the invite. The season, venue, and even time of ceremony are all helpful indicators of what kind of dress to pick—you wouldn’t wear a velvet floor-length gown to a morning ceremony in July, just as a strapless style in floral crepe might be a poor choice for a snowy winter fête.

What are the key guidelines for black-tie wedding guest dresses?

Can a wedding guest wear a midi dress to a black-tie wedding?

Absolutely not. Black tie equals floor-length hemlines, and a midi will look out of place in a room full of gowns.

What are the differences between a black-tie and a black-tie optional wedding guest dress?

According to recent reports, black-tie optional gives you more flexibility with your eveningwear, whereas black tie is stricter about what you can wear. In other words, a sophisticated midi is acceptable at a black-tie optional wedding, though a gown is still your best choice. (Minis, on the other hand, are always off-limits.).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare. But cut a steak into bite-size pieces and suddenly it transforms into a quick-cooking protein that’s no more demanding than chicken breast or tofu. Rub the steak with the spices and make the quick no-recipe yogurt sauce a few hours ahead if it’s helpful with time management. To account for the extra liquid thrown off by the spinach as it cooks, the water-to-couscous ratio in this recipe differs from that often found on the back of the bag (or box) so measure accordingly.

More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.

In a recent development, place 1–1¼ lb. boneless Fresh York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp. dried oregano, 2 tsp. onion powder, 2 tsp. sugar, and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl; season generously with freshly ground pepper and toss to coat. Let sit at least 10 minutes or cover and chill up to 8 hours (no need to bring to room temperature before cooking if chilling).

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or medium Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid over medium. Add 1 bunch scallions, thinly sliced, ½ cup finely chopped dill, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until scallions are softened, about 5 minutes. Add 10 oz. baby spinach in 2–3 handfuls, stirring and letting wilt slightly after each addition before adding more, 5–7 minutes total. Pour in 1 cup water and bring to a boil; season with more salt if needed. Add 1 cup Moroccan couscous and stir to break up any lumps. Remove from heat; quickly cover with lid and let sit 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over high. Arrange steak in a single layer; cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 6–8 minutes. Reduce heat to medium; continue to cook, stirring often, until meat is just cooked through, about 1 minute more. Remove from heat. Add remaining 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; toss to combine. (Residual heat from pan will cook out any raw garlic flavor.).

Industry observers note that uncover couscous and fluff with a fork to separate grains. Spoon into a large shallow bowl or onto a platter. Top with steak. Cut 1 lemon into quarters and squeeze juice from 1 quarter over steak. Scatter thinly sliced cucumber and some dill sprigs on top; drizzle with oil.

Industry observers note that combine 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt and a generous pinch of kosher salt in a small bowl; squeeze juice from 2 lemon quarters into yogurt. Stir to combine. If sauce is thick, stir in water, a spoonful at a time, to loosen.

Serve steak and couscous with yogurt sauce and remaining lemon quarter and more lemon wedges for squeezing over.

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1009 w)

In Trans Communities Across the Country, Clothing Swaps Are Promoting Style—and Safety

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1009 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, every time Isaiah Kirk leaves the Uncommon Closet’s clothing swap, he steps out onto the streets of Chicago in a new look.
  • "It’s a lot of fun," says Kirk, who identifies as nonbinary and transmasculine, of sourcing upcoming wardrobe items at clothing swaps like the one held by the Uncommon Closet.
  • For Kirk and other trans and queer people, clothing isn’t just about style; it’s about expressing themselves in a way that aligns with their gender identity and feeling as comfortable as possible in their own skin, even as anti-trans legislation continues to threaten or limit trans existence in public life across the United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every time Isaiah Kirk leaves the Uncommon Closet’s clothing swap, he steps out onto the streets of Chicago in a new look. Most recently, his haul included a pair of jeans matched with a Pokémon graphic tee and a button-up shirt. The total cost of this outfit? $0.00.

"It’s a lot of fun," says Kirk, who identifies as nonbinary and transmasculine, of sourcing upcoming wardrobe items at clothing swaps like the one held by the Uncommon Closet. “The environment, the camaraderie, it’s safe and inclusive.”.

For Kirk and other trans and queer people, clothing isn’t just about style; it’s about expressing themselves in a way that aligns with their gender identity and feeling as comfortable as possible in their own skin, even as anti-trans legislation continues to threaten or limit trans existence in public life across the United States.

A clothing swap setup at Chicago’s Uncommon Closet.

“I primarily work with people who have body dysmorphia or dysphoria,” indicates AJ Mix, who runs community outreach at the Uncommon Closet. Many of their clients are trans or queer people who have faced discrimination for expressing a different gender identity than their sex assigned at birth. “A lot of people have trauma going to stores,” Mix says. Their job is often to function as a sort of therapeutic personal stylist, accompanying clients—some of whom are trans women early in their transition—on trips to gendered shopping aisles they might be afraid to navigate alone.

Industry observers note that according to Mix, the Uncommon Closet’s clothing swap was meant to be a one-time event in 2024, during the queer sewing and alteration business’s grand reopening. But then they noticed the huge demand for this free service. Mix now hosts three swaps a year—in spring, summer, and winter—to help people prepare for the seasonal shifts in Chicago’s weather. “We have a lot of new people coming in from the South to Chicago due to the political climate,” Mix states. “A lot of people use their entire savings to haul their entire lives up here, and so they just don’t have any money.”.

Elsewhere, on the East Coast, Alex Carroll, the 20-year-old founder of NYC Youth for Trans Rights, organizes clothing swaps for young people who struggle to afford gender-affirming accessories. A binder, which flattens the chest to give wearers a more masculine silhouette, can run upwards of $50 and be difficult to source in person. Carroll loves to see people walk away from their clothing swaps, visibly thrilled to have scored a binder for free.

But even more than that, Carroll loves seeing people make latest friends and find their community at these meetups. “There’s constantly stuff being thrown at trans people,” Carroll indicates. “You have to find people who are similar to you to help support each other.”.

According to recent reports, in Austin, Christabell Nunez wanted to create a safe space for marginalized people of all different body sizes to explore fashion. “It is still so hard to shop for plus-sized people. You really have to scavenge,” Nunez says. “A lot of our trans people, they are getting stared at. They’re getting looked at in retail spaces.”.

It has been revealed that in 2024, Nunez hosted a plus-sized clothing swap in her backyard that was attended by 20 friends. Now that work has expanded into the nonprofit I Slay, which hosts swaps for well over 150 people every month. Everyone is welcome to take as much as they want, Nunez states; the only limitation is that people are asked not to resell the clothes for profit.

“Our mind gets blown every month,” Nunez states. “There’s somebody who flew in from Canada one time to come to our swap.”.

Melissa Grzybowski, head librarian of youth services at the Pflugerville Public Library in central Texas, says the trans clothing-swap program held by the library doesn’t just help the trans community: “It helps everyone.” At one of the library’s first swaps, Grzybowski saw a refugee mother find new clothes for her children after fleeing their country with only two suitcases of belongings.

It has been revealed that in 2021, Texas proposed the highest number of anti-trans laws in the United States. Still, Grzybowski tries to make her programming and literature inclusive. “Public libraries are supposed to be welcoming to all people,” she notes. “We have lots of books that represent the LGBTQ+ experience.”.

A clothing swap attendee browses at Tennessee’s Trans Empowerment Project.

One state over, in Tennessee, Jack Knoxville saw very little representation for trans people when he started a clothing swap back in 2016. At the time, he felt there were only negative representations and ideas of what it meant to be trans in his home state.

Sources indicate that “I’ve been on my own and dealt with being unhoused from the age of 14 on, and had to deal with surviving so many things,” Knoxville notes. “I know what it’s like to be trying so hard to get a job and getting the door shut in your face because your name on paper doesn’t match the perception of your gender with that interviewer.”.

Knoxville states they’ve seen people walk out of their clothing swaps feeling more confident for job interviews and equipped for the cold winter while couch surfing. “It’s the same kind of euphoria that you feel when you have a good haircut… You can feel like you’re on top of the world,” Knoxville says. “Clothing has a huge impact on people and their ability to interact with each other, but then on top of it is that layer of safety and how other people perceive you.”.

Now, with the nonprofit Trans Empowerment Project, Knoxville has helped to show people from across the country how to host clothing swaps in their own cities.

“Queer people especially have to be resilient, and they have to tap into creativity and create something from nothing,” Knoxville says. “We find ways to take what’s left, the crumbs that are given to us, and turn them into celebrations.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home.
  • More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mussels deserve your attention on weeknights. An affordable and accessible protein, they also happen to cook in less time than it takes to boil water. As the bivalves steam, they release a briny liquid, further perfuming the buttery, sake-fortified miso broth. Load up each bowl with a few good ladles, slurping every drop with an assist from crusty bread or warm rice. And why not enjoy the rest of the bottle of sake alongside your meal?

The seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home. Discard any with cracked shells. Gently tap open raw mussels on a counter to see if they slowly close; if they do, those are okay to use. Swish them in a water-filled salad spinner or colander fitted inside a bowl, draining and refilling until water runs clear (give any especially dirty ones a scrub with a sponge). Use a towel to pull off the fibrous beard and set on a towel-lined tray in the fridge until you’re ready to cook.

More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.

In a recent development, place 2 Tbsp. scallions from 8 scallions, thinly sliced on a diagonal, in a small bowl and set aside for serving.

Melt 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add 8 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining scallions to pot and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 2 Tbsp. white miso paste and ½ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (if using) and cook until miso is broken up and incorporated into butter, about 20 seconds. Pour in 1 cup dry sake or dry white wine and stir to combine, then add 3–3½ lb. mussels, scrubbed, debearded. Cover pot and increase heat to medium-high. Cook, shaking pot occasionally, until mussels open, 5–7 minutes (discard any that do not open). Remove pot from heat.

Squeeze 1 lemon half over mussels. Cut remaining 1 lemon half into wedges for serving. Taste broth and season with kosher salt if needed.

Recent findings suggest that ladle mussels and broth among shallow bowls, then scatter reserved scallions over. Serve with country-style bread or steamed white rice if desired and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s official: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond. After months of speculation, it has finally been confirmed that the 40-year-old Brit will slip into 007’s tux.

Probably the most high-profile name on the list of likely contenders, Pattinson may seem, to many, a more logical choice for a Bond villain than 007 himself, but I’d already argued he’d make an excellent franchise lead: The Batman demonstrates that he can be a convincing action hero, and with his weird and wonderful array of projects of late (Dune: Part Three, Primetime, The Odyssey, The Drama, et al), he’s the perfect person to breathe fresh life into this dated cinematic universe.

Industry observers note that last year, Bond fans received seismic news about the future of the classic British spy franchise: Barbara Broccoli and Michael G Wilson—the children of Albert R “Cubby” Broccoli, the legendary producer of the original James Bond films—who have overseen the series since the ’90s, ceded creative control to Amazon Studios. (The streamer bought MGM, the studio which produces the Bond movies, back in 2022, but has now reportedly shelled out an additional $1 billion for the right to freely develop this particular cinematic universe on its own terms.).

Industry observers note that then, a few months later, it emerged that Denis Villeneuve, the Oscar-nominated helmer of the Dune franchise, would be in the director’s chair. After that, we got some more intel, thanks to a report in Deadline. Villeneuve was remarked to have embarked on his search after completing production on Dune: Part Three.” At the time, fans learned he was apparently after “a fresh face”, ideally “an unknown,” possibly “in his late 20s or early 30s.”.

According to reports in Deadline, The Hollywood Reporter and Variety, as well as Pattinson, the final screen tests featured Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, and Nicholas Hoult. Harry Styles allegedly “had discussions about the part,” and Theo James was in the mix at one point, too.

As Pattinson emerges victorious, revisit his major competition below.

According to recent reports, at 36, the Emmy-winning, Southampton-born actor was about the right age, and a beloved star of stage and screen—from Challengers and Disclosure Day to indie hits including God’s Own Country, La Chimera, and The Mastermind, and his latest stint on stage at the Almeida in Golden Boy. Given his impressive acting chops and penchant for working with internationally lauded auteurs, he would have been a high-brow choice in the Daniel Craig mould (lest we forget the latter was a critics’ favorite before he slipped on the tux).

Industry observers note that callum Turner as the next Bond? In many ways it made perfect sense. Dua Lipa’s husband is easy on the eyes and incredibly talented—just see his performances in Emma, Masters of the Air, and The Capture, the latter of which earned the Londoner a BAFTA TV nomination. Though not an unknown, he just about qualified as a fresh face.

His turn as a floppy-haired young intelligence officer in Apple TV+’s Slow Horses saw the gruff Scotsman enter the race, though when asked by British Vogue if he’d consider swapping River Cartwright’s low-key sweatshirts for a tuxedo and martini, he was coy. Of Daniel Craig, whom he grew up watching as 007, the actor remarked: “It’s going to take a long time to get him out of my head. Or anybody else’s.”.

Brilliant in Nosferatu, The Great, and The Favourite, as well as more contemporary projects like The Menu, the 36-year-old from Berkshire had the action credentials (he’s Lex Luthor, after all) and the charisma for the top job.

Since his stint on The White Lotus, the dashing 41-year-old Oxford native had been considered a potential 007 (and The Gentlemen no doubt helped, too).

If you thought the musical superstar’s acting days were already behind him, post Dunkirk, Don’t Worry Darling, and My Policeman, then think again—apparently the opportunity to shrug on 007’s suit might have persuaded him back onto set.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as we inch towards the end of the year, there’s always a massive holiday rush in the sneaker industry (in addition to, well, everywhere else). Annual seasonal drops like the reliable Black Friday and Holiday XI launches from Jordan Brand, plus every major label trying to end the year on the highest note possible, make November and December some of the most exciting times to be a sneakerhead. To be fair, 2026 certainly still has some gas in the tank—plenty of us are already looking ahead to the return of the “Space Jam” Air Jordan 11 next month. Still, this week stands out even in an already crowded release calendar—in fact, I’m inclined to say it’s the biggest and best week of sneaker releases this year has had to offer so far.

Nike and Adidas lead the way with collaborations from massive designers and some up-and-comers alike, including one release that makes a strong argument for being the best sneaker of the year. Reebok’s gradual revitalization takes a massive step in a fun, innovative latest direction. And over at Converse, one of the most reliable celebrity designers in the footwear world is dropping some of his best work yet. Start drafting an apology letter to your credit card for everything you’re about to do with it—these are just a few highlights from the biggest, boldest week of sneakers in 2026 yet.

Who noted anything about Samba fatigue? Turns out all it takes to make one of the most gen-pop shoes of the last decade feel brand new is a take like the one offered this week by Adidas Consortium collaborator Invincible, a Taiwanese brand that’s rapidly establishing itself as a can’t-miss partner for the Three Stripes. Alongside a stellar line of apparel the brand has savvily outmaneuvered any semblance of cultural exhaustion with one of Adidas’s signature silhouettes by keeping it simple: They’ve outfitted the silhouette in a premium black unstructured leather and, bafflingly, a dress shoe sole rather than the Samba’s traditional gum rubber. With perforated Stripes and detailing that mimics those found on dressy leather brogues, it’s an instant contender for sneaker of the year…even if it just barely qualifies as one. This one goes on sale on November13, but with a catch—it’s an Asia exclusive. Pray to the resale market gods.

Nike has been struggling to find their next substantial-name collaborator, but in the meantime, some old favorites are still holding strong. One of those names is Union, the Los Angeles-based boutique founded by streetwear giant Chris Gibbs. This week, the brand is offering a buzzy iteration on the classic Nike Dunk that comes in a luxe brown suede and a heel-less mule silhouette. Like the Invincible Samba, the MO here is that all it takes to make an old shoe feel latest again is a left-of-center take. These are dropping via SNKRS and Union on November 13, for $130 a pop.

According to recent reports, through Reebok’s ups and downs over the last decade, there has been one shining constant: Allen Iverson, the greatest athlete they’ve ever had on their roster. AI’s shoes are always in style, so if the brand simply brought back the original Question Mid silhouette for the shoe’s 30th anniversary, it’d be noteworthy enough. This year, though, they’ve taken the shoe to a upcoming and fairly innovative space, refitting it with modern performance enhancements, making it court-worthy for the first time in decades. Sure, you can still wear them with oversized tees and baggy shorts. But for the first time in ages, the Question could also make it back onto an NBA court (or at least the pavement at your local park). It’s priced at $170 and is available now via Reebok and select retailers.

According to recent reports, ever since he first inked a deal with Converse in 2017, Tyler, the Creator has been one of the best celebrity collaborators in the sneaker biz. This has only become more true since the launch of the 1908 Project last year. The endeavor has seen the pair diving deep into Converse’s archive to revive everything from classic nautical boating shoes, to a jogging silhouette that hadn’t seen the light of day in decades. Ahead of Tyler’s annual Camp Flog Gnaw festival last year, he and Converse launched their best work at the time: the Bronco Boot, a canvas and rubber-toed banger of a sneaker-boot. This year, they’re running it back on a low-top Bronco Boot silhouette—once again ahead of the festival, where we’ll likely see Tyler wearing them. Think of it as the Doc Martens 1461 to the original Bronco Boot’s Doc Martens 1460. Coming your way in four earthy colorways, these are on sale now via Converse.

Speaking of Converse and boots: One of the biggest sneaker stories of the year has been Rick Owens’s return to Adidas after a fruitful stint over at Converse. The designer’s much-anticipated return collection launched this week, with these stunners at the center of the capsule. Debuting on the runway at Paris Fashion Week this past summer, Owens’s Springblade boots are a showstopper of a return. The shoe’s upper is made from a loose textile that fits up over the ankle and a leather toe cap, but the real heat comes in the return of the Springblade sole Owens and Adidas first debuted over ten years ago. They retail for a crazy $850, and can be purchased via the Adidas Confirmed app. Rick’s gonna Rick!

According to recent reports, the biggest night in music is on its way! February 7, 2027, will mark the 69th Grammy Awards, where acts like Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo, Raye, Olivia Dean, Phoebe Bridgers, and Rosalía—who had a fantastic night at the Latin Grammys last week, taking home five awards—will go head-to-head.

Leading the list of contenders is Raye, with 11 nods, followed by Rosalía with nine, and Phoebe Bridgers, Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley, and Olivia Rodrigo, all tied at seven.

Last night, the 2026 Governors Awards served as the official kickoff to the 2027 awards season—and all of Hollywood’s finest came out for the cinematic occasion. One such well-clad star in attendance was the French actor Léa Seydoux, who hit the red carpet in a red, crêpe jersey off-the-shoulder gown by Louis Vuitton, complete with an oversized satin bow at the back. “It was a night to celebrate the people who make us love cinema,” indicates Seydoux of attending the ceremony. “It's about the craft—the people behind the films. That means a lot to me.”.

Recent findings suggest that the star herself has been garnering buzz for her fresh film, Marie Kreutzer’s Gentle Monster, which releases this week. In the dark drama, Seydoux portrays a renowned concert pianist whose life is turned upside down after her husband is arrested for possessing child sexual abuse material. “Marie Kreutzer is a fearless director, and she trusted me with something very delicate,” says Seydoux. “Honestly, at first I was afraid of the subject. But I think when you are afraid, it means maybe you have to do it.” The film served up another challenge for Seydoux, too: It marked her first time having to sing in a project. “It was like jumping from a cliff,” says Seydoux. “And to finally work with Catherine Deneuve—it was a dream!”.

Last look. We kept the hair and makeup very simple—the bob, a red lip—and we let the dress speak.

Given that she has a buzzy new film everyone is talking about, it only made sense that Seydoux went into full-on movie star mode at the Governors Awards last night. She wanted a look that channeled classic Hollywood glamour—and who better to do it custom than Vuitton, who Seydoux has worked with for a decade now. “It’s always like coming home,” says Seydoux of collaborating with the French label. “I wanted something a bit old Hollywood, but clean and modern. And Red, because it’s a night for the cinema: It's joyful, confident, and not shy.”.

Though the powerful color made a statement on its own, Seydoux was also drawn to the striking silhouette of her Vuitton look—courtesy of that major bow. Forget making an entrance, this was a dress that made an exit. “I liked that from the front it's simple, and then when you see the back, there is a surprise,” says Seydoux. “The front of the dress is very pure, just the shape and the satin on the shoulders. And then you turn, and there is this huge bow with the train. It's a bit theatrical, a bit playful—I love it.” She accessorized with the label’s high jewelry pieces.

C'est bow. I think this is my style—quite minimal, but with one strong idea.

Industry observers note that it made for one of the night’s most memorable fashion serves—and the good news is Seydoux has plenty more red carpets to hit in the busy awards season ahead. Gentle Monster hits Netflix on Wednesday, but she also has other projects coming up. “I'm very excited for people to see it,” she indicates. “There is also The Unknown from Arthur Harari, with Neon. And in February, I will be president of the César [Awards], which is a substantial honor for me.”.

Industry observers note that in between all of the premieres and red carpets, however, Seydoux will be trying to squeeze in a little “me time” this fall—back in her native City of Light, of course. “In between, I try to stay home in Paris with my family as much as I can,” she says. “For me this balance is very vital.” One can’t be serving glamour 24/7—even stars need a little break.
