💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • It has been revealed that when it’s really hot or humid out, opening a window or turning on a fan only gets you so far, especially when your house feels like it’s holding onto heat long after the sun goes down.
  • Recent findings suggest that window air conditioning units work by pulling in warm and humid air, cooling and drying it, and sending it back into the room while pushing heat outside.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

It has been revealed that when it’s really hot or humid out, opening a window or turning on a fan only gets you so far, especially when your house feels like it’s holding onto heat long after the sun goes down. If you’ve ever tried to sleep in a hot, airless room, you know how quickly feeling “a little warm” turns into being completely miserable. For homeowners and renters without central air conditioning, the standard solutions are typically ductless air conditioners, freestanding units, or window air conditioners.

Recent findings suggest that window air conditioning units work by pulling in warm and humid air, cooling and drying it, and sending it back into the room while pushing heat outside. Most units double as fans, and many now include dehumidifier modes, which is something you’ll appreciate on those sticky, midsummer days when the air feels truly soupy. And, unlike central air, a window air conditioner can run on a generator during a blackout. That’s a major plus in extreme climates.

The tricky part is finding a window air conditioner that actually fits your space, is easy to install, and doesn’t drive up your energy bill. We looked at a range of models with various features and specs. Some of these we’ve tested hands-on, and a few are newer standouts with great customer reviews. Continue reading to find the window air conditioners that are worth buying right now.

In a recent development, as someone who lives in an older home without ductwork, I’ve owned quite a few window air conditioners over the years in my never-ending quest to find the perfect unit for my house and family. Beyond this personal experience, I worked with a team of testers here at Popular Mechanics to find units on the market that feature reliable construction, notable energy efficiency, quiet operation, and exceptional functionality.

I also spoke with industry expert Kim Lincoln to make sure our recommendations check every box. She’s a third-generation HVAC expert and sales trainer at Service Experts with 25 years of experience.

For the most recent patch, I added three newly introduced products. The GE 14,000-BTU Smart Window Air Conditioner is an excellent air conditioner for cooling spA/Ces up to about 700 square feet (like living rooms or some open space floors). Meanwhile, the LG ThinQ Window Air Conditioner includes the best collection of smart features I’ve seen out of a window AC.

The GE Profile ClearView sits on your windowsill, taking up just a few inches of space while preserving most of your view. This type of AC may not work well in older homes with radiators below the windows, but it’s a great option if you have the clearance space.

Recent findings suggest that we love that you can still fully open the window for fresh air, which is a rare win for a window unit. This AC also uses an inverter compressor for efficient, low-noise cooling, which makes it perfect for offices and nurseries. The digital controls are simple and straightforward, and the app makes it easy to adjust settings without needing to walk over to the unit itself. Installation can be a bit of a project due to its shape and length, so plan on having an extra set of hands close by.

Full GE Profile ClearView Window Air Conditioner Review.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a reason my family owns several of these air conditioners: it’s a no-frills model that’s inexpensive, reliable, and well-sized for rooms up to 150 square feet (most small- to medium-sized bedrooms). My family was gifted one, and we loved it so much that we purchased more for our kids’ bedrooms because the knobs are easy to use and there are no smart features for them to mess with.

Sources indicate that this air conditioner has a simple two-knob control system. The top knob controls the cooling setting, while the bottom knob controls fan speed, and you have the option to run the fan with or without cooling. The appliance’s thermostat cycles the air conditioner on and off to keep the temperature within range based on the temperature you set with the top knob.

The lack of smart tech means it can only be controlled from the knobs. That was a pro for us, but it may be a con for other shoppers. Still, it’s an efficient window unit that won’t hurt your wallet and its washable filter saves you money on having to buy replacements.

Full Frigidaire FFRA051WAE Window Air Conditioner Review.

It has been revealed that this Windmill AC stands out for combining energy efficiency with reliable performance and quiet operation, all of which make it especially useful in bedrooms up to 350 square feet. Its CEER rating of 15 is one of the strongest in this lineup, and the inverter design helps it maintain temperature without the hard stop-start cycling of many traditional window units.

On lower settings, our testing team found it to run subtly enough for overnight use, and we loved how the display dims automatically for better sleep. The fan alone can handle cooler evenings, while hotter days call for full cooling. The app is intuitive and truly smart, letting you adjust settings remotely and sending helpful alerts when it’s time to clean or replace the filter. Maintenance is a key factor in air conditioner longevity, so that’s a huge plus.

According to recent reports, similar in design to our best overall pick, this Midea window unit uses a true U shape so the window can close deeper into the body of the air conditioner. The end benefit is quieter cooling: Once it’s properly installed, the window acts as a sound barrier between the compressor outside and your room inside. That makes it a strong choice for offices up to 350 square feet, where excess noise can become an unwelcome distraction.

Industry observers note that the U shape also means the window does not need to be all the way closed—you can lift the window midway up the body of the unit, and let in air from the outside without uninstalling the entire air conditioner. The biggest issue with this option is that it requires a more skilled hand when installing it, with many customers reporting difficulty doing it themselves.

We’ve been using this beast of an AC to cool the entire first floor of our home with great success for a few summers now. It’s a solid pick for larger rooms up to 700 square feet, per the unit’s specifications, which is about the total square footage of our first-floor foyer, dining room, living room, kitchen, and pantry. Depending on your home’s layout and airflow, it’s hard to guarantee it will successfully and sufficiently cool multiple spaces, but it packs serious power for big rooms, too. That stated, it’s noisier than other models, so take that into consideration.

Sources indicate that while we didn’t need smart features, it’s nice that it connects to Wi-Fi so you can control settings from your phone (or with the included remote), and the interface is straightforward. The unit is designed with energy efficiency in mind, which helps to keep operating costs reasonable for its size. Installation is fairly standard with the included kit, though the unit is heavy, so you’ll want an extra set of hands. It’s likely you’ll need a support bracket, too.

Overall, this is a dependable option for cooling bigger living spaces without overcomplicating things or having to install a mini-split.

If you need an AC that can bring down the temperature rapidly in a medium-sized room, take a look at this model. This smart GE unit impressed our team with speed, cooling a 100-square-foot room from 85 to 75 degrees Fahrenheit in about 15 minutes, and it’s rated for spaces up to 350 square feet. That powerful fan helps move cool air farther into the room, so it’s a good fit if you want quick relief without jumping up to an oversized unit that will drive up energy costs for no reason.

The standout feature here (and the reason for that great performance) is the powerful fan, which kept air moving even when full cooling wasn’t necessary. We love the unit’s eco mode, which cycles the compressor and fan to maintain temperature without overworking the unit. We found the installation to be manageable, but easier with two people. We love that GE includes insulation, though you may need to purchase some additional products to create a perfect seal depending on your window. The main drawback is the app, which was difficult to connect to, despite troubleshooting. Customer service at GE is great, though, and the one-year warranty gives peace of mind.

Read Full GE 8,000 BTU Air Conditioner Review.

This LG 6,000 BTU unit is a strong small-space pick that adds genuinely useful smart features without overcomplicating things. It’s designed for rooms up to about 250 square feet, making it a better option for bedrooms and home offices than larger living areas.

According to recent reports, it pairs easily with LG’s ThinQ app, so you can adjust temperature, fan speed, and schedules from your phone (or with Alexa or Google Assistant). While it’s easy to find an app-controlled window AC these days, this one stands out from the pack a bit. LG has a deeper smart-home ecosystem than most brands manufacturing window ACs, and this model brings that app control, voice-assistant compatibility, scheduling, energy-saver mode, and filter alerts to rooms up to 250 square feet. Customers find the cooling performance is consistent, and the unit includes practical touches like a filter alert and energy saver mode. It’s not the quietest or most powerful option out there, but it balances size, features, and price well for a smart-enabled window AC.

Recent findings suggest that air conditioners are rated in British thermal units (BTUs), which indicate how much space they can effectively cool. A unit that’s too small will run constantly and never quite get there, but one that’s too large will cool too swiftly without removing enough humidity. This leaves the room feeling clammy and uncomfortable.

Recent findings suggest that that’s why several of our superlatives are organized around room size and use case, rather than just standout features. A 5,000-BTU unit may be a smart pick for a small bedroom, dorm room, or compact home office, while an 8,000-BTU model is better suited to a medium-size room where faster cooling and stronger air movement matter. Larger living rooms, open layouts, or rooms with high ceilings may need 10,000 BTUs or more. As a loose rule of thumb, small bedrooms may need around 5,000 to 8,000 BTUs, while larger living areas can require 10,000 BTUs or more. Lincoln indicates the most common concern is choosing a unit that is too small.

“A window unit may be able to knock down the temperature right near the unit, but that doesn’t mean it’s doing a good job across the full area,” claims Lincoln. “In oversized rooms or open floor prepares, I see units run nearly nonstop while still leaving parts of the space warm and damp.” She says that’s when customers note a room feels cool but clammy. “The system may be lowering temperature near the unit, but it isn’t really winning the humidity battle across the space.”.

Recent findings suggest that this also explains why a powerful fan, efficient compressor, or smart app only matters if it supports the way you’ll actually use the A/C. A stronger fan is most helpful when it moves cool air across a medium or large room, while an efficient inverter unit is especially useful in bedrooms or offices where the AC may run for long stretches. Smart controls are most valuable when they make daily use easier, whether that means scheduling, remote adjustments, energy tracking, or filter reminders.

Sources indicate that before you buy, measure your window—twice. Window units are designed for specific opening widths and heights, and some, like casement or sliding windows, require specialized models. Even with careful planning, you may strike out at first.

“Not every window unit fits every window well, even when the box says it should,” says Lincoln. “Consumers need to look at more than width. The window style, the sash opening, the weight of the unit, and the need for support all matter.” A window unit should be level side-to-side and pitched slightly outward so condensed water drains out of the house—not into your room.

In a recent development, it’s notable to consider the unit’s weight, too. Larger units may require a bracket or homemade support to avoid strain and damage to the window and air conditioner.

CEER stands for Combined Energy Efficiency Ratio, and it tells you how efficiently a unit uses electricity over time, not just when it’s actively cooling. Older ratings like EER measure efficiency only while the compressor is running. CEER goes a step further by also factoring in energy used when the unit is idle, like when it’s on standby or cycling on and off throughout the day.

Efficient units use less electricity to deliver the same cooling power, which matters if you’re running the A/C daily through peak summer. Features like programmable timers, eco modes, and inverter technology can further reduce energy use.

When it comes to energy efficiency, Lincoln states it’s just as much about the rating as it is about how you install the unit—specifically how well-sealed the gaps are.

“The best sealing materials are simple, cheap, and worth the effort,” states Lincoln. Foam weatherstripping, rope caulk, and other similar materials can go a long way. “I’ve seen homeowners blame the A/C when the real matter was a half-inch gap letting hot, wet air pour in all afternoon. Sealing is not just about stopping heat. It’s about stopping humidity. And in summer comfort, that distinction matters.”.

If you’re used to old-school window units, you’re familiar with the buzz and crackle as they cool. Thankfully, advancements in technology have resolved that problem a bit. Not all A/Cs are created equal when it comes to sound, though. “Traditional window units tend to be louder because they cycle on and off more abruptly,” shares Lincoln. She says inverter models are often better for bedrooms and offices. An inverter unit works more like a dimmer switch than an on/off switch. Instead of turning the AC off, it slows down once it reaches your desired temperature and maintains it by running at a lower, steady speed. “The difference between a hard compressor kick and a steadier low hum is noticeable when you live with it every night.” We’ve noted this feature on the units we reviewed when applicable.

Industry observers note that check the decibel (dB) rating, too. Units in the low 40s are considered quiet, while anything pushing 60 dB or higher can be disruptive, especially at night.

Modern air conditioners do more than just cool. Remote controls, WiFi connectivity, and app integration let you adjust settings from anywhere. Some units include dehumidifier modes, sleep settings, or directional airflow controls that improve comfort without cranking the temperature.

Lincoln says that the “extras” worth paying for don’t often top the specs list, though. “The features worth paying for aren’t always the flashy ones. A lot of people get distracted by phone apps and forget the basics,” she says of most consumers. “The extra features I’d actually pay attention to are variable-speed operation, a true dry mode if you live in a humid climate, auto-restart after a power outage, and a thermostat or sensor that’s actually useful for where people sit or sleep.”.

“Window units can be efficient, but only if the install is right,” indicates our expert Kim Lincoln. “A poorly sealed window AC is basically paying to cool the air around the leak.”.

With the right setup, though, window air conditioners can be surprisingly efficient — especially compared to cooling an entire home with central air. Window units give you the option of cooling only the rooms you need at that time.

It has been revealed that the key is choosing the right size and looking for models with strong CEER ratings or Energy Star certification. Features like eco mode, programmable timers, and inverter compressors can further reduce energy use by preventing the unit from constantly running at full power.

Industry observers note that BTUs measure cooling power, and getting this right is critical. As a baseline, you’ll need about 20 BTUs per square foot of living space. For example, a 150-square-foot room typically calls for a 5,000–6,000 BTU unit. You should also factor in real-world conditions: increase capacity for sunny rooms, kitchens, or higher ceilings, and scale down slightly for shaded spaces.

According to recent reports, “When people ask how to calculate the right BTU for a room, the honest answer is that manufacturer charts are a starting point, not a finish line,” says Lincoln. “For a window unit, those charts can get you close.” Be careful about over-purchasing power, though. That doesn’t mean your room will be cooler. Oversizing can lead to quick cooling without proper dehumidification, while undersizing can leave the unit running constantly.

Industry observers note that “This is the least glamorous advice and still one of the most important,” says Lincoln. “Clean filters are still one of the biggest performance factors. For window units, the filter should be checked regularly and cleaned about once a month during heavy cooling season, sometimes more often if the home has pets, dust, smoke, renovation debris, or high traffic.”.

Most manufacturer specs recommend cleaning the filter every two to four weeks during periods of heavy use, as well. A clogged filter restricts airflow, which can reduce efficiency and force the unit to work harder. The good news is that most window AC filters are washable—just remove, rinse, let dry, and reinstall. Keeping the filter clean helps maintain strong airflow, improves cooling performance, and can extend the lifespan of the unit. If your AC does not have a washable filter, Lincoln recommends keeping a spare on hand. If your AC does not have smart features or a filter reminder, it’s clutch to add this task to your personal calendar so it is not neglected.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sometimes all it takes to make dinner feel special is a substantial, bold piece of protein. Case in point: This salty-sweet salmon glazed in a glossy teriyaki-style sauce. Brushed in two rounds with the quick sauce made with nothing more than sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and vinegar, the salmon sizzles under the broiler, charring as it takes on a smoky flavor. This recipe calls for one large piece of salmon, but you can use smaller fillets or opt for a white fish such as cod or halibut. Just note that the cooking time will be shorter if using smaller pieces, so keep an eye on them. Add a quick garnish of sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds, and dinner is done.

More salmon winners this way: Hot Honey-Glazed Salmon; Green Curry-Glazed Salmon; and Slow-Roasted Salmon With Harissa.

Recent findings suggest that bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp. unseasoned rice vinegar, and 2 tsp. toasted sesame oil to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat; cook until reduced by half and syrupy, 5–7 minutes. Let sauce cool until thickened slightly, about 10 minutes.

Heat broiler (if broiler is in your oven, place rack in upper third). Season both sides of one 1½–2-lb. skinless or skin-on center-cut salmon fillet with kosher salt. Place, skin side down, in a skillet or baking dish. Transfer one third of sauce to a small bowl and set aside for serving. Brush about half of remaining sauce over fillet. (If the salmon has a lot of room around it in the pan, line with foil to prevent runoff sauce from burning onto pan.).

Broil salmon until sauce is just starting to burn in spots, 4–7 minutes. Brush remaining sauce over fillet and broil until deeply charred and salmon is opaque all the way through, about 5 minutes.

Remove fish from oven and spoon reserved sauce over. Top with thinly sliced scallions and/or toasted sesame seeds if desired.

Latest Update: I Tried The Great British Bake Off’s Most Controversial Recipe—Here’s How It Went

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the “technical challenge,” a blind-baking test where contestants receive the same recipe and ingredients, often with minimal or deliberately sparse instructions, is a staple of The Great British Bake Off.
  • Recent findings suggest that after bakers argued that an hour wasn’t enough, Paul said, “There’s plenty of time.” But fans, critics, and former bakers alike have been plenty vocal about their feelings.
  • It has been revealed that with all the controversy, I was curious to see if the challenge was even possible—so I tried it myself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the “technical challenge,” a blind-baking test where contestants receive the same recipe and ingredients, often with minimal or deliberately sparse instructions, is a staple of The Great British Bake Off. And contestants have seriously struggled with it over the years. But according to Paul Hollywood, this season’s challenge featuring blue cheese and roasted grape flatbreads was the worst yet. After 60 minutes of kneading, grape-roasting, and undercooking, the bakers produced trays of thick, raw flatbreads that Paul and Nigella could barely eat.

Recent findings suggest that after bakers argued that an hour wasn’t enough, Paul said, “There’s plenty of time.” But fans, critics, and former bakers alike have been plenty vocal about their feelings. The popular opinion? The bakers were set up to fail—and also that the flavors seemed a little weird.

It has been revealed that with all the controversy, I was curious to see if the challenge was even possible—so I tried it myself. While I purposefully did NOT watch the episode before my attempt, I did print the full recipe from the GBBO website. This recipe was definitely WAY more helpful than the one the bakers were given, and I followed it to the letter.

Here’s how it went: the good, the bad, and the very ugly.

Recent findings suggest that the beginning? Very smooth. I put the grapes in the oven (the online recipe told me to roast them as a whole bunch rather than cutting them up) and made the bread dough, kneading it for the five minutes specified before letting it rest.

As soon as I set the dough aside to rest, I discovered how absolutely torturous technical downtime is. I was at an absolute loss. I had nothing to do…except read the recipe over and over again and make sure I knew what 8 cm and 23 cm looked like.

According to recent reports, interestingly enough, the bakers on the show didn’t have this downtime; they were busy cutting and roasting their grapes by then. That said, I don’t think that order was necessarily better; with the time spent slicing the grapes, they wouldn’t have had much time at ALL to roast—and not nearly enough to cool.

The grapes came out of the oven. They weren’t very roasted—as one of the bakers said, they just looked like “raw grapes”—but the recipe said 20 minutes and gave no indicators for how roasted they should be (and also I knew they needed to cool before stuffing), so I just went with it.

I dumped out the dough (a rude awakening after its 15-minute rest) and chopped it into eight pieces. Immediately, I realized I should have weighed the larger ball and divided it by eight so I could make sure all the pieces were equal, but I didn’t have much time to fuss, so I tried to make them roughly the same weight and moved on.

The recipe noted to roll out each portion of dough into an 8 cm circle, fill it with five roasted grapes and one-eighth of the blue cheese, lift the edges of the circle up to pinch them together, then turn the little ball seam side down and roll the whole thing out into a 23 cm circle.

I ran into problems immediately.

To begin, I cut my dough into wedges from the larger ball, and it was hard to roll them out into a circle to fill. But that was nothing compared to the problems I had rolling out the filled dough. First, the dough wasn’t rested enough, so it kept springing back at me as I tried to roll it out. But the bigger issue was the grapes. Since they were still pretty juicy, they started bursting as I rolled out the flatbread, flying to the edges and tearing holes in the dough as they oozed out.

After over 15 minutes of stuffing and rolling, my workstation was littered with burst grape guts. None of my flatbreads were 23 cm wide (I think the widest they got was 18?) and I still had three to roll out, but I also knew I needed to start cooking or I was going to have eight totally raw flatbreads at the end of time.

Industry observers note that cooking the flatbreads wasn’t a total disaster—I guess—but grape juice oozed out of the holes where they burst and left black patches of burnt sugar on the pan, which I had absolutely no time to clean out since I was still racing the clock. Fortunately, the flatbreads didn’t seem to need the full 90 seconds per side. In fact, they seemed to need constant attention to prevent them from burning, which was bad news since I was still trying to roll out the remaining three flatbreads on the side.

Sources indicate that time was up, and I had five cooked (burst) stuffed flatbreads on my sheet tray, three totally raw ones on the countertop, and a smoking pan. I now know how the bakers feel at the end of such challenges: slightly insane and utterly defeated.

Recent findings suggest that looking back on the challenge, I can honestly say that it was difficult and somewhat impossible. Ultimately, I couldn’t get all the flatbreads cooked in time, even though I was rolling them out much thinner than the bakers were. But while timing was definitely a problem, the bigger problem was the impossible stupidity of stuffing juicy grapes inside a flatbread and then trying to roll it out without the grapes bursting out and ruining the dough.

Since I managed to cook five flatbreads, I could (unlike Paul and Nigella) taste the finished result—but honestly, I wasn’t a fan. The blue cheese was WAY too strong, and the grapes felt like random pockets of juice in an otherwise savory flatbread. Overall, I wouldn’t recommend trying this challenge yourself—unless you want to be scrubbing the burnt bits of grape sugar off your pan for the next week.

Hot Honey Brussels Sprouts

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that these honey-glazed brussels sprouts are saucy, tangy-sweet, and have a bit of kick.
  • In a recent development, the trick to perfectly charred brussels sprouts?
  • Make the glaze while the sprouts roast or up to five days ahead, then toss everything together just before serving to preserve those crispy edges.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that these honey-glazed brussels sprouts are saucy, tangy-sweet, and have a bit of kick. Caramelizing the honey gives it a deeper, toastier sweetness. Vinegar, red pepper flakes, and a good dose of butter transform it into a sticky sauce that seeps into the nooks of each and every sprout. The recipe makes a generous amount: Use it all, or save some for drizzling on pizza a few days later.

In a recent development, the trick to perfectly charred brussels sprouts? Preheat the sheet pan, then arrange the halved sprouts cut side down on the hot metal. It might feel a little fussy flipping each sprout onto its flat side, but the deeply browned results are worth it.

Make the glaze while the sprouts roast or up to five days ahead, then toss everything together just before serving to preserve those crispy edges.

How thick should the hot honey glaze be?

According to recent reports, glossy and pourable, about the consistency of warm maple syrup—not thick like caramel. The honey will foam as it cooks, and the mixture will bubble aggressively when you add the vinegar. Both are normal. The glaze will thicken a bit as it cools, so don’t worry if it seems slightly thin while still bubbling.

They have a noticeable kick, but they’re more tangy-sweet than fiery. The honey and butter temper the chile flakes. If you’re sensitive to spice, use less than the suggested ¾ tsp. or leave the flakes out entirely.

According to recent reports, place a rimmed baking sheet on bottom rack of oven; preheat to 450°. Toss 1½ lb. brussels sprouts, trimmed, halved, and ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil in a large bowl; sprinkle with ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and season with freshly ground black pepper.

According to recent reports, carefully remove baking sheet from oven. Using tongs, arrange brussels sprouts cut-side down on hot baking sheet. Roast brussels on bottom rack until softened and deeply browned, 15–25 minutes.

Meanwhile, bring ¼ cup honey to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring often, until honey is a deep amber color but not burnt (it will be foamy, that’s okay), 3–4 minutes.

Industry observers note that remove from heat and add ⅓ cup sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar (it will bubble up quite aggressively) and ¾ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes; whisk until sauce is smooth. Return saucepan to medium heat and add 3 Tbsp. unsalted butter and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt. Cook, whisking constantly, until glaze is glossy, bubbling, and slightly thickened, 3–4 minutes.

It has been revealed that transfer roasted brussels sprouts to a large bowl. Add half the hot honey glaze and scallions and toss to combine. Taste and add more glaze if desired. Transfer to a platter and top with lemon zest. Serve remaining glaze alongside.

Do ahead: Glaze can be made 5 days ahead; refrigerate after cooling.

40 More Million-Dollar Watches Just Sold at Auction

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Back in June, I reported on the bonanza of watches crossing the million-dollar-plus mark at auction.
  • In just the first half of 2026, the number of million-dollar watches sold nearly eclipsed the total from all of 2025.
  • According to recent reports, if you’re keeping score at home, we’ve seen 133 watches sell at or above seven figures this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Back in June, I reported on the bonanza of watches crossing the million-dollar-plus mark at auction. What once felt like a unicorn price for watchmakers, auction houses, and the industry as a whole no longer feels so magical. “I joke with people that $1 million is like the new $250,000 of five years ago,” Paul Boutros of Phillips auction house mentioned over the summer.

In just the first half of 2026, the number of million-dollar watches sold nearly eclipsed the total from all of 2025. Now, after a raft of high-profile auctions in Geneva a couple of weeks ago, the industry has set yet another record. In just the last month alone (including Monaco Legend Group, which kicked things off in late October), 40 million-dollar watches hammered, according to numbers provided by EveryWatch. That’s more sold than in any entire year before 2020.

According to recent reports, if you’re keeping score at home, we’ve seen 133 watches sell at or above seven figures this year. And we’ve still got plenty of year left.

In a recent development, the question is: How much steam does the auction world have left? And what’s driving this radical spike in big-ticket timepieces?

Recent findings suggest that A $10 million Patek Philippe Perpetual Calendar Chronograph ref. 2499.

According to recent reports, mike Nouveau, WatchTok King and dealer, has told me that if more kids knew how much growth potential there is in the vintage market, they’d put down the creator-style tiny microphones and start studying reference numbers. The vintage market spiked in the middle of the pandemic, when prices on sport watch grails like the Patek Philippe Nautilus and Rolex Daytona went crypto-mode as a new wave of speculators flooded the high-end collecting scene.

Industry observers note that but while the steel sport watch craze has cooled—or at least leveled off—the market has continued riding a remarkably durable wave, helped in part by the arrival of a previously quiet category: the insiders-only independent brands. “For many years at auction, we always mentioned, ‘You have Patek Philippe and Rolex. What’s the third brand that can compete?’” Alexandre Ghotbi, a deputy chairman at Phillips auction house, told me in 2024 for a story on the beloved watchmaker Rexhep Rexhepi. “Today’s third brand is not a brand—it’s a genre: independent artisanal watchmakers.”.

It has been revealed that think F.P. Journe, Berneron, Phillipe Dufour, Rexhepi’s Atelier Akrivia—companies helmed by watchmaking auteurs turning out hyper-limited runs, most of which sell out long before a perfectly-lit product photo ever hits the web. Oftentimes, the only way to get your hands on one of their wares—if you haven’t yet achieved friend-of-the-brand status—is by raising a paddle at auction.

According to recent reports, when I asked dealer Eric Wind if he thought the indie insanity would remain strong, he was unequivocal: “At the top end, yes.” The dealer Zoe Abelson, of Graal Watches, actually believes we haven’t reached the peak yet. “I do think there's still room for the pieces that are actually rare to continue to grow in value with a continuance in new interest in collecting watches and the yearning to build the most impressive collection,” she said.

It has been revealed that two weekends ago, a fresh independent brand joined the list of million-dollar watchmakers. Sylvain Pinaud cut his teeth restoring antique watches and established his eponymous brand in 2018. He’s known for showing his work—the instrumental components of his watches are often highlighted on the dial. A unique version of his Origine, a model that only introduced in 2022, sold for 1,011,200 Swiss francs (roughly $1,211,500).

Pinaud’s success is indicative of what happens to the elite independent brands that hit the substantial time. Compared to many of the heavyweight Swiss makers working at scale, independent watchmakers are seen as artisans who hand-produce their designs in extremely limited quantities. It’s why a watchmaker like Kari Voutilainen, considered a master of his craft, has sold more million-dollar pieces this year than many of the big fellas getting rap lyric shoutouts. “There's a growing appreciation for what these watchmakers are producing,” mentioned Ben Horesh, EveryWatch’s CEO. “It’s great to see more independents challenging the old guard.".

Look at that list above. Voutilainen ranks just after Rolex and Patek Philippe but ahead of Cartier for the most million-dollar watches sold at auction in 2026. The list is heavy on independents, including Rexhepi’s Akrivia, George Daniels, Philippe Dufour, and Vianney Halter. The real headline, though, is seeing F.P. Journe—the godfather of the indie scene—at the very top. If one area of the market doesn’t feel entirely sustainable, it’s the inferno around FPJ’s pieces. For deep-pocketed newcomers to the “hobby” of catching major-ticket whales, the Geneva-based maker has come to represent the grailiest of grails. Nearly every Journe piece that comes to auction sells for multiples of its estimate. And I mean everything: an empty watch box made for a set of FPJs sold for $230,000 at Christie’s! “The less rare—or in Journe's case, current production—pieces that get swept up in the overall market growth will slow down soon,” Abelson mentioned. “I don't think it's sustainable; at a certain point the values will price out enough people that there should be a correction.”.

Would you pay $230,000 for this box?

Industry observers note that A $13 million F.P. Journe Chronomètre à Résonance "Régence”.

In a recent development, if six-figure watches were once rare, 10-million-plus pieces were true spectacles. Between 2020 and 2023, not a single watch crossed that threshold. In the last decade, from 2015 to 2025, there were just seven 10-million watches total. But with some time still on the clock, seven watches have already topped that threshold in 2026. A solid chunk of that is thanks to the wild one-of-one Daytonas that Rolex made for a charity auction—three out of the four sold for seven figures—but it’s still an astounding feat. The rest of the list is filled out by:.

These days, it’s hard to find a category of watches that isn’t doing well at auction. Cartier hasn’t fallen off—in fact, the brand keeps setting records: a very cool clock known as Portico No. 4 hammered for approximately $5,768,400 at Phillips the weekend before last, becoming the most expensive Cartier ever sold in the process. Breguet is, rightfully and finally, on the rise. And after relaunching just last summer, Urban Jürgensen’s vintage pieces are hotter than ever. A super sexy pink-gold version of the brand’s Reference 2 went for 358,400 Swiss francs (about $430,000) at Sotheby’s.

To put a fine point on all this, just look at how overall sales are soaring. Last year, Phillips set the record with $83,018,538 worth of timepieces sold in a single auction. It only took 12 months to shatter that number. This month saw Phillips reset the record with a $112.3 million auction. I would say 2026 is an inflection point for the industry…if I didn’t anticipate that we’ll be back here talking about even more record-setting sales every year for the foreseeable future.

Chili Crisp Yogurt Chicken

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (414 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior.
  • More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.
  • Industry observers note that preheat oven to 425°.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior. But the best part of this sheet-pan dinner comes after the chicken is cooked: Spread cooked rice into the pan’s juices, then slide the baking sheet back into the oven. As the rice soaks up the deeply savory sauce, it will crisp in spots, creating a texture that’s somewhere between chewy-fluffy steamed grains and a freshly toasted pita chip. And when it comes to chili crisp, we love the iconic and easy-to-source Lao Gan Ma, but specialty brands like Fly By Jing are great too—just make sure the one you use is not too spicy, which will overpower the dish.

More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

Industry observers note that preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

According to recent reports, arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.

Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

Meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

Recent findings suggest that combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a big pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.

Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

While traditional stuffing is technically supposed to be stuffed inside the turkey to cook, that isn’t actually the ideal or even recommended way to cook your Thanksgiving turkey (or stuffing). I've found that you’ll achieve much better results by cooking them separately. By cooking your stuffing in a baking dish, you get crunchy, buttery pieces of bread on top and soft, bread pudding-esque pieces underneath. It's my perfect version of the holiday side—I tested it again and again, so it was worthy of your Thanksgiving table.

Industry observers note that what People Are Saying:"[It's] an excellent recipe you can tweak it for taste. I like to up the onion by half again and use a lot more fresh sage." - GreenClover.

According to recent reports, "Using a [mandoline] made the final preparation fast and easy. It was a significant hit over a lovely meal. The dressing brought high praise from two trained chefs." - RedFish.

As I mentioned above, sourdough bread is my go-to for stuffing. The first step is to bake it! You'll need 2 sheets, or do this in batches. You want to dry it out, so bake for 15 to 20 minutes.

Industry observers note that while that's toasting, it's time to cook the aromatics. Melt some butter, then cook the onions, leeks, and garlic until your kitchen smells amazing and everything is softened.

It has been revealed that time for the liquids: Simply whisk eggs, broth, milk, and some fresh herbs in a large measuring cup. You can use a touch of red pepper for a hint of spice, which I highly recommend, but if you have a spice-averse crowd, you can skip it.

When the bread is done toasting, turn the oven temp up to 375°. Prepare a 13" x 9" baking dish by coating it with a thin layer of butter.

It has been revealed that time to combine it all together: In a large bowl, mix the bread, aromatics, and liquid ingredients and toss until combined. You can let this sit at room temperature for up to 1 hour if you're planning ahead. Dot with even more butter, then bake until crispy. You can serve this stuffing warm or at room temperature.

Few jackets have managed to cross as many style tribes—and decades—as the Harrington. In fact, if you were to enroll in Classic Menswear 101, the Harrington jacket would be a prerequisite. The transitional season staple—a favorite of Elvis, James Dean, Steve McQueen, and every member of The Clash—is constantly found across lookbooks and style Instagram accounts, because it does so many things so well.

Sources indicate that for one, it's incredibly practical: Water-resistant, pocket-forward, lightly insulating, and ever-adaptable to the day's conditions thanks to its full-zip and collar. But the almost-cropped length—and popped collar, if you so dare—is also a style swerve that makes every wearer feel one dose cooler than they did before. No wonder it’s been embraced over the decades by everyone from golfers to preppies to A-Listers and punks.

Recent findings suggest that the original Harrington—a Baracuta G9—is still available almost a century on from its release, and still excellent. But if you’re looking to broaden your horizons, today’s Harrington jackets aren’t resting on their laurels. Below, the standout versions worth adding to your rotation before we’re into parka territory.

The classic Baracuta G9 golf jacket is as British as beans on toast. This is the original tartan-lined, ribbed-cuff Harrington, the jacket you picture when you think of Steve McQueen or Paul Newman, and the brand that insider-y menswear favorites like Engineered Garments and Noah have collaborated with when they wanted to make Harringtons of their own. Baracuta got its start making raincoats for other brands—Burberry included—before branching out with its own designs, and the G9 is still made in England today. Crafted from a water-resistant cotton-poly blend, and featuring the signature Fraser tartan lining and iconic umbrella back yoke (which keeps rain off your back while letting air circulate) it really doesn't get any better than this.

In a recent development, uniqlo delivers a whole Harrington jacket without sacrificing anything, and in fact saves you some precious dollars along the way. We’re talking a slightly cropped, slightly relaxed silhouette, a touch of stretch, classic slant pockets and even a genre-affirming plaid lining. And while it’s not water-resistant like some other options, it makes up for it with a durable cotton fabric that’ll dry off in no time, and still keep you protected from a few unforeseen raindrops. If you’re after the workaday Harrington aesthetic without spending a lot, this one gets the job done and then some.

According to recent reports, if you're looking to purchase a Harrington jacket that'll serve you for seasons to come, but don't particularly want to spend half your rent check on it, J.Crew's faithful take on the Harrington is as true as it gets. And this is no compromise pick: It still comes with plenty of details to get excited about, from the handsome, buttoned interior chest pocket to the warming full lining, leather zip tag, and 10-ounce cotton twill that's already been washed a few times by the brand to make it feel lived-in and well-loved from the jump. It also comes in multiple colors, partly because J.Crew is confident you'll be back for more. Oh, and if you want a winterized Harrington, check out the corduroy iteration, which also has a quilted, Primaloft-stuffed lining.

A pared-down, easygoing take on the classics, Quince’s Harrington strikes a smart balance of polished and sporty, without even the faintest fuss. Offered in khaki, navy and black, this one is the modern minimalist’s Harrington—a clean, contemporary style that does what a staple should do: make you look good without causing a scene. Oh, and that twill outer will break in wonderfully over time, in case you were wondering.

One of the best parts about a Harrington Jacket is that the idea is fully formed. As such, it can be a hard style to riff on, mostly because the source material is so dialed in that it’s often best to leave well enough alone. Ernest W. Baker designers Reid Baker and Inês Amorim, however, couldn’t care less about that tradition and went nuclear with this one: it’s a true-blue Harrington complete with a cropped fit, ribbing at the waist, barrel cuffs and a point collar. But then the inclusion of a leather collar and Western-inspired yoke details in lieu of the classic back vent turns it into something else entirely, without changing the fit one bit. And they nailed it. It’s transformative without being performative, utterly distinct and eminently familiar and, most improbably, contradiction free.

This has most of the trappings of your classic Harrington—stand collar, cool back vent, functional cuffs—but it also eschews the classic ribbed hem for a cinched waist, which adds a little bit of drama to the notoriously no-drama silhouette.

In a recent development, todd Snyder often plays it straight—Ivy-ish classics with just the right details. Here, they’ve ditched part of the trad playbook and leaned into the modern with water-resistant tech cotton-nylon blend, but it's also a bit cropped and fits very much like you'd remember. And now, it's also on sale.

A Harrington is already pretty pared down, but Barbour trimmed every ounce of fat on this one, leaving us with a slightly longer silhouette, all the *essential* bells and whistles and a brown cotton outer that gets to take center stage.

We could get into the buttery leather collar or the insane Italian wool serge fabric that Wanze deployed on this stunner, or even lock in on that two-way RiRi zipper, but that'd be burying the lede because you're not going to get a red like this anywhere else.

We wouldn't typically include different versions of the same style in one guide, but when our Best Overall version also comes in a buttery suede, exceptions are made.

Stone Island traffics in the unexpected, so, in a way, it should come as no surprise that the Italian label's take on the classic is a Gonzo, teched-out one—one made with a garment-dyed fabric that's been treated with an "anti-drop" finish.

According to recent reports, the Harrington is an icon of preppy style, so of course Ralph Lauren has blessed us with its lightweight cotton take, complete with the signature Polo pony on the chest. It’s preppy, American, and exactly the kind of jacket your kids will proudly say “This used to be my Dad’s” about.

You might not think of a Harrington as a "winter jacket," but hear us out: it can be. This Percival joint, for instance, is made out of a hardy birdseye wool blend that will hold up to some chilly weather and layer up nicely when calling things "chilly" is understatement.

Why is it called a Harrington jacket?

Recent findings suggest that the funniest thing about the Harrington? It wasn’t originally called a Harrington at all. The original—and, as you've read above, our favorite—was called the “G9.” It was cooked up by Baracuta in 1937 in rainy old Manchester, England, as a golf jacket—the “G” stands for “golf.” (The idea was to make a garment that could take a beating from British weather without cramping your backswing.) But the jacket earned its now-iconic name thanks to Rodney Harrington, a character from the 1960s TV show Peyton Place, who wore one so often that the name just stuck.

How should a Harrington jacket fit?

The traditional Harrington jacket fits close to the shoulders and chest, but still has enough room for a full range of arm motion—it is a golfing style, after all. The hem then typically sits either at the waist, or for a more stylized look, just above the belt line. It should be easy to spot from product shots whether the designer in question has stuck to this traditional shape, or elongated the style a touch. From that point, the only thing left to consider is whether you initiative to wear it over thick sweaters, or lighter T-shirts and shirts. If it's the former, you may want to consider sizing up.

In a recent development, style is subjective, we know—that’s the fun of it. But we’re serious about helping our audience get dressed. Whether it’s the best white sneakers, the flyest affordable suits, or the need-to-know menswear drops of the week, GQ Recommends’ perspective is built on years of hands-on experience, an insider awareness of what’s in and what’s next, and a mission to find the best version of everything out there, at every price point.

Sources indicate that our staffers aren’t able to try on every single piece of clothing you read about on GQ.com (fashion moves fast these days), but we have an intimate knowledge of each brand’s strengths and know the hallmarks of quality clothing—from materials and sourcing, to craftsmanship, to sustainability efforts that aren’t just greenwashing. GQ Recommends heavily emphasizes our own editorial experience with those brands, how they make their clothes, and how those clothes have been reviewed by customers. Bottom line: GQ wouldn’t tell you to wear it if we wouldn’t.

We make every effort to cast as wide of a net as possible, with an eye on identifying the best options across three key categories: quality, fit, and price.

Recent findings suggest that to kick off the process, we enlist the GQ Recommends braintrust to vote on our contenders. Some of the folks involved have worked in retail, slinging clothes to the masses; others have toiled for small-batch menswear labels; all spend way too much time thinking about what hangs in their closets.

It has been revealed that we lean on that collective experience to guide our search, culling a mix of household names, indie favorites, and the artisanal imprints on the bleeding-edge of the genre. Then we narrow down the assortment to the picks that scored the highest across quality, fit, and price.

Across the majority of our buying guides, our team boasts firsthand experience with the bulk of our selects, but a handful are totally new to us. So after several months of intense debate, we tally the votes, collate the anecdotal evidence, and emerge with a list of what we believe to be the absolute best of the category right now, from the tried-and-true stalwarts to the modern disruptors, the affordable beaters to the wildly expensive (but wildly worth-it) designer riffs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that this sausage stuffing has everything you want on your Thanksgiving plate: crisp, craggy edges, a plush, savory center, and plenty of browned sausage throughout. Torn pieces of country-style bread soak up the broth and eggs without falling apart, turning golden and crunchy on top while staying tender underneath.

Industry observers note that breakfast sausage does much of the heavy lifting. Once browned, its drippings join plenty of butter to cook the onions, celery, and garlic. Fresh sage, parsley, and thyme bring balance, while optional fennel seeds add a little extra aromatic punch.

What kind of sausage should I use?

Uncooked pork breakfast sausage is the first choice. Typically seasoned with sage and black pepper, it brings familiar Thanksgiving flavors and plenty of richness. For some heat, choose spicy breakfast sausage. If you can't find the packaged kind or want to avoid pork, try making your own with our breakfast sausage recipe, using ground dark-meat turkey in place of pork.

This stuffing relies on the fat from breakfast sausage for its flavor. Want a vegetarian version? Our Simple-Is-Best Stuffing is a long-standing reader favorite and was the inspiration for this version; use that recipe with vegetable broth for a meat-free stuffing.

What’s the best bread for sausage stuffing?

According to recent reports, look for a sturdy country-style white loaf or sourdough with a relatively thin crust. Avoid soft sandwich bread, which can turn mushy, and very crusty artisan loaves, which won’t absorb the broth as readily. Even if your bread is a day or two old, don’t skip drying it in the oven—that’s what helps the stuffing hold its shape.

Can I make sausage stuffing ahead of time?

You can dry the bread a day ahead and store it loosely covered at room temperature. For more ways to get ahead of Thanksgiving, including cooking, refrigerating, and reheating stuffing, see our make-ahead stuffing guide.

Made In 9-x-13-inch Baking Dish.

Sources indicate that place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 350°. Grease a 13x9" baking dish with unsalted butter. Arrange one 1–1¼-lb. loaf country-style white bread, torn into 1" pieces, in a single layer on a large rimmed baking sheet and bake until dried out and golden around the edges, 30–40 minutes. Let cool.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, melt 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high heat. Cook 1 lb. breakfast sausage, casings removed if needed, stirring and breaking into small pieces, until well browned and cooked through, 8–10 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer sausage to a small plate, leaving fat behind.

Reduce dial to medium heat and add remaining 8 Tbsp. unsalted butter to fat in pot; heat until melted. Cook 2 medium onions, finely chopped, 6 celery stalks, finely chopped, 8 garlic cloves, coarsely chopped, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. fennel seeds (if using), stirring occasionally, until onions are softened and golden around the edges, 12–15 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth along with sausage, ½ cup (packed) coarsely chopped parsley, 2 Tbsp. finely chopped sage, 2 Tbsp. finely chopped thyme, and ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper.

Sources indicate that whisk 3 large eggs and remaining 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth in a small bowl to combine, then stir into pot (don’t worry, eggs won’t scramble). Add bread to pot and toss gently to combine. Let sit, tossing occasionally, until liquid is almost completely absorbed, about 10 minutes.

Sources indicate that transfer stuffing to prepared dish (don’t pack or press down) and cover loosely with foil. Place dish on a clean large rimmed baking sheet and bake until stuffing is hot throughout (an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should register 160°), 35–45 minutes. Increase oven temperature to 400° and remove foil (no need to remove stuffing from oven while heat increases). Continue to bake until stuffing is light golden brown on top, 25–30 minutes longer.

Sources indicate that do Ahead: Bread can be baked 1 day ahead; store loosely covered at room temperature. Stuffing can be assembled 1 day ahead; cover and chill. Bring to room temperature before baking.

Industry observers note that this is a Japanese-style rice porridge known as okayu. I ate this every morning in the early weeks of postpartum after my first daughter was born. It’s what our family reaches for whenever we need a simple, nourishing dish that warms from the inside out. For the smoothest porridge, let the rice soak in cold water before cooking.

Industry observers note that if you have time, soak the rice, which makes the texture softer and can aid in digestion. Place washed rice in a bowl and pour in water to cover by 1". Soak at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours. Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

Industry observers note that in The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

In a recent development, combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

Industry observers note that remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

Everything You Need to Know About Korean Scalp Scalers

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1208 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’ve ever been to a Korean head spa, you know it’s less a hair wash than a full reset.
  • It has been revealed that you don’t need a spa appointment to get the same effect, though.
  • Below, experts explain what a scalp scaler does, who should use one, how to avoid overdoing it, and which formulas are worth trying.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve ever been to a Korean head spa, you know it’s less a hair wash than a full reset. Before reaching for the shampoo, a technician typically examines your scalp with a magnifying camera, then applies a treatment to loosen the oil, dead skin, and product residue a regular wash leaves behind. It’s the step that makes your hair feel impossibly light afterward, and it’s called scaling.

It has been revealed that you don’t need a spa appointment to get the same effect, though. Scalp scalers bring that deep clean home, whether that’s an acid-based treatment you leave on before shampooing or a salt scrub that lathers up in the shower. They’re especially useful if you lean on dry shampoo, work out often, or have fine hair that goes flat a day after washing.

Below, experts explain what a scalp scaler does, who should use one, how to avoid overdoing it, and which formulas are worth trying.

It has been revealed that the name actually comes from the dentist’s office. “In Korean, ‘scaling’ is the same word we use for dental cleaning,” claims Ellie Byun, a doctor of Korean medicine and licensed acupuncturist. “Plaque builds up on your teeth even when you brush, and in the same way, oil and dead skin build up on your scalp even when you shampoo.” For many Korean women, it’s a familiar routine. “I’ve been using scalp scalers since high school,” says Kristin Lim, founder of Base-K.

Some scalers work differently from regular shampoos because they require additional time on the scalp. “A clarifying shampoo only cleanses during the short time it’s on your scalp,” Dr. Byun says. “A scaler stays on for several minutes and chemically dissolves dead skin and oil with acids and enzymes—the same principle as an exfoliating toner for your face.”.

That’s true of some chemical scalers, but others, including several below, use salt granules instead of acids, or a combination of chemical and physical exfoliants. “A scalp scaler focuses on loosening dead skin and buildup, using acids, physical exfoliants, or a combination of both,” Lim notes.

Sources indicate that if you go the gritty route, keep it gentle. “A scrub physically buffs the surface with grains, and if you use it too often, it can make the scalp barrier sensitive,” Dr. Byun says. “It’s especially good for oily scalps, flaking caused by buildup, fine hair that goes flat swiftly, people who use a lot of dry shampoo and styling products, and anyone who sweats a lot.”.

Flaking is where it gets tricky, though. “It can also help loosen surface flakes, but persistent flaking and itching deserve a closer look,” Lim notes. “Dandruff and other scalp conditions may need targeted treatment rather than more exfoliation.”.

The first thing most people notice is how light their hair feels afterward. “Removing that residue can leave the scalp feeling cleaner and the hair feeling lighter,” Lim notes. With regular use, it can reduce oil and flaking. Some research suggests that exfoliating ingredients can help address scalp flaking and discomfort. In one small study, a four-week regimen containing salicylic acid and other scalp-care ingredients improved dandruff, itching, redness, and oiliness in people with seborrheic dermatitis. However, the results don’t necessarily apply to every scalp scaler. Improving scalp health may also benefit hair quality over time. “Studies show that when scalp health declines, hair quality declines too, and when the scalp recovers, hair quality recovers with it,” Dr. Byun says.

The biggest risk is doing too much. “Over-exfoliating weakens the scalp barrier and can cause irritation, dryness, and even a rebound increase in oil,” Dr. Byun says. It’s not the right fit for every scalp, either. “Individuals with sensitive or irritated scalps should approach exfoliating treatments cautiously,” says Joe Cho, team lead of media relations at Medicube. Even a product labeled gentle may cause problems. “Even a gentle formula may not suit a scalp that’s actively inflamed,” Lim says. If something feels off, don’t push through it. “If you notice sudden heavy shedding, pain, or lesions, see a professional,” Dr. Byun says.

“Some scalers go onto a dry or damp scalp before shampooing, while others are used on wet hair as part of the wash,” Lim says. Either way, the product needs to reach your scalp, not just your hair. “Part your hair in sections about an inch apart and apply it directly to the scalp along each part,” Dr. Byun says. “Then massage with your fingertips, never your nails, for two to three minutes, pressing slowly on the crown and the base of the skull.” Then rinse it out on time. “Leaving it on longer or scrubbing harder won’t improve the result,” Lim says. Because formulas vary, follow the timing and application instructions on your particular product.

According to recent reports, less is more when it comes to frequency too. “I recommend once a week for oily scalps and once every two weeks for normal or dry scalps,” Dr. Byun says. Your scalp will tell you when you’ve gone too far. “Signs you’re overdoing it include tightness, stinging, redness, or tenderness, more flaking instead of less, upcoming itching, or a scalp that feels oilier than before.” Lim also recommends sticking to one exfoliant at a time and avoiding combining several scalp exfoliants in the same wash.

Afterward, think of your scalp the way you’d think about your face after an exfoliating toner. “Korean care follows a simple idea—clear first, then nourish,” Dr. Byun indicates. “Use a mild, low-pH shampoo, then a lightweight scalp serum with niacinamide, panthenol, or centella, and apply conditioner only from the midlengths to the ends.”.

Recent findings suggest that not directly. “While scalp health plays an key role in overall hair care, there’s presently limited clinical evidence that scalp exfoliation alone can directly stimulate hair growth or prevent shedding,” Cho states. Dr. Byun sees it as groundwork. “A scaler doesn’t grow hair on its own, but it does have a real, research-backed role,” she says. “So I see scaling as the first step in creating an environment where healthy hair can grow.” Lim is just as clear: “Promising that a scaler alone will regrow hair or stop shedding would be overpromising.”.

Many scalp scalers can be used on color-treated hair, but it’s important to check the product’s instructions, since some exfoliating ingredients and cleansing formulas may affect color longevity. “It’s generally fine on color-treated hair as long as you apply it to the scalp, not the hair itself,” Dr. Byun says.

When we test and review a product, we take a holistic approach to deliver well-rounded product recommendations. First, we lean on Vogue’s vast network of experts—from board-certified dermatologists to celebrity estheticians—for professional insight into the industry’s standout products these specialists would use themselves or recommend to their clients. We pair their expertise with our editorial best practices to curate the thoughtful edits you read on our site.

For Korean scalp scalers, we selected the best based on the following characteristics: ingredients, exfoliant type, texture, packaging, finish, and the hair-care concerns they address. To do this, we paired our personal tests of each formula with expert guidance and reviewer insights to determine which we would recommend. Read more about our testing methodology here.

It has been revealed that when shopping for a cheap washing machine, you’ll need to decide whether you want a full-size, portable, or manual model. Most of the full-size options you’ll find under $1,000 are top-loading washers, and they offer a large capacity as well as more settings and cycles. For those with limited space, portable washing machines have a more compact footprint and can easily be stored in a closet. However, these machines typically require a faucet connection for operation and don’t always wring out your clothes, making them trickier to dry.

Sources indicate that finally, manual washing machines are the most affordable, but they require a bit of elbow grease for operation. You usually have to crank or agitate the machine by hand, but these models don’t require electricity, making them ideal for camping or off-the-grid living.

In a recent development, the capacity of washing machines is generally measured in cubic feet. Most standard-size appliances have a capacity of 3.5 to 5 cubic feet and are suitable for average households. For reference, a washer with a capacity of 4.5 cubic feet can wash a king-size comforter. If you have a small household, you’ll likely be fine with a smaller-capacity washing machine. A compact machine with 2.3 cubic feet can wash about 6 towels.

Cheap washing machines often have fewer wash cycles than more expensive models. In general, you’ll find most affordable washers have between eight and 12 wash cycles, including standard ones like quick or light wash, delicates, and heavy-duty. There are also several temperature settings on most washers, and some allow you to select the water level and soil level as well. These basics are generally sufficient for most loads of laundry, but if you want more advanced settings—such as sanitization or fabric-specific cycles—you may need to spend a little extra.

According to recent reports, to help save money on operation costs, you may want to look for a high-efficiency washing machine, frequently abbreviated as HE. These models use 20 to 66 percent less water, saving around 6,000 gallons of water per year for an average family. You may also want to look for an Energy Star-certified appliance, which uses 25 percent less energy than standard models.

Recent findings suggest that the trade-offs at lower price points are less about cleaning power and more about small details. “You are usually giving up fabric care refinement and overall build quality rather than basic cleaning performance,” Chernoff notes.

In a recent development, that means simpler drum movement, fewer specialty cycles, and suspension systems that don’t dampen vibration as well. Over the years, a pricier washer tends to be gentler on your clothes, but for most people washing everyday loads, a more affordable model gets the job done.

A cheap washer doesn’t automatically mean higher utility bills. “Many affordable modern models are still quite efficient, especially if they carry an Energy Star certification,” Chernoff indicates. In a recent development, between sniffing out paternal autism and perfecting his Robert F. Kennedy impression, you may have noticed that John Mulaney was wearing an extraordinary watch while hosting Saturday Night Live this weekend. It’s a beauty—a gold vintage Patek Philippe with swoopy Breguet numerals—but its backstory is even more impressive. On December 12, 1948, Fresh York Yankees legend Joe DiMaggio purchased this timepiece and owned it until his death in 1999.

The Patek Philippe, a ref. 130 circa 1947, is already a rare bird before you add in its Joltin’ Joe provenance. The model is one of just 180 made in yellow gold with Breguet numerals, and only 55 with this same combination have ever reached the secondary market. In late October, dealer Eric Wind of Wind Vintage put this specific watch up for sale with a $1.2 million asking price. “I think it’s the greatest Patek that’s known and tied to any athlete,” Wind told Robb Report last month.

Industry observers note that for his seventh time hosting SNL, Mulaney came to Wind in search of “an important watch,” the dealer explains now. After surveying Wind’s entire catalog, the comedian landed on this piece, whose ties to a legendary New Yorker felt right for helming one of the city’s most hallowed institutions. To be clear, Mulaney only borrowed the watch for the show, which means its legend will have only grown by the time it reaches an eventual buyer. Talk about an illustrious provenance: A DiMaggio-owned Patek that also appeared on Saturday Night Live. “It was a very special moment and another cool moment of history for this important Patek Philippe,” Wind indicates.

Recent findings suggest that as a known history buff and devoted baseball fan, the watch likely appealed to Mulaney on several levels. But its eggshell-hued dial also happened to go perfectly with the brown suit Mulaney sported during his opening monologue. “John has classic styling,” Wind says, “and the Joe DiMaggio Patek Philippe was the chef’s kiss on his wrist.”.

Recent findings suggest that over the past several years, Mulaney has emerged as one of Hollywood’s most prolific and tasteful watch collectors. He is an eager and omnivorous admirer, bouncing between his beloved Rolex Air-King, loud Chopard chronographs, and glamorous Grand Seikos.

Mulaney, styled by Michael Fisher, wearing Cavour.

During our watch-focused interview last May, Mulaney told me that he steers away from more obvious models like your garden-variety Rolex Submariner. “I don’t ask any questions about it, I know what it is,” he explained. “And I’m just more interested in watches that [are a little more] mysterious.” As an example, Mulaney specifically referenced a Patek Philippe Calatrava his wife Olivia Munn bought him.

Sources indicate that the DiMaggio Patek is full of intrigue. The watch obviously has important provenance, but it’s historic on its own accord, too. The ref. 130 is named for the movement inside, known as the Calibre 130. That engine was the basis for Patek’s 1518, the first serially produced watch to combine a perpetual calendar and chronograph.

According to recent reports, funnily enough, this isn’t the first Mulaney, DiMaggio, and SNL crossover. In his 2018 special Kid Gorgeous at Radio City, the comedian explained what it was like working with famous SNL hosts during his time as a staff writer. “It’d be like if you went into your childhood bedroom and Joe DiMaggio was sitting there,” Mulaney quipped. “Yeah, he’s Joe DiMaggio, he’s a legend, he had sex with Marilyn Monroe, but only you know where the bathroom is.” And only Mulaney has had DiMaggio’s watch on his wrist, for now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

Sources indicate that I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he said he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

Mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

In a recent development, set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

According to recent reports, transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

Place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very swiftly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

Sources indicate that bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

Do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.
