Last month, while taking in the spring/summer 2027 shows at Paris Fashion Week, I was eager to write about the street style trends bubbling up around the showgoers in town. Which proved harder than anticipated. For one thing, the flashiest dressers had been given full looks by the brands whose shows they were being paid to attend, and reporting on those felt like a somewhat dishonest exercise in journalism. For another, the consensus seems to be that we are living in a post-trend world, and fashion people in particular have little interest in dressing like anyone else. And so I turned my attention to real-life Parisians, among whom one item seemed to proliferate: jeans.

In a recent development, no, this isn’t going to be a trend report on something as perennially popular as denim, but on a particular high-waisted, flared style that I spotted so frequently, I was forced to dredge up what little French remains from my GCSEs to ask a woman where hers were from as I caught her climbing onto a Lime bike outside Le Saint-Gervais bar. “Excuse-moi, madame, votre pantalons… le brand?” She paused for a moment, swung her leg over the saddle, and unleashed a torrent of French from which I managed to decipher just two words: “Anna” and “Gérard Darel”, the latter needing no explanation.

Founded in Saint-Germain-des-Prés in the 1970s, the brand has long been a shorthand for what the rest of the world considers the tenets of French-girl style: discreet, easy-to-wear classics with a cultivated air. (So cultivated, in fact, that the brand acquired the original handwritten Proust Questionnaire in 2003, and recently collaborated with the philosopher Alain de Botton on a card-game version.) Which is all very Left Bank, of course, but perhaps the clearest evidence of its credentials is just how commonplace Gérard Darel is in everyday Parisian life. You can scarcely move for its iconic 24H bag—a soft, logo-free shoulder bag that Vogue once named among the bags of the century, alongside the Hermès Birkin – during the school rush on the Métro, where it is generally to be found stuffed with binders and tangled wired headphones.

Recent findings suggest that but back to the jeans–an American invention, admittedly, but then again, this is the land of French fries. What made my startled Parisienne’s look so good? Much of it comes down to the cut–something Kate Moss, a woman who found fame in nothing more than a pair of jeans, understands, having been photographed in the brand’s Anna jeans as early as 2019. Designed by former creative director Valérie Gerbi and named after her daughter Anna – granddaughter of the brand’s founders, Danièle and Gérard Darel–the design braces at just the right point on the hips, fits snugly through the thighs and flares outwards just below the knee, skimming the top of a pair of shoes to create the illusion of longer legs. The double belt loops, meanwhile, criss-cross along the waistband to give the impression of a cinched waist, while the back pockets perform a similarly flattering service for the bum.

Recent findings suggest that and yet the technicalities of a good fit can only explain so much. Perhaps the true appeal was in the way she wore them–with white ballet flats that I’m convinced were from Repetto’s men’s section (the Luciens) and a navy three-quarter-zip jumper with the sleeves pushed up–or the ease with which disappeared into the Marais, hair whipping in the wind.

Now, in other news of a formerly Brosnan-led, menswear-centric franchise being rebooted: Oscar winner Michael B. Jordan is the producer, director, and star of a third riff on The Thomas Crown Affair, as he declared at CinemaCon back in April. Judging by the first trailer that dropped last week, the film aims to uphold the sartorial reputation of its forebears.

Industry observers note that hitting theaters in March 2027, Jordan’s The Thomas Crown Affair remake follows the same premise as the 1968 and 1999 versions: a wealthy playboy businessman plots art heists for fun while being pursued by a sexy insurance investigator, played in this iteration by potential future Wonder Woman Adria Arjona. There’s crime, there’s glamour, there’s sexual tension—but most of all, in the spirit of the Thomas Crowns before him, there appears to be plenty of high-octane menswear. The movie’s style credit is bolstered by Ruth E. Carter, the two-time Oscar-winning costume designer of the Black Panther movies, who also dressed Jordan for his Oscar-winning turn in Sinners.

Sources indicate that but how will MBJ’s high-fashion Thomas Crown land? In the trailer, he can be seen wearing a stiff gray shirt with a matching tie and trousers by Bottega Veneta. The shirt, marked by the luxury brand’s signature triangle pocket detail, had an odd fit: taut around the torso yet puffy around the biceps. Here’s hoping we’ll see some sharper tailoring in the next preview.

Still, to understand Thomas Crown’s legacy as one of the best-dressed guys in film, and why the forthcoming reboot will likely be a smorgasbord of massive-time menswear, it’s worth looking back at what made the original such a gem of classic American style. Beyond Jewison’s use of Mondrian-esque split-screen and a very cool soundtrack by French composer Michel Legrand, McQueen’s wardrobe is a perfect embodiment of late 1960s cool, and a how-to for anyone looking to capture it.

Recent findings suggest that equal parts finely tailored and adventurous, Crown is the ultimate man’s man: He closes million-dollar deals by day, but also flies planes, plays polo, and does donuts on the beach in a juiced-up dune buggy. Likewise, his wardrobe is split between incredible tailoring and a supremely dialed-in lineup of casual pieces. Crown’s suits are a primer on old-school Savile Row: structured, traditional, and precisely tailored, and his shirts, ties, and pocket squares are equally on point. Crown’s double-Albert style watch chain (attached to a Patek Philippe pocket watch, naturally) is a decidedly advanced swerve, but his Cartier Tank Cintrée looks as good in 2026 as it did in 1968 (or 1928, for that matter).

Steve McQueen and Faye Dunaway in The Thomas Crown Affair (1968).

Off-duty Crown’s casual looks include a parade of hall-of-fame menswear pieces like the Baracuta G9 Harrington jacket (classic navy blue with a red tartan lining), brown suede desert boots, and Persol aviators he wears while piloting his glider (gliders—also extremely cool). Club rules be damned, he plays golf in a non-regulation long-sleeved tee, whacks polo balls in an outfit straight out of a Ralph Lauren campaign, and later dons an Aran sweater for a romantic evening clambake at his beach house. It’s often said that Steve McQueen could look good in anything, and that might be true, but the clothes in this movie hit hard enough to make anyone look several orders of magnitude cooler.

In a recent development, set to the funky bars of Fela Kuti’s “Gentleman,” the trailer for Jordan’s forthcoming Thomas Crown Affair offers several tantalizing tidbits of what’s in store, including a Ferrari F40, several razor-sharp tuxes, and a glimpse at a watch that’s almost certainly a vintage Piaget. That monochrome Bottega look aside, between Jordan’s leading man chops and Carter’s knack for high-concept menswear, we’re assuredly in good hands.

The 8 Best Handheld Vacuums for Cleaning Small Messes

📅 07 Feb 2020 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Cleaning is soothing for some, but for others, it’s simply another task to add to an overwhelming to-do list.
  • But don't retire your go-to vacuum just yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Cleaning is soothing for some, but for others, it’s simply another task to add to an overwhelming to-do list. Hauling your clunky upright vacuum out of the closet every time you need to tidy up a minor spill or dust bunny makes the task of cleaning even more inconvenient. That’s why handheld vacuums are such a practical companion to your regular vacuum. They help you reach narrow spaces such as stairs, corners, under car seats, and around furniture and cut down on how much large, clunky equipment you need to carry around.

But don't retire your go-to vacuum just yet. Handheld vacs are better suited for tackling small messes in between your deeper cleans. Since they have lower dustbin capacities and less suction power, they aren’t equipped to handle whole rooms or entire floors and can’t penetrate deep enough into your carpet fibers. However, if you’re looking for a machine that can supplement your usual cleaning tools, then a handheld vacuum might be right for you.

According to recent reports, we evaluated a host of handheld vacuums from top brands like Black+Decker, Dyson, and Shark. We looked at their capability, features, and capacities to find the best devices to help you maintain cleanliness. These are the eight models we recommend, along with expert insight and valuable tips before you shop.

Recent findings suggest that for handheld vacuums that we tested ourselves, we evaluated their performance around the house on a mix of surfaces and different types of furniture, paying attention to how well they handled everyday messes and how easy they were to maneuver. We also considered some of the more practical details like emptying the dustbin, maintaining the filter, and overall ease of use.

For models we haven’t tested firsthand, we drew on our extensive vacuum-testing knowledge, researching leading contenders and focusing on key features like battery life, filtration, suction performance, and attachments.

Industry observers note that we prioritized cordless, rechargeable handheld vacuums that work well for a range of messes, such as pet hair and crumbs. This list reflects our top selections for handling everyday messes and more demanding cleanup jobs.

Lightweight, user-friendly, and full of power, the Dustbuster HHVK515J is an excellent vacuum to take on an array of tasks across the home, the shop, and even inside your car.

Industry observers note that the nozzle at the end of the vacuum stretches an additional 7.5 inches—all you have to do is pull it forward to get into all the hidden nooks and crannies. It has two cleaning speeds, one of which is a power boost in case you need to maximize suction for a bigger mess.

The Dustbuster uses a foam filter and a pre-filter to trap debris and other common allergens, both of which you can wash from time to time. This vacuum doesn't come with any additional attachments besides the adjustable nozzle, so it might be best used for immediate messes that you need to clean up right away.

Recent findings suggest that the Black+Decker Dustbuster AdvancedClean is reasonably priced, lightweight, compact, and has a good amount of suction power. The battery only lasts for about 15 minutes off of a single charge, but that's more than enough time to clean up a workspace, countertop messes, and other light debris.

Even with its smaller build, the Dustbuster comes with a built-in flip-up dusting brush and crevice tool, so you don’t have to deal with storing any attachments. It uses a washable pleated filter, but it’s not HEPA, so some dust and allergen particles may not be trapped completely.

Recent findings suggest that the dustbin holds about half a liter of debris at a time, and it empties with a quick press of a button. The Dustbuster comes with a wall mount for quick and convenient storage.

Recent findings suggest that what we appreciate about this handheld vacuum is that Shark has packed in similar features to some of the pet hair vacuums we love, like a paddled roller brush for scooping up deeply embedded hair and making continuous contact with surfaces. Alongside these features, you also get a self-cleaning brush roll.

This handheld vacuum uses two cyclonic air streams, one for powerful suction and one to separate debris away from the motor to protect its lifespan. When it's time to empty the dustbin, just hit the eject latch and the chamber door falls open, discharging dust and hair. You don’t have to touch any of the gunk.

Recent findings suggest that we also like how the design uses a two-stage filter, and you can wash and use it again. The vacuum runs for up to 10 minutes off of its rechargeable lithium-ion battery.

The Dyson Car+Boat is a handheld vacuum that can easily alternate between detailing the interior of your car and cleaning small messes from bare floors, carpet, and furniture. Plus, it offers up to 50 minutes of fade-free suction in standard mode, which is more than any other handheld vacuum on this list (besides the corded option, that is).

Similar to Dyson cordless stick models, the Car+Boat uses a fully sealed filtration system to pick up and trap almost 100 percent of airborne particles as small as 0.3 microns.

In a recent development, it also comes with a mini motorized brush, a crevice tool, and a combination tool for messes both substantial and small. The main caveat is that you have to keep a trigger button depressed for the duration of your cleaning session in order for the vacuum to stay powered on.

The DeWalt DCV517B stands up to tough chores, tackling anything like a bowl of breakfast cereal dumped on the floor (milk and all), or a handful of metal shavings on top of your garage workbench.

In a recent development, the HEPA filter traps debris of varying sizes effectively, and the vacuum has two cleaning modes so you can alternate between the nozzle head and extendable hose. This model also has a half-gallon tank that easily detaches for emptying.

The DCV517B uses DeWalt-brand batteries, which may add some considerable heft to the body itself (it weighs 4.5 pounds to start). But a high-capacity battery gives superior vacuuming strength and provides the suction needed to clean both wet and dry messes.

The Shark Wandvac is the sleek, modern hand vacuum that could just as easily serve as an accent piece in your living room as it does for cleaning up spills. While the exterior might be flashy, the bones of the machine are solid as well.

The large mouth is great for significant messes, and the powerful suction means even serious dirt or food spills will be pulled up without much matter. Beyond this, the Wandvac has multiple attachments including the Multi-Surface Pet Tool and Duster Crevice Tool.

During our testing, the Duster Crevice Tool was quite effective for hard-to-reach corners, ceilings and otherwise ignored spaces like under the fridge, but we were most impressed by the Surface Pet Tool. In combination with a bit of elbow grease, it lifted tons of hair and dander out of carpets, furniture, and other upholstery. Just note that the dustbin is a little small, which means frequent emptying.

In a recent development, the Bissell Pet Hair Eraser is the only thing that worked to remove embedded pet hair, litter paw prints, and dander from my black polyester couches (and I tried plenty of other methods). Suction is consistent and strong, and the motorized pet tool provided the power I needed to get rid of wiry hairs that had found themselves looped in the fabric.

It has been revealed that the Pet Hair Eraser has a pleated post-motor filter, a washable inner foam filter, and a mesh pre-filter for trapping dust and allergens. The dustbin is easy to empty once you remove the filter, and you can give it a quick rinse if you want to remove any lingering debris. The vacuum lasts for up to 17 minutes, but it takes a long time to fully recharge.

Sources indicate that don’t want to deal with rechargeable batteries? A corded handheld vacuum is a great option if you prefer to have continuous power for your cleaning tools. The Dirt Devil Scorpion has a 15-foot power cable so you don’t have to always be within range of an outlet, along with a 2.5-foot detachable hose and built-in crevice tool for picking up dirt and debris in hard-to-reach areas.

Recent findings suggest that the dustbin holds a little less than half a liter, which is right around the capacity we recommend to cut down on trips to the trash can. This model also uses a washable filter to reduce the amount of maintenance and replacements needed.

Use this alongside your corded upright, and you’ll have the suction power you need to tackle tough household messes. We just wish it came with some more attachments to really take it to the next level.

It has been revealed that A quality handheld vac should be ready to use whenever you need it, which means having a dependable battery with a run time that lasts long enough so you don’t lose power mid-clean. Many of our selections use a lithium-ion battery that can last anywhere from around 10 to 50 minutes between charges. Just be prepared that some models take several hours to go from fully dead to fully charged, so keeping the vacuum docked and hooked up to power consistently is important.

Sources indicate that handheld vacuums have a smaller dustbin capacity and fill up faster than full-size, upright versions, but that’s because they handle light spills, not whole-home cleaning. If you regularly reach for your handheld vacuum, look for models that hold up to half a liter or more of debris, so you don’t have to make as many trips to the garbage can.

A handheld vacuum with multiple attachments may be a worthwhile investment if you have kids that are prone to dropping crumbs or furry friends that shed profusely. Crevice tools get into the nooks and crannies of the couch, whereas bristled or motorized brushes pick up stubborn pet hair.

Additional hose pieces can also be beneficial if you need extended reach. These types of attachments focus airflow and suction to a designated area, and may be used on different surfaces like upholstery, carpet, and hardwood floors.

Handheld vacuums often come with cloth, foam, or pleated filters that trap dust, hair, grime, and allergen particles—and most of these versions are washable to avoid buying replacements all the time.

It has been revealed that some handheld vacuums include an additional filter, called the pre-filter, which traps larger particles before they reach the main filter. Others might have a HEPA filter that removes up to 99.7 percent of airborne particles and is useful for allergy sufferers.

We recommend shopping for a handheld vacuum with at least a two-step filtration system or a HEPA filter if you’re trying to keep your home or car clear of common allergens like pollen and pet dander. Otherwise, a washable filter will do just fine for general cleaning tasks.

What is a good suction power rating for a handheld vacuum?

Sources indicate that first, it’s key to note that brands don’t all advertise suction power the same way. Some list air watts (AW), some use pascals (Pa), and some don’t provide a suction rating at all and focus more on the motor.

These measurements aren’t directly interchangeable, but for everyday messes and light debris I would look for a handheld vacuum rated around 20 to 40AW or between 5,000 to 10,000Pa.

How often should I clean or replace the filter?

Recent findings suggest that A light cleaning should be done every few weeks or whenever you notice reduced suction power. Foam and felt filters can be washed every 1 to 3 months, and should be replaced every 3 to 6 months.

HEPA filters are not washable unless specified by the vacuum manufacturer and should be replaced between 6 to 12 months. You can adjust the frequency of maintenance based on your cleaning needs and how much debris you typically pick up.

How long do handheld vacuums last?

Recent findings suggest that there’s no one-size-fits all for how long a handheld vacuum lasts because it largely depends on build quality, frequency of use, battery health, and maintenance. Cleaning the filter and dustbin regularly helps preserve the battery and motor, too, but if the vacuum is losing suction or the battery can’t hold a charge, it might be time for a replacement.
